sections.title: 11.5. Serialization

summary.text: Specifies that C2PA Manifest Stores and C2PA Manifests are serialized using JUMBF (ISO 19566-5:2023), and that this format shall also be used in formats without native JUMBF support or when stores are kept separately from the asset. Table 2 gives the JUMBF type UUID, label and contents for the Manifest Store (c2pa), standard manifest (c2ma), update manifest (c2um), compressed manifest (c2cm), deprecated standard manifest type (c2md), Assertion Store (c2as, label c2pa.assertions), Claim (c2cl, label c2pa.claim.v2) and Claim Signature (c2cs, label c2pa.signature). These boxes shall satisfy Section 11.5.3.2 Toggles and Section 11.5.3.3 Labels, and Manifest Consumers shall accept c2md superboxes as standard manifests while claim generators shall not create them.

sections.extract: The C2PA Manifest Store and individual C2PA Manifests are serialized using the JPEG Universal Metadata Box Format (ISO 19566-5:2023, JUMBF). This serialized format shall be used also in formats that do not natively support JUMBF, or when C2PA Manifest Stores are stored separately from the asset, such as in a separate file or URI location. The following type, label, and content requirements shall apply: Table 2. C2PA

sections.title: 11.5.1. Assertion Store Contents

summary.text: Specifies that the C2PA Assertion Store is a JUMBF superbox with the label and type given in Table 2, containing one or more C2PA Assertion superboxes whose JUMBF type defines the type of their content sub-boxes. Each assertion superbox shall have a label as defined in Standard Assertions and contain a JUMBF Description Box, one or more JUMBF Content Boxes and possibly a Padding Box. Recommends CBOR, JSON, Embedded File (bfdb and bidb) or UUID content types while permitting any JUMBF content type and a JUMBF Protection Box per ISO 19566-4:2020, and notes that custom formats such as encrypted data are supported through a UUID Content Box.

sections.extract: The C2PA Assertion Store is a JUMBF superbox that shall have the label and type given in Table 2, “C2PA JUMBF boxes”. It shall contain one or more JUMBF superboxes (called C2PA Assertion boxes) whose JUMBF type defines the type of the sub-boxes that contain the assertion data (ISO 19566-5:2023, Annex B). These superboxes shall each have a label as defined in Standard Assertions and shall contain a JUMBF Description

sections.title: 11.5.2. Compressed Manifests

summary.text: Specifies that standard and update C2PA Manifests can be compressed in their entirety using a new brob JUMBF content box with box ID 0x62726F62, based on a similar JPEG-XL box. A compressed manifest shall have a TYPE of c2cm, a label identical to that of the compressed manifest superbox, and brob contents that are the Brotli-compressed (RFC 7932) bytes of the entire manifest superbox, as shown in Figure 10. Hashing a compressed box follows Section 9.4.2.3 Hashing JUMBF Boxes, covering the Description Box and the brob box with its compressed payload without decompressing it first. Anywhere the specification references a standard or update manifest, a compressed one is also valid.

sections.extract: Both standard and update C2PA Manifests can be compressed, in their entirety. To support this, C2PA defines a new brob JUMBF content box, based on a similar box in JPEG-XL (ISO/IEC 18181-2:2024). The brob box shall have box ID of 0x62726F62 (brob). For either type of manifest, the value of the TYPE field shall be c2cm, the value of the label field shall be identical to the label of the compressed manifest superbox,

sections.title: 11.5.3. General C2PA JUMBF Requirements

summary.text: Heading that opens section 11.5.3 General C2PA JUMBF Requirements; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 11.5.3.1. Processing Rules

summary.text: Requires that a C2PA Manifest Consumer never process an assertion, assertion store, claim, claim signature or C2PA Manifest that is not contained in a C2PA Manifest Store, and that it skip over and ignore the contents of any JUMBF box or superbox whose type UUID it does not recognize. Notes that this lets a consumer process private boxes it knows about while ignoring unknown ones.

sections.extract: A C2PA Manifest Consumer shall never process an assertion, assertion store, claim, claim signature or C2PA Manifest that is not contained inside of a C2PA Manifest Store. Additionally, when a C2PA Manifest Consumer encounters a JUMBF box or superbox whose JUMBF type UUID it does not recognize, it shall skip over (and ignore) its contents. NOTE: This means that the C2PA Manifest Consumer can process private boxes

sections.title: 11.5.3.2. Toggles

summary.text: Requires the Label Present toggle (xxxxxx1x) and the Requestable toggle (xxxxxx11) to be set on all JUMBF Description boxes used in a C2PA Manifest, because labels are required and boxes are referred to by JUMBF URIs. When a salt is included in a PRIVATE box as described in Section 9.4.2.3 Hashing JUMBF Boxes, the Private toggle (xxx1xxxx) shall also be set.

sections.extract: All JUMBF Description boxes (ISO 19566-5:2023, A.3) used in a C2PA Manifest require a label and so the Label Present toggle (xxxxxx1x) shall be set. In addition, because JUMBF URIs are used to refer to boxes throughout the system (e.g., listing assertions, references to ingredients, etc.), the Requestable toggle (xxxxxx11) shall be set. When including a salt in a PRIVATE box as described in Section 9.4.2.3, “Hashing

sections.title: 11.5.3.3. Labels

summary.text: Requires JUMBF labels to be stored as null-terminated Unicode characters in UTF-8, per ISO 19566-5:2023, A.3. Labels may not contain characters in the ranges U+0000 to U+001F or U+007F to U+009F, or the characters '/', ';', '?' and '#', and because labels are used in JUMBF URIs, U+FEFF, U+FFFF and U+D800-U+DFFF shall also not be used.

sections.extract: As described in the JUMBF specification (ISO 19566-5:2023, A.3), a label shall be stored as Unicode characters in the UTF-8 encoding and shall be null-terminated. Characters in the ranges U+0000 to U+001F inclusive and U+007F to U+009F inclusive, as well as the specific characters '/', ';', '?', and '#', are not permitted in the label. Because labels are used as part of JUMBF URIs, the characters U+FEFF, U+FFFF, and

sections.title: 11.5.3.4. Unrecognized Boxes

summary.text: Allows the C2PA Manifest Store (c2pa) and C2PA Manifests (c2ma, c2um, c2cm and c2md) to contain JUMBF boxes and superboxes whose type UUIDs are not defined in the specification, provided they satisfy Section 11.5.3.2 Toggles and Section 11.5.3.3 Labels, enabling custom extensions and future additions without breaking compatibility. Requires any box or superbox with both the Requestable and Label Present toggles set to be maintained in any updated C2PA Manifest Store, since such boxes are intended to be referenced via JUMBF URIs and removing them could cause downstream workflows to fail.

sections.extract: The C2PA Manifest Store (c2pa) and C2PA Manifest (c2ma, c2um, c2cm, and c2md) may also contain JUMBF boxes and superboxes that satisfy the requirements in Section 11.5.3.2, “Toggles” and Section 11.5.3.3, “Labels” and whose JUMBF type UUIDs are not defined in this specification. NOTE: Allowing other boxes and superboxes enables custom extensions to C2PA as well as enabling the addition of new boxes in future

sections.title: 11.5.4. JUMBF Rationale

summary.text: Explains why JUMBF (ISO 19566-5:2023) was chosen to serialize C2PA Manifests: it can store multiple manifests in one container, refer to elements within and across manifests via URIs, clearly identify the parts of an element to be hashed, and store both C2PA's predefined data types (e.g. JSON and CBOR) and arbitrary data formats. It is also natively supported by the JPEG family and compatible with the ISO BMFF box model, letting it work with classic image formats such as JPEG/JFIF and PNG as well as 3D and document formats such as PDF. A note explains that using CBOR for the entire manifest was considered but not chosen because CBOR is not a container format, and re-implementing JUMBF's features in CBOR would be a lot of work and would not fully remove the need for a JUMBF/BMFF parser.

sections.extract: In order to support many of the requirements of C2PA, C2PA Manifests needed to be stored (serialized) into a structured binary data store that enables some specific functionality including: Ability to store multiple manifests (e.g., parents and ingredients) in a single container. Ability to refer to individual elements (both within and across manifests) via URIs. Ability to clearly identify the parts of an element

sections.title: 11.6. Embedding

summary.text: States that a C2PA Manifest Store can be embedded into a variety of file formats covering images, video, audio, fonts and documents, with technical details for each supported format in Appendix A Embedding manifests. Notes that many classic image formats such as BMP do not support embedding arbitrary data, so an external manifest is required for them.

sections.extract: A C2PA Manifest Store can be embedded into a variety of file formats covering media types including images, videos, audio, fonts, and documents. Appendix A, Embedding manifests provides the technical details on how to embed C2PA Manifests into each specifically supported file format. NOTE: Many classic image formats such as BMP do not support the embedding of arbitrary data, so the use of an external manifest is

sections.title: 11.7. Multiple Step Processing

summary.text: Explains that some file formats require the file offsets of the C2PA Manifest Store and asset content to be fixed before signing so content bindings align, yet the size of the manifest and its signature cannot be precisely known until after signing, citing JPEG 1, where the entire Manifest Store must appear before the image data. Requires a multiple step approach, similar to how PDF signatures are done, to accomplish this.

sections.extract: Some asset file formats require file offsets of the C2PA Manifest Store and asset content to be fixed before the manifest is signed, so that content bindings will correctly align with the content they authenticate. Unfortunately, the size of a manifest and its signature cannot be precisely known until after signing, which could cause file offsets to change. As an example, in JPEG 1 files, the entire C2PA Manifest

sections.title: 11.7.1. Create content bindings

summary.text: Requires a standard manifest's claim to include one or more content binding assertions so that the asset is tamper-evident, and describes creating the data hash assertion using exclusion ranges, where a single hash covers only the asset ranges outside the exclusions (e.g. the claim creator may exclude the APP11 segments holding a manifest in a JPEG 1 file). To prevent insertion attacks a single exclusion range is desirable; when the manifest's size or location is unknown, start and length shall both be zero and pad should be large enough for the values written in the second pass, with at least 16 bytes recommended and pad consisting of all 0x00 bytes. Claim generators shall ensure that changes to pad data or other excluded data cannot change how the asset is interpreted; for JPEG 1, a note says this can be achieved by eliminating padding or by including all APP11 segment headers and 2-byte length fields in the data-hash-map.

sections.extract: When creating a standard manifest, its claim shall include one or more content binding assertions in its list of assertions to ensure that the asset is tamper-evident. Create the data hash assertion and add it to the assertion store taking into account the following considerations.
