sections.title: 11.7.2. Create a temporary Claim and Signature

summary.text: Describes adding the data hash assertion reference to the claim's assertion list with a temporary hash value, such as empty spaces, after which the temporary claim can be added to the C2PA Manifest. Because the temporary claim cannot be signed yet, it describes building a temporary COSE_Sign1_Tagged structure so the claim signature box holds valid CBOR. The four-element array consists of an empty protected header bucket (a zero-length bstr), an unprotected header map with one pad entry holding a zero-filled bstr of the desired padding size (25 kilobytes is recommended initially), a nil payload, and a zero-length bstr signature.

sections.extract: Add the newly created data hash assertion reference to the claim’s assertion list providing a temporary hash value, such as empty spaces. At this point, the temporary claim is complete and can be added to the C2PA Manifest being created. Since the claim is only temporary at this time, it is not possible to sign it. To ensure the claim signature box contains a valid CBOR structure, create a temporary

sections.title: 11.7.3. Complete the C2PA Manifest

summary.text: Describes completing the C2PA Manifest by assembling all its boxes into final form and combining the asset's manifest with the manifests of any ingredients into the complete C2PA Manifest Store. Requires the active manifest to be the last C2PA Manifest superbox in the C2PA Manifest Store superbox, after which the store can be embedded into the asset as discussed in Appendix A, Embedding manifests.

sections.extract: At this point all of the boxes that comprise the entire C2PA Manifest for the asset are completed and can be (if not already) constructed into its final form. The asset’s C2PA Manifest, along with the manifests of any ingredients, are combined together to form the complete C2PA Manifest Store. The active manifest is required to be the last C2PA Manifest superbox in the C2PA Manifest Store superbox. The C2PA Manifest

sections.title: 11.7.4. Going back and filling in

summary.text: Describes updating the data hash assertion with the active manifest's starting offset and length after embedding, without changing the assertion box's size, by adjusting the pad field; a note explains that some padding sizes cannot be expressed in pad alone and can be split between pad and pad2. The updated assertion is then hashed into the reserved space, and the claim is hashed and signed per Section 10.3.2.4, Signing a Claim, with the unprotected pad header shrunk so the claim signature box keeps its size. Requires repeating the multiple step processing with larger padding chosen in Section 11.7.2 if the serialized COSE_Sign1_Tagged exceeds the reserved size, noting that still-valid revocation information should be reusable but a new time stamp will be required. Recommends that claim generators use padding before assertion creation when assertions defined outside this specification may depend on file layout.

sections.extract: Now that the C2PA Manifest Store has been embedded into the asset, the starting offset and the length of the active manifest can be updated in its data hash assertion. It is necessary that when doing so, you do not change the size of the assertion’s box, only its data. This is done by adjusting the value of the pad field to be the necessary length to "fill up" the remaining bytes. NOTE: Preferred/deterministic CBOR

sections.title: 11.8. External Manifests

summary.text: Describes keeping C2PA Manifests external to the asset, in a manifest repository easily locatable by a Manifest Consumer (such as by reference or URI), when embedding is not possible or practical. Requires the C2PA Manifest Store to be served with the media type application/c2pa, noting that application/x-c2pa-manifest-store is deprecated. Lists common reasons for external manifests: embedding may be technically impossible, impractical when the manifest store is larger than the asset's digital content, or inappropriate when the asset cannot be modified.

sections.extract: In some cases, it may not be possible (or practical) to embed a C2PA Manifest Store in an asset. In those cases, keeping the C2PA Manifests externally to the asset is an acceptable model for providing provenance to assets. The C2PA Manifest should be stored in a location, referred to as a manifest repository, that is easily locatable by a Manifest Consumer working with the asset, such as by reference or URI. As the

sections.title: 11.8.1. Embedding a Reference to an external Manifest

summary.text: Recommends that, when an asset has embedded XMP and its C2PA Manifest Store is stored externally, the claim generator add a dcterms:provenance key to the XMP whose value is a URI reference to the manifest store. Notes that this mechanism is now only for external manifests, and that fonts, which do not support XMP, use an equivalent method described in the clause on fonts.

sections.extract: If the asset has embedded XMP, and the C2PA Manifest Store will be stored externally, it is recommended that the claim generator add a dcterms:provenance key to the XMP, the value (a URI reference) being where to locate the C2PA Manifest Store. NOTE: A previous version of this specification also recommended using this method for references to embedded manifests. Now this mechanism is only for external manifests.

sections.title: 12. Cryptography

summary.text: Heading that opens Chapter 12, Cryptography; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 12.1. Hashing

summary.text: Requires all cryptographic hashes used in creating and validating C2PA Manifests to use algorithms from an allowed list (generators should use, validators shall support) or a deprecated list (validators should support, generators shall not produce), excluding soft bindings and custom assertions. Requires that an algorithm appear in at most one list, that each output length be listed separately, and that unlisted algorithms be forbidden and not supported optionally. Requires hash outputs to be stored as CBOR byte strings with an algorithm identifier (alg) in the same structure, an enclosing structure, or the claim-map or claim-map-v2, with the nearest identifier taking precedence and the claim-map alg used as the fallback. The allowed list is SHA2-256 (sha256), SHA2-384 (sha384) and SHA2-512 (sha512); SHA-3 is excluded for consistency with the signature algorithm list, and the deprecated list is empty.

sections.extract: All cryptographic hashes used in the creation and validation of C2PA Manifests (and their contents) as per the technical requirements of this specification shall be generated using one of the hash algorithms as described in this section. This section defines both: A list of hash algorithms that generators should use for generating hashes of new content and that validators shall support for validating hashes of

sections.title: 12.2. Binding to Content

summary.text: Heading that opens section 12.2 Binding to Content; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 12.2.1. Overview

summary.text: Describes content bindings in a standard C2PA manifest, distinguishing hard (cryptographic) bindings, which let a validator confirm the manifest belongs to this asset and that the asset is unmodified, from soft bindings, which are computed from the digital content and help identify derived assets and renditions. Requires that a single manifest contain no more than one hard binding assertion, while allowing zero or more soft binding assertions.

sections.extract: A key aspect to the standard C2PA manifest is the presence of one or more data structures, called content bindings, that can uniquely identify portions of the asset. There are two types of bindings that are supported by C2PA - hard bindings and soft bindings. A hard binding (also known as a cryptographic binding) enables the validator to ensure that (a) this manifest belongs with this asset and (b) that the asset

sections.title: 12.2.2. Hard Bindings

summary.text: States that every hard binding assertion is built from the hash algorithms defined in Section 12.1, Hashing, and that the specific hard binding assertion used depends on the asset's format and structure, as described in the following subsections.

sections.extract: Every hard binding assertion is built from the hash algorithms defined in Section 12.1, “Hashing”. The specific hard binding assertion used depends on the format and structure of the asset, as described below.

sections.title: 12.2.2.1. Hashing using byte ranges

summary.text: Describes the simplest hard binding as a cryptographic hash over some or all bytes of an asset, usable on any asset type but recommended only for formats that do not support box-based hashing. Specifies that a data hash assertion defines which byte ranges are hashed, works for single binaries or multi-chunk assets, and binds a C2PA Manifest to the codec configuration of live media over Enhanced RTMP (V2), as described in Section 15.5.3.3, Initialization data binding.

sections.extract: The simplest type of hard binding that can be used to detect tampering is a cryptographic hashing algorithm, as described in Section 12.1, “Hashing”, over some or all of the bytes of an asset. This approach can be used on any type of asset, but should only be considered for formats that don’t support one of the forms of box-based hashing. When using this form of hard binding, a data hash assertion is used to define

sections.title: 12.2.2.2. Hashing using a general box hash

summary.text: Recommends using a general box hash assertion for non-BMFF box-based formats such as JPEG 1, PNG and GIF. Describes the assertion as an array of structures, each listing one or more boxes by name or identifier with a hash covering those boxes (and any data between them) and the hashing algorithm used.

sections.extract: When an asset’s format is a non-BMFF-based box format, such as JPEG 1, PNG, GIF or others listed here, then a general box hash assertion should be used. This assertion consists of an array of structures, each one listing one or more boxes (by their name/identifier) and a hash that covers that data of those boxes (and any possible data that may be present in the file between them), along with the algorithm used for

sections.title: 12.2.2.3. Hashing a BMFF-formatted asset

summary.text: Permits ISO BMFF-based assets to use BMFF-based hash assertions instead, which for a monolithic MP4 with mdat validated as a unit work nearly like a data hash assertion but use a box exclusion list rather than byte ranges. Requires that, for fragmented MP4 files, the assertion be combined with chunk-specific hashing information located as specified in Section A.5, Embedding manifests into BMFF-based assets, and points to the live media section for hashing individual segments.

sections.extract: If the asset is based on ISO/IEC 14496-12, ISO BMFF then a hard binding optimized for the box-based format (called BMFF-based hash assertions) may be used instead. For a monolithic MP4 file asset where the mdat box is validated as a unit, the assertion is validated nearly identically to a data hash assertion. It simply uses a box exclusion list instead of byte ranges to define the range of bytes that are hashed (and

sections.title: 12.2.2.4. Hashing unstructured text assets

summary.text: Requires a data hash assertion for unstructured text assets whose C2PA Manifest is embedded using Unicode Variation Selectors as described in Section A.8, Embedding Manifests into Unstructured Text. The hashing follows the text-specific normalization rules defined in Validating a text data hash.

sections.extract: For unstructured text assets that have a C2PA Manifest embedded using Unicode Variation Selectors as described in Section A.8, “Embedding Manifests into Unstructured Text”, a data hash assertions shall be used. This assertion provides a hard binding mechanism specifically designed for text content where the C2PA Manifest is embedded as a sequence of non-rendering Unicode characters, and its hashing follows the

sections.title: 12.2.2.5. Hashing structured text assets

summary.text: Requires a data hash assertion for structured text assets associated with a C2PA Manifest using ASCII armour-style delimiters as described in Section A.9, Embedding Manifests into Structured Text. The exclusion range covers the manifest block so the hash is computed without the manifest reference, with details in Section A.9.5, Hard Binding.

sections.extract: For structured text assets that have a C2PA Manifest associated using ASCII armour-style delimiters as described in Section A.9, “Embedding Manifests into Structured Text”, a data hash assertion shall be used. The exclusion range covers the manifest block so that the hash is computed over the file content without the manifest reference. Details of the hard binding are defined in Section A.9.5, “Hard Binding”. <a

sections.title: 12.2.2.6. Hashing append-only text assets

summary.text: Requires a segment hash assertion for files written only by appending complete lines, such as application logs, event logs and JSON Lines streams, as described in Section A.3.17, Embedding manifests into append-only text files. Each assertion is a hard binding over one bounded segment, and the segments are linked into a chain of checkpoints so the file's complete history can be verified.

sections.extract: For files that are written only by appending complete lines to the end of the file, such as application logs, event logs and JSON Lines streams, as described in Section A.3.17, “Embedding manifests into append-only text files”, a segment hash assertion shall be used. Each such assertion is a hard binding over one bounded segment of the file rather than over the file as a whole, and the segments are linked into a

sections.title: 12.2.2.7. Hashing a Collection

summary.text: Requires the collection data hash assertion to be used to specify hard bindings when a C2PA Manifest refers to a collection of assets rather than a single asset. A note gives the example of describing each folder of an AI/ML training data set.

sections.extract: In workflows where the C2PA Manifest will refer to a collection of assets, instead of a single asset, the collection data hash assertion shall be used as the method to specify the hard bindings for the assets in the collection. NOTE: For example, a collection data hash assertion can be used to describe each folder of a training data set for an AI/ML model.

sections.title: 12.2.2.8. Hashing assets with multiple parts

summary.text: Requires the multi-asset hash assertion, alongside the whole-file hard binding assertion, for formats that aggregate multiple independently verifiable parts, such as CIPA Multi-Picture Format (MPF) or Android Ultra HDR, recording a hash for each part. States that a multi-asset hash assertion modifies how a hard binding is validated but is not itself a hard binding.

sections.extract: For file formats that aggregate multiple distinct parts, such as CIPA Multi-Picture Format (MPF) or Android Ultra HDR, where the integrity of each part must be independently verifiable, the multi-asset hash assertion shall be used alongside the hard binding assertion for the file as a whole, recording a hash for each part. A multi-asset hash assertion modifies how a hard binding is validated but is not itself

sections.title: 12.2.2.9. Binding Non-C2PA Asset Metadata

summary.text: Recommends that a Claim Generator, where possible, include asset metadata outside the C2PA Manifest, such as EXIF or XMP, in the hard binding to protect its integrity. A note clarifies that only signed C2PA created_assertions are attributed to the signer, so metadata covered only by a hard binding is not, whereas serializing it into a c2pa.metadata assertion in created_assertions explicitly signals that the signer asserts it. Recommends copying asset metadata values supported by the common metadata assertion, as described in Appendix C, into such an assertion when the signer can assert them.

sections.extract: One of the capabilities of a hard binding is that it can exclude parts of an asset, for various reasons. However, a Claim Generator should, where possible, include asset metadata (i.e., metadata outside a C2PA Manifest such as EXIF or XMP) in the hard binding, in order to protect its integrity throughout the asset’s lifecycle. NOTE: Only signed C2PA created_assertions are attributed to the signer. Any asset metadata

sections.title: 12.2.3. Soft Bindings

summary.text: Heading that opens section 12.2.3 Soft Bindings; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 12.2.3.1. General

summary.text: Describes soft bindings, expressed through soft binding assertions such as a fingerprint of the digital content or an invisible watermark, as enabling digital content to be matched even when the underlying bits differ, for example in another resolution or encoding. Notes that if a manifest is removed from an asset but a copy remains in a provenance store, soft bindings may be used to match the two. Requires that a soft binding not be used as a hard binding.

sections.extract: Soft bindings are described using soft binding assertions such as a fingerprint computed from the digital content or an invisible watermark embedded within the digital content. These soft bindings enable digital content to be matched even if the underlying bits differ. NOTE: For example, an asset rendition in a different resolution or encoding format. Additionally, if a C2PA manifest is removed from an asset, but a

sections.title: 12.2.3.2. Referenced List of Soft Binding Algorithms

summary.text: Specifies that soft bindings are generated by an algorithm named in the alg field of the soft binding assertion, and recommends that the name be among those in the soft binding algorithm list supported by this specification.

sections.extract: Soft bindings are generated by an algorithm named in the `alg' field of the soft binding assertion. The algorithm name should be among those algorithms listed in the soft binding algorithm list as supported by this specification.

sections.title: 12.3. Digital Signatures

summary.text: Requires all claim signatures to use digital signature algorithms and key types from an allowed list (generators should use, validators shall support) or a deprecated list (validators should support, generators shall not use), excluding custom assertions and time stamps. Specifies that the lists reference COSE algorithm identifiers from standards such as RFC 9052, RFC 9053, RFC 8230 and RFC 9964, which also specify the hash used in each signature scheme. Requires that Section 12.1, Hashing, not apply to those hash algorithms, whose use is allowed and followed for any listed signature algorithm.

sections.extract: All claim signatures shall be generated using one of the digital signature algorithms and key types listed as described in this section. This section defines both: A list of digital signature algorithms and key types that generators should use for new claim signatures and that validators shall support for validating existing claim signatures (the allowed list); A list of digital signature algorithms and key types

sections.title: 12.3.1. Signature Algorithms

summary.text: Lists the allowed claim signature algorithms: ES256, ES384, ES512, ESP256, ESP384, ESP512, PS256, PS384, PS512, EdDSA (Ed25519 only), and ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 (COSE identifiers -48, -49, -50); the deprecated list is empty. Notes cover ML-DSA's larger signature and key sizes, the fully-specified ESP identifiers binding each hash to one curve, and that certificate signing algorithms are governed separately by Section 13.5.1.1, General Requirements. Requires implementations to check that keys are correct for the chosen algorithm (P-256/P-384/P-521 curves paired with the matching ECDSA algorithms, edwards25519 for Ed25519, RSA moduli of at least 2048 bits, and ML-DSA parameter sets matching the identifier) and to refuse incorrect keys, while allowing refusal of RSA keys over 16384 bits. Recommends deterministic signature algorithms for live media streaming so segment caching is not harmed.

sections.extract: The allowed list is: ES256 (ECDSA with SHA-256); ES384 (ECDSA with SHA-384); ES512 (ECDSA with SHA-512); ESP256 (ECDSA with SHA-256, fully-specified equivalent of ES256); ESP384 (ECDSA with SHA-384, fully-specified equivalent of ES384); ESP512 (ECDSA with SHA-512, fully-specified equivalent of ES512); PS256 (RSASSA-PSS using SHA-256 and MGF1 with SHA-256); PS384 (RSASSA-PSS using SHA-384 and MGF1 with SHA-384);

sections.title: 12.3.2. Use of COSE

summary.text: Specifies that the CBOR-encoded claim is signed using COSE as described in RFC 9052, sections 4.2 and 4.4, noting that payloads may be embedded or detached, in which case the COSE_Sign1_Tagged payload field is nil. Requires that the payload field of the in-memory Sig_structure always be populated with the relevant external data and never be nil. For standard or update manifests, that payload is the contents of the claim JUMBF box, as described in Section 10.3.2.4, Signing a Claim, and Section 11.5, Serialization.

sections.extract: The signature for the CBOR-encoded claim is produced by CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) as described in RFC 9052, sections 4.2 and 4.4. NOTE: Payloads can either be present inside a COSE signature, or transported separately ("detached content" as described in RFC 9052, section 4.1). In "detached content" mode, the signed data is stored externally to the COSE_Sign1_Tagged structure, and the payload field of

sections.title: 12.3.3. Computing the Signature

summary.text: Specifies additional requirements for building Sig_structure under RFC 9052, section 4.4: the context shall be Signature1 (or CounterSignature where specified, never Signature), external_aad shall be a zero-length bstr, the payload is set by each use, and the alg header shall be in body_protected. Requires all C2PA digital signatures to be COSE_Sign1_Tagged structures with the same alg header in the protected bucket. Requires a detached payload to be nil and an embedded payload to be stored as a bstr, noting that a zero-length byte array cannot indicate detached content.

sections.extract: The signature is computed or verified as described in RFC 9052, section 4.4. The following additional requirements apply to the construction of Sig_structure: The value for the context element shall be Signature1 except where a particular use of digital signatures in this specification specifies using CounterSignature instead. Signature shall not be used. The value for the payload element will be specified by each

sections.title: 12.3.4. Adding a claimed time of signing

summary.text: Permits a claim generator to add an iat protected header with a NumericDate value as a claimed time of signing, which, if present, shall represent when the signature was generated. Notes that NumericDate is a CBOR numeric date without the leading tag 1, and that the recommendation is based on in-process JAdES updates for a generator-provided timestamp useful when no trusted time source is available but not used for certificate validity checking.

sections.extract: A claim generator may also wish to establish a "claimed time of signing" by adding an iat protected header, whose value is a NumericDate. If present, it shall represent the time at which the signature was generated. NOTE: A NumericDate is a CBOR numeric date (as described in RFC 8949, section 3.4.2) but with the leading tag 1 (epoch-based date/time) omitted. It is not used anywhere else in this specification. NOTE:

sections.title: 12.3.5. Signature Validation

summary.text: Recommends that a claim generator able to act as a validator check that its signing credential is acceptable under Chapter 13, Trust Model, and warn if it is not. Permits signing with that credential anyway, for instance when the local validator's configuration differs from that of validators used by the asset's expected audience.

sections.extract: When producing a signature, if the claim generator can also act as a validator, the claim generator should validate that the signing credential is acceptable according to Chapter 13, Trust Model and produce a warning if it is not. The claim generator may still allow signing with that credential if so desired. This may be desirable if it is known that the local claim generator’s validator has a different

sections.title: 12.3.6. Cryptographic validation

summary.text: Describes building an in-memory Sig_structure when verifying a signature, with body_protected filled from the COSE_Sign1_Tagged protected header bucket and the payload taken from the COSE_Sign1_Tagged payload field when present. Requires that, when the payload is detached (nil), the Sig_structure payload be populated from the same external source used when generating the signature, as defined where each signature is used.

sections.extract: When verifying a signature, an in-memory Sig_structure is generated. Its body_protected field is populated with the contents of the protected header bucket from the COSE_Sign1_Tagged structure (RFC 9052, section 4.4). For the payload field, if the payload was specified as present in the signature, it is populated from the payload field of the COSE_Sign1_Tagged structure. If the payload was specified as detached, the

sections.title: 12.3.7. Inclusion of signer icons

summary.text: Requires a C2PA Manifest Consumer that wants to display a signer icon or logo to look for a logotype, as defined in RFC 9399, inside the embedded certificate. If none is present, the consumer may use icons or logos from other sources in an implementation-dependent manner.

sections.extract: A C2PA Manifest Consumer may wish to display an icon or logo for the signer. To locate such a graphic, it shall look inside the embedded certificate for a logotype as defined in RFC 9399. If no logotype is present, the Manifest Consumer may use icons or logos from other sources in an implementation-dependent manner.

sections.title: 13. Trust Model

summary.text: Heading that opens Chapter 13, Trust Model, with a note that "user" in this chapter refers to human actors using C2PA-compliant validators in consumption and authoring scenarios.

sections.extract: NOTE: In this section, "user" refers to human actors that are using C2PA-compliant validators in consumption and authoring scenarios.

sections.title: 13.1. Overview

summary.text: Presents Figure 11, the C2PA Trust Model Diagram, showing the three entities specified in the trust model, which concerns trust in a signer's identity. Describes the consumer, who is not specified in the trust model, as using the signer's identity along with other trust signals to decide whether assertions about an asset are true.

sections.extract: C2PA Trust Model Diagram Figure 11. C2PA Trust Model Diagram Figure 11, “C2PA Trust Model Diagram” shows, in yellow, green and red, the three entities specified in the trust model, which is concerned with trust in a signer’s identity. In dashed lines, below, is the consumer (who is not specified in the trust model), who uses the identity of the signer, along with other trust signals, to decide whether the assertions

sections.title: 13.2. Identity of Signers

summary.text: Defines identity in the trust model as the means of associating a signing key (credential) with the signer for trust decisions about anything signed with that key. Requires the credential to be listed in the COSE protected headers of the COSE_Sign1_Tagged structure, with exactly one credential across protected and unprotected headers, and requires rejecting structures with none or with two or more, including repeats of the same credential. An exception treats the same X.509 chain under both the x5chain string label and integer label 33 as a single credential, with further details in Section 13.5, X.509 Certificates.

sections.extract: Identity in the trust model is the means by which a cryptographic signing key (aka credential) is associated with the signer for the basis of making trust decisions based on the claim signature or any structure (including, but not limited to, assertions and claims) signed with that key. The credential shall be listed in the COSE protected headers of the COSE_Sign1_Tagged structure used for digital signatures in all

sections.title: 13.3. Validation states

summary.text: Heading that opens section 13.3 Validation states; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 13.3.1. General

summary.text: Describes a validator as a Manifest Consumer that makes validation statements about an asset and its active manifest, following the process in the validation section. The actor consuming the asset, usually through a user agent, then interprets those statements and the asset's contents to reach their own conclusions about its provenance.

sections.extract: A validator is a Manifest Consumer that will make some validation statements about that asset and its associated active manifest. The process for retrieving these statements is described in the validation section. The actor consuming the asset, usually through their user agent and its user interface, then has to interpret those statements to arrive at a set of conclusions of their own about the provenance of the

sections.title: 13.3.2. Manifest States

summary.text: Lists the states a C2PA Manifest may have based on validation statements: Well-Formed, Valid and Trusted. Notes that any Trusted manifest is also Valid, and any Valid manifest is also Well-Formed.

sections.extract: Based on these statements, a C2PA Manifest may be one of the following: Well-Formed Valid Trusted NOTE: Any Trusted manifest is also Valid, and any Valid manifest is also Well-Formed.

sections.title: 13.3.3. Asset States

summary.text: Defines a Valid asset as one whose content-binding-covered portions a validator reports as unmodified since the active manifest was produced (per Section 14.12, Validate the Asset's Content) and whose active manifest is Valid or Trusted.

sections.extract: If a validator reports that the portions of the asset that are covered by content bindings have not been modified since the active manifest was produced [Section 14.12, “Validate the Asset’s Content”], and its active manifest is either Valid or Trusted, then the asset itself is a Valid asset.

sections.title: 13.3.4. Well-Formed Manifest

summary.text: Defines a Well-Formed C2PA Manifest as one where validation determines that its contents meet the normative requirements checked by the validation process, only assertions allowed for its manifest type are present (Section 14.10.1), its assertions meet all assertion requirements (Section 14.10.4), and any ingredients meet all ingredient requirements (Section 14.11).

sections.extract: A C2PA Manifest is Well-Formed if validation determines that each of the following is true: The manifest’s contents abide by the normative requirements of this specification, that are validated via the validation process. Only those assertions allowed for the specific type of the manifest are present [Section 14.10.1, “Validate the correct assertions for the type of manifest”]. The assertions of the manifest meet

sections.title: 13.3.5. Valid Manifest

summary.text: Defines a Valid C2PA Manifest as one that is Well-Formed, unmodified since signing, has a claim signature with success code claimSignature.validated, receives claimSignature.insideValidity for the signature validity period, and whose signer credential is not rejected with signingCredential.ocsp.revoked. States that a Valid manifest's claim can be attributed to the claim generator identified by the claim's claim_generator_info field.

sections.extract: A C2PA Manifest is Valid if validation determines that each of the following is true: The manifest is Well-Formed [Section 13.3.4, “Well-Formed Manifest”]. The manifest has not been modified since the manifest was signed [Section 12.3.6, “Cryptographic validation”]. The claim signature receives a success code of claimSignature.validated [Section 14.7, “Validate the Signature”]. Validation of the claim signature

sections.title: 13.3.6. Trusted Manifest

summary.text: Defines a Trusted C2PA Manifest as one that is Valid and whose signing credential receives the success code signingCredential.trusted under Section 14.7, Validate the Signature.

sections.extract: A C2PA Manifest is Trusted if validation determines that each of the following is true: The manifest is Valid [Section 13.3.5, “Valid Manifest”]. The signing credential of the C2PA Manifest receives the success code of signingCredential.trusted [Section 14.7, “Validate the Signature”].

sections.title: 13.4. Trust Lists

summary.text: Heading that opens section 13.4 Trust Lists; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 13.4.1. C2PA Signers

summary.text: Requires a validator to maintain a list of accepted Extended Key Usage (EKU) values and, for each, a list of trust anchor configurations, each including the trust anchor's X.509 certificate and recommended to include notBefore and (when trust has ended) notAfter date/times. Requires that a configuration not be used for claim signatures whose timestamp, or the current time if none, falls before notBefore or after notAfter. Requires the list for the c2pa-kp-claimSigning EKU to include the C2PA Trust List, and recommends letting users configure additional anchors for that or other EKUs and offering default or externally maintained lists. Notes that including id-kp-emailProtection or id-kp-documentSigning alongside c2pa-kp-claimSigning can improve compatibility with older validators.

sections.extract: A validator shall maintain the following information for evaluating C2PA signers: A list of accepted Extended Key Usage (EKU) values. For each accepted EKU value, a list of "trust anchor configurations". An individual trust anchor configuration shall include the X.509 certificate for that trust anchor. Additionally, the configuration should include a "notBefore" date/time, before which there is no trust for that

sections.title: 13.4.2. Time Stamping Authorities

summary.text: Requires a validator to maintain trust anchor configurations for Time Stamping Authorities (TSAs) separately from the C2PA signer lists, each including the X.509 certificate and recommended to include notBefore and notAfter date/times. Requires that a configuration not be used for time-stamps asserting times outside those bounds, and that the list include the C2PA TSA Trust List. Recommends allowing users to configure additional TSA trust anchor stores, and permits offering default or externally maintained lists.

sections.extract: A validator shall maintain a list of trust anchor configurations for Time Stamping Authorities (TSAs), which shall be separate from the lists for C2PA signers. An individual TSA trust anchor configuration shall include the X.509 certificate for that trust anchor. Additionally, the configuration should include a "notBefore" date/time, before which there is no trust for that trust anchor configuration. If the trust

sections.title: 13.4.3. Private Credential Storage

summary.text: Permits a validator to let users maintain a private credential store, an address book of signing credentials trusted through out-of-band relationships. Requires that the store apply only to validating signed C2PA manifests (not time stamps), trust only signer credentials directly, and never act as trust anchors. Requires that the store not be pre-configured and that entries be added or removed only at the user's request.

sections.extract: A validator may also allow the user to create and maintain a private credential store of signing credentials. This store is intended as an "address book" of credentials they have chosen to trust based on an out-of-band relationship. If present, the private credential store shall only apply to validating signed C2PA manifests, and shall not apply to validating time stamps. If present, the private credential store

sections.title: 13.5. X.509 Certificates

summary.text: Specifies that X.509 certificates are stored per RFC 9360, quoting its x5chain definition, and adds requirements beyond it. Requires claim generators to include the signer's certificate and all intermediate CA certificates in x5chain, recommends omitting the root certificate, and notes that the first certificate's public key validates the signature. Requires claim generators to use only integer label 33 (the string label x5chain is deprecated) and to place the header only in the protected bucket. Requires validators to accept either label from either bucket, treat both labels together as one credential using label 33, and reject the signature as malformed if the same label appears in both buckets.

sections.extract: X.509 Certificates are stored as defined by RFC 9360 (CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE): Header Parameters for Carrying and Referencing X.509 Certificates). For convenience, the definition of x5chain is copied below. IMPORTANT: This specification adds additional requirements beyond those of RFC 9360, which are listed after the quoted text. In particular, this specification requires all intermediate

sections.title: 13.5.1. Certificate Profiles

summary.text: Heading that opens section 13.5.1 Certificate Profiles; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 13.5.1.1. General Requirements

summary.text: Defines requirements for an X.509 certificate to be acceptable as a C2PA claim signing credential, not applying to TSA, OCSP or CA certificates. Requires the signatureAlgorithm to be one of the listed ECDSA, RSA, RSASSA-PSS, Ed25519 or ML-DSA identifiers, with constraints on RSASSA-PSS parameters, absent parameters for ML-DSA, named curves prime256v1, secp384r1 or secp521r1 for EC keys, and RSA moduli of at least 2048 bits; a note explains that RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 is permitted for CA certificate signatures but not for C2PA claims. For all certificates outside the private credential store, requires v3, no unique IDs, correct Basic Constraints (only end entity certificates sign claims, time stamps and OCSP responses), Authority and Subject Key Identifiers as prescribed, and a Key Usage extension with digitalSignature for manifest signers. Requires a non-empty EKU extension in end entity certificates, forbidding anyExtendedKeyUsage, requiring id-kp-timeStamping or id-kp-OCSPSigning for those purposes exclusively, and not rejecting certificates for unrelated extra EKUs.

sections.extract: This section defines the requirements to validate that an X.509 certificate is acceptable as a signing credential as described in Section 14.7, “Validate the Signature”. All C2PA Claim signing certificates shall fulfill the following requirements. The requirements do not apply to TSA, OCSP or CA certificates in certificate chains. NOTE: The signatureAlgorithm field identifies the algorithm the issuing Certificate

sections.title: 13.5.1.2. Certificate Trust Chain

summary.text: Specifies that a signing certificate in the private credential store is accepted, while otherwise the trust chain shall be built and validated per RFC 5280, section 6, for the relevant purpose and trust anchor store, with any failure causing rejection; the private credential store is never used to build chains or validate time stamps. Requires validators to reject certificates used for purposes not authorized by their EKU, and requires claim signing certificates to have at least one EKU for which the validator has trust anchors, using only those anchors. Requires validators to verify Certificate Profile compliance (outside the private credential store), including EKU presence and authorization for no more than one of C2PA signing, time stamp signing or OCSP signing, and to ignore any EKU present on CA certificates.

sections.extract: When validating a certificate as the signing credential, if the certificate is present in the private credential store for X.509 certificates, the certificate is accepted. The private credential store is not consulted when validating time stamps. If the certificate is not present in the private credential store, or the validator does not implement one, the trust chain shall be built and validated according to the

sections.title: 13.5.2. Certificate Revocation

summary.text: Recommends that claim generators implement revocation using OCSP and OCSP stapling, and forbids them from using Certificate Revocation Lists, noting CRLs are slow to download and large. Recommends that CAs include an AuthorityInfoAccess extension, and requires that, when present, revocation information be stored in an unprotected COSE_Sign1 header labelled rVals following the given CDDL with an ocspVals array. Recommends that before signing, a claim generator query the OCSP service for the signer's certificate and any included intermediate CA certificates and store the responses in ocspVals, with validation described in Validate the Credential Revocation Information.

sections.extract: X.509 certificates support revocation status queries. A claim generator should use the Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP, RFC 6960) and OCSP stapling (as originally conceptualized in RFC 6066, Section 8, but implemented as described in this clause) to implement revocation. The claim generator shall not use Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs, RFC 5280). NOTE: Using CRLs requires downloading the entire list of

sections.title: 14. Validation

summary.text: Heading that opens Chapter 14, Validation; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.1. Validation Process

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.1 Validation Process; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.1.1. Description

summary.text: Describes validation of a C2PA Manifest as a multi-step process covering its assertions, claim and claim signature, plus any associated hard bindings for active manifests only. Defines a validator as a hardware or software actor that implements the validation algorithms in this clause.

sections.extract: Validation of a C2PA Manifest is a multi-step process that involves validating the assertions, claim & associated claim signature contained within it along with (for active manifests, only) validation of any associated hard bindings. This validation process is performed by a validator, which is a hardware or software actor that implements the validation algorithms described in this clause. <a

sections.title: 14.1.2. Phases of Validation

summary.text: Lists the phases of validation, in no particular order: validating the assertions (Section 14.10), the ingredients if any (Section 14.11), the time stamp (Section 14.8), the credential revocation information (Section 14.9), the claim signature (Section 14.7), and the asset's content (Section 14.12). States that the results determine whether a manifest is Well-Formed, Valid or Trusted as described in Section 13.3, Validation states.

sections.extract: These phases, which are listed in no particular order, are described in the following clauses: Section 14.10, “Validate the Assertions”: Validation of the assertions. Section 14.11, “Validate the Ingredients”: Validation of the ingredients, if any. Section 14.8, “Validate the Time Stamp”: Validation of the time stamp. Section 14.9, “Validate the Credential Revocation Information”: Validation of the credential

sections.title: 14.1.3. Visual Representation

summary.text: Presents Figure 12, Validating a Claim, as a visual representation of validating a C2PA Manifest, noting that the text is authoritative where it differs from the figure.

sections.extract: Figure 12, “Validating a Claim” is a visual representation of the process of validating a C2PA Manifest. Validating a Claim Figure 12. Validating a Claim NOTE: If there are any discrepancies between the visual representation and the text, the text is considered authoritative.

sections.title: 14.2. Returning Validation Results

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.2 Returning Validation Results; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.2.1. General

summary.text: Requires the validation algorithm to return a consolidated set of results, per the schema in Section 14.2.2, for all manifests in the asset's C2PA Manifest Store, including the active manifest and those referenced by ingredient assertions. Specifies standard success, informational and failure codes from Appendix D and permits custom codes that follow entity-specific namespace syntax. Requires a claim generator adding an ingredient to act as a validator, run the full algorithm on it, and record the results in the ingredient assertion's validationResults field. Permits results to include a SemVer specVersion and either a deprecated trustListUri or a trustListUris field identifying the trust lists used.

sections.extract: The validation algorithm shall return a consolidated set of validation results, per the CDDL Definition schema in Section 14.2.2, “Validation Structures”, for the all manifests in the asset’s C2PA Manifest Store, including the active manifest as well all other manifests in the C2PA Manifest Store that are referenced via ingredient assertions. Validation results include a standard set of success, informational, and

sections.title: 14.2.2. Validation Structures

summary.text: Defines, in CDDL, the data structures for validation results, with a complete normative schema in Section G.7.3. These include status-map (a code, at most one of url or resourceUrl, an optional explanation, and a deprecated success flag), status-codes-map with success, informational and failure arrays, and trust-list-uri-map with uri, type and optional identifier. Also defines validation-results-map with optional activeManifest, ingredientDeltas, specVersion, and either trustListUri (deprecated) or trustListUris, and ingredient-delta-validation-result-map with ingredientAssertionURI and validationDeltas.

sections.extract: The following CDDL Definition schema defines the data structures used for validation results (see Section G.7.3, “Validation Result Structures” for the complete normative schema): CDDL for Validation Results ; custom status codes $status-code /= tstr .regexp "([\da-zA-Z_-]+\.)+[\da-zA-Z_-]+" status-map = { "code": $status-code, ; A label-formatted string that describes the status ; At most one of "url" and

sections.title: 14.3. Displaying Manifest Information

summary.text: Recommends that Manifest Consumers not display data from manifests or assets that are not Valid. Requires that, if such data is displayed anyway, the display include a warning about the lack of validity and a warning that the data shall not be attributed to the manifest's signer (or, for an ingredient manifest, to the asset's manifest's signer). A note says authoring scenarios should raise warnings more prominently.

sections.extract: Manifest Consumers should not display data from manifests which are not Valid nor from assets which are not Valid. If the Manifest Consumer chooses to display such data, it shall include as part of the display: a warning about the lack of validity, a warning that the data shall not be attributed to the manifest’s signer, and in the case of an ingredient manifest, additional not to the asset’s manifest’s signer.

sections.title: 14.4. Determining the hashing algorithm

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.4 Determining the hashing algorithm; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.4.1. For hard binding assertions

summary.text: Requires the alg field of a hard binding assertion, if present, to be used as its hashing algorithm, otherwise the Claim's alg field. Requires the Claim to be rejected with algorithm.unsupported if neither is present.

sections.extract: Each hard binding assertion has an alg field that specifies the hashing algorithm used to compute the hash of the asset. If the alg field is present, it shall be used as the hashing algorithm for the hard binding assertion. If no alg field is present in the hard binding assertion, the value of the alg field in the Claim shall be used as the hash algorithm. If no alg field is present in the Claim, the Claim shall be

sections.title: 14.4.2. For Hashed URIs

summary.text: Requires the hash algorithm for a hashed_uri structure to be taken from its own alg field if present, otherwise from the nearest enclosing structure with an alg field, otherwise from the claim's alg field. Requires the claim to be rejected with algorithm.unsupported if no alg field is found in any of these locations.

sections.extract: Various parts of the C2PA Manifest utilize a hashed_uri structure for encapsulating a URI, its hash and (optionally) the algorithm used to compute the hash. If there is an alg field in the hashed_uri structure, it shall be used as the hashing algorithm. If the alg field is not present in the hashed_uri structure, the hash algorithm shall be determined by evaluating the nearest enclosing structure that contains an

sections.title: 14.4.3. For Hashed Ext URIs

summary.text: Requires the alg field of a hashed_ext_uri structure, which encapsulates an external URI and its hash, to be used as its hashing algorithm, and requires the failure code algorithm.unsupported if it is absent. Notes that alg is mandatory in hashed_ext_uri, so no recursive lookup is needed.

sections.extract: Some parts of a C2PA Manifest utilize a hashed_ext_uri structure for encapsulating an external URI, its hash and the algorithm used to compute the hash. If there is an alg field in the hashed_ext_uri structure, it shall be used as the hashing algorithm. If the alg field is not present in the hashed_ext_uri structure, the failure code of algorithm.unsupported shall be used. NOTE: The alg field is mandatory in

sections.title: 14.4.4. Algorithm validation

summary.text: Requires the determined hashing algorithm to be compared against the allowed and deprecated lists in Section 12.1, Hashing. Requires rejecting the claim with algorithm.unsupported if it is in neither list, and issuing the informational code algorithm.deprecated if it is in the deprecated list.

sections.extract: Once the hashing algorithm is determined, it shall be compared to the values in the allowed list or the deprecated list in Section 12.1, “Hashing”. If it is not present in either list, the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of algorithm.unsupported. If the algorithm is present in the deprecated list, the claim shall be issued an informational code of algorithm.deprecated. <a

sections.title: 14.5. Locating the Active Manifest

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.5 Locating the Active Manifest; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.5.1. General

summary.text: Requires the last C2PA Manifest superbox in the C2PA Manifest Store superbox to be considered the active manifest, noting that locating the store may involve several locations and is a prerequisite with no validation status code of its own. Requires an asset to be treated as if no manifests were located when no store can be found, or when more than one store is found where an embedding method admits only one. Notes that implementations may surface additional information about why no manifests were located.

sections.extract: The last C2PA Manifest superbox in the C2PA Manifest Store superbox shall be considered the active manifest, but locating the C2PA Manifest Store may involve looking in a number of possible locations. Locating the C2PA Manifest Store is a prerequisite to validation and is not itself associated with a validation status code. If no C2PA Manifest Store can be located by the methods described below, the asset shall be

sections.title: 14.5.2. Embedded

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.5.2 Embedded; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.5.2.1. General

summary.text: Requires the validator to locate the C2PA Manifest Store embedded at the standard embedding locations, and permits checking an HTTP Link header if none is found. Requires multiple embedded stores to be considered invalid, with validation that should treat this as no manifests located and with none included in an ingredient assertion. Requires an embedded store to take precedence over a remote one indicated by a Link header. Requires rejection with manifest.inaccessible.encrypted if the store is unreadable due to encryption (excluding mechanisms such as the PDF Identity crypt filter) and with manifest.inaccessible.malformed if it is readable but cannot be interpreted as a valid store.

sections.extract: The C2PA Manifest Store shall be located by the validator embedded inside the asset at the standard locations for embedding manifests. If no embedded C2PA Manifest Store is found, and if an asset was retrieved via an HTTP connection, a validator may look for a Link header, as described in the Link Header clause below, to determine if a C2PA Manifest Store is present. NOTE: Checking the Link header, if present,

sections.title: 14.5.2.2. Special Considerations for PDF

summary.text: Describes how PDF incremental updates require support for multiple C2PA Manifest Stores, but only one per update section. Requires multiple stores in a single update section to be considered invalid (treated as if no manifests were located), while stores in earlier updates or the original PDF remain valid and are processed.

sections.extract: PDF files support a technology called "incremental update", where information is appended to the end of the document instead of modifying the original. This requires that PDF files support multiple C2PA Manifest Stores - though there shall only be one per update section. If there are multiple C2PA Manifest Stores present in a single update section, they shall all be considered as invalid and the validation should

sections.title: 14.5.2.3. Special Considerations for HTML

summary.text: Requires the C2PA Manifest Store for HTML assets to be located using the procedure in Section A.7, Embedding Manifests into HTML. Requires the asset to be treated as if no manifests were located if the head element contains more than one C2PA manifest element, such as multiple script elements with type="application/c2pa" or both a script and a link element.

sections.extract: For HTML-based assets, the C2PA Manifest Store shall be located by following the procedure defined in Section A.7, “Embedding Manifests into HTML”. If more than one C2PA manifest element is present in the head element — more than one script element with type="application/c2pa", both a script element and a link element referencing a C2PA Manifest Store, or otherwise — the asset shall be treated as if no manifests

sections.title: 14.5.2.4. Special Considerations for Structured Text

summary.text: Requires locating the C2PA Manifest Store for structured text per Section A.9 by reading the file in binary mode and searching for the -----BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST----- and -----END C2PA MANIFEST----- delimiters, treating the asset as having no manifests if delimiters are missing, unpaired or there is more than one block. Requires extracting and whitespace-trimming the reference between delimiters. Specifies resolving a data: URI only if it has media type application/c2pa and base64 encoding, resolving other URIs per Section 14.5.3 (retrieval is optional; if not retrieved, no manifests are treated as located), and otherwise treating the asset as having no manifests.

sections.extract: For assets consisting of structured text, the C2PA Manifest Store shall be located by following the procedure defined in Section A.9, “Embedding Manifests into Structured Text”. The validator shall read the file in binary mode and search for the -----BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST----- and -----END C2PA MANIFEST----- delimiters. If the delimiters are not found, only one delimiter is found, or more than one manifest block is

sections.title: 14.5.2.5. Special Considerations for Append-Only Text Files

summary.text: Requires locating the C2PA Manifest Store for append-only plain-text files and JSONL streams per Section A.3.17 by scanning in binary mode from the end for the last complete sentinel line (a BEGIN/END C2PA CHECKPOINT line for plain text, or a JSON object with a c2pa:checkpoint member for JSONL). Requires treating the asset as having no manifests and reporting manifest.appendOnlyText.noSentinel if no such line is found or it is malformed. Specifies extracting and trimming the reference, decoding valid application/c2pa base64 data: URIs (otherwise reporting manifest.appendOnlyText.noSentinel) and resolving other URIs per Section 14.5.3, reporting manifest.inaccessible if retrieval fails. The located store is that of the active checkpoint, with earlier checkpoints found by following the chain described in Section 14.12.6.

sections.extract: For append-only plain-text files and JSONL streams, the C2PA Manifest Store shall be located by following the procedure defined in Section A.3.17, “Embedding manifests into append-only text files”. The validator shall: 1. Read the file in binary mode and scan from the end, line by line, for the last complete sentinel line. For plain-text files, this is a line beginning with -----BEGIN C2PA CHECKPOINT----- and ending

sections.title: 14.5.2.6. Special Considerations for Unstructured Text

summary.text: Requires the C2PA Manifest Store for unstructured text to be located using the procedure in Section A.8, Embedding Manifests into Unstructured Text. Requires the asset to be treated as if no manifests were located if no valid C2PATextManifestWrapper, or more than one, is found.

sections.extract: For assets consisting of unstructured text, the C2PA Manifest Store shall be located by following the procedure defined in Section A.8, “Embedding Manifests into Unstructured Text”. If no valid C2PATextManifestWrapper is found, or more than one valid C2PATextManifestWrapper is found, the asset shall be treated as if no manifests were located.

sections.title: 14.5.2.7. Special Considerations for TIFF

summary.text: Requires the C2PA Manifest Store for TIFF-based assets to be located in either the first IFD or the last IFD.

sections.extract: For assets consisting of TIFF based format, the C2PA Manifest Store shall be located in either the first IFD or the last IFD.

sections.title: 14.5.2.8. Special Considerations for WARC

summary.text: Requires the C2PA Manifest Store for WARC files to be located per Section A.10 by scanning for a record with WARC-Type c2pa-provenance and Content-Type application/c2pa. Specifies that if none is found the file has no manifest store, if more than one is present the asset shall be treated as if no manifests were located, and if exactly one is found the store shall be extracted from its block. Notes that a companion CDX or CDXJ index may be used to locate the record without scanning the whole file.

sections.extract: For WARC files, the C2PA Manifest Store shall be located by following the procedure defined in Section A.10, “Embedding manifests into WARC files”. The validator shall scan the file for a record whose WARC-Type is c2pa-provenance and whose Content-Type is application/c2pa. If no such record is found, the file does not contain a C2PA Manifest Store. If more than one such record is present, the asset shall be treated

sections.title: 14.5.3. By Reference or URI

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.5.3 By Reference or URI; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.5.3.1. By Reference

summary.text: Recommends that, when no store is embedded, a validator attempt in order to locate a remote C2PA Manifest Store via an HTTP Link header, an XMP dcterms:provenance URI, a font C2PA table with non-zero activeManifestUriLength, sidecar files named with an added or replacement .c2pa extension, or a similarly named entry in the same archive, stopping at the first found. Permits looking in other places if these fail. Requires the manifest.inaccessible error code when a documented remote manifest is missing or unreachable, and rejection with manifest.inaccessible.encrypted or manifest.inaccessible.malformed when a retrieved store is unreadable due to encryption or cannot be interpreted as valid.

sections.extract: If there is no embedded C2PA Manifest Store, the following attempts should be made to locate one at a remote location. Once a C2PA Manifest Store is located, the validation process should proceed with that manifest as the active manifest (and therefore not continue looking for additional manifests). The following attempts should be made in order: If the asset was retrieved via an HTTP connection, the Link Header

sections.title: 14.5.3.2. By Link header

summary.text: Recommends that, for assets retrieved over HTTP, a validator look for a Link header (per RFC 8288) with rel=c2pa-manifest, from whose http or https URI the C2PA Manifest Store can be retrieved. Describes that the link may also refer to an embedded store using a JUMBF URI fragment to the C2PA Manifest Store superbox, and requires validators to ignore any childlabel portion since references to specific manifests are not permitted. Notes that HTTP refers to the protocol in RFC 9110, not only the http:// scheme.

sections.extract: If the asset was retrieved via an HTTP connection, the validator should look in the header of the HTTP response for a Link header, as defined in RFC 8288, containing a parameter of rel=c2pa-manifest. If present, a C2PA Manifest Store can be retrieved from that URI reference. The URI will be a standard http or https URI, such as https://c2pa.org/image.c2pa. It is also possible to use the link relation to refer to the

sections.title: 14.5.4. Decompression

summary.text: Requires a validator to decompress compressed standard or update manifests before standard validation. Requires rejection with manifest.compressed.invalid if decompression fails or the brob box data is not a standard or update manifest.

sections.extract: As described previously, both standard and update manifests can be compressed. When a compressed manifest is encountered, a validator shall decompress it before proceeding with the standard validation process. If the data contained in the brob box of a compressed manifest is not either a standard or update manifest or if the decompression fails, the validator shall reject the manifest with a failure code of

sections.title: 14.5.5. Validating a Match

summary.text: Describes that a validator may wish to confirm that the located C2PA Manifest Store belongs to the asset. Requires using the active manifest's hard binding assertion for this, and, since a mismatch could mean either modification or the wrong store, requires treating it as a non-matching hard binding and rejecting with assertion.dataHash.mismatch, assertion.boxesHash.mismatch, assertion.collectionHash.mismatch, assertion.segmentHash.mismatch or assertion.bmffHash.mismatch depending on the assertion type.

sections.extract: A validator may wish to validate that the located C2PA Manifest Store is indeed the one associated with asset. If the C2PA Manifest Store was located then the hard binding assertion present in its active manifest shall be used to validate that it is the matching manifest and whether the asset has been modified without manifest updates. If the hard binding does not match, it is unknown if that is because of (a)

sections.title: 14.6. Locating and Validating the Claim

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.6 Locating and Validating the Claim; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.6.1. Locating

summary.text: Specifies locating the claim within the current manifest as the JUMBF superbox labelled c2pa.claim.v2 (or c2pa.claim for older claims) with JUMBF type UUID 6332636C-0011-0010-8000-00AA00389B71 (c2cl), which is the same for both formats. Requires exactly one such box, rejecting the manifest with claim.multiple if more than one is found.

sections.extract: Once the manifest to be validated has been located (hereafter referred to as the "current manifest"), the claim is found by locating, within the current manifest, the JUMBF Superbox with a label of c2pa.claim.v2 (or c2pa.claim for files with older claim structures) and a JUMBF type UUID of 6332636C-0011-0010-8000-00AA00389B71 (c2cl). Note that the JUMBF type UUID is the same for both the new (with c2pa.claim.v2

sections.title: 14.6.2. Validating

summary.text: Requires a claim whose content is not well-formed CBOR to be rejected with claim.cbor.invalid. Requires a c2pa.claim.v2 to contain instanceID, signature, created_assertions and claim_generator_info, and requires rejection with claim.malformed if any is missing or if claim_generator_info lacks a name field. Requires any icon field in the generator-info-map to be validated as described in Section 14.10.4.3, Validation of References.

sections.extract: If the content of the claim is not well-formed CBOR, the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of claim.cbor.invalid. NOTE: Well-formed CBOR is defined in RFC 8949, Appendix C. For a "c2pa.claim.v2", the following fields are expected to be present in the CBOR object. If any are absent, then the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of claim.malformed. instanceID signature created_assertions

sections.title: 14.7. Validate the Signature

summary.text: Requires the validator to resolve the claim's signature field to the COSE signature, rejecting with claimSignature.missing if it is absent, unresolvable or outside the same C2PA Manifest box. Requires credential validation per Chapter 13, rejecting with signingCredential.invalid for unacceptable credentials and algorithm.unsupported for algorithms not on the allowed or deprecated lists. Requires checking for a valid time stamp first, then recommends verifying a chain of trust to a trust anchor configuration while honouring notBefore and notAfter, assigning signingCredential.trusted or rejecting with signingCredential.untrusted. Requires then verifying the signature per Section 12.3, assigning claimSignature.validated or rejecting with claimSignature.mismatch, and states that headers in the rest of the chapter mean the union of protected and unprotected headers.

sections.extract: The validator shall retrieve the URI reference for the signature from the value of the claim’s signature field and resolve the URI reference to obtain the COSE signature. If the signature field is not present, or the URI cannot be resolved, or the URI does not resolve to a location within the same C2PA Manifest box (as the claim), then the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of claimSignature.missing. For

sections.title: 14.8. Validate the Time Stamp

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.8 Validate the Time Stamp; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.8.1. Obtaining the TimeStampToken

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.8.1 Obtaining the TimeStampToken; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.8.1.1. Embedded in the Claim Signature

summary.text: Specifies that when a sigTst or sigTst2 header is present its tstTokens array is expected to hold a single tstToken, and requires issuing timeStamp.malformed and ignoring the time stamps if there is more than one. Requires a validator supporting sigTst to take the val property as an RFC 3161 TimeStampResp, issue timeStamp.malformed and ignore it if the PKIStatusInfo status is not 0 (granted) or 1 (grantedWithMods), and otherwise use its timeStampToken. Requires a validator for sigTst2 to take the val property as an RFC 3161 timeStampToken.

sections.extract: If either the sigTst or sigTst2 header is present, then the tstTokens array is expected to contain a single tstToken. If the header contains more than one tstToken, the validator shall issue a timeStamp.malformed informational code and ignore the time stamps. A validator that supports sigTst shall perform the following procedures to validate the time stamp response: Retrieve the val property from the tstToken, which

sections.title: 14.8.1.2. Referenced by a time stamp assertion

summary.text: Requires a validator to skip this step if a TimeStampToken from a sigTst or sigTst2 header has already passed validation, and to follow it otherwise. Requires that, if time stamp assertions were previously mapped from C2PA Manifest identifiers to TimeStampTokens, the validator use the token mapped to the current manifest's identifier, trying each one if several exist until one passes. States that no error is raised when the identifier is absent from the mapping.

sections.extract: If a validator has already located a TimeStampToken in a sigTst or sigTst2 header, that passes validation (as per Section 14.8.2, “Validating the TimeStampToken”), then it shall skip this step. When no such header exists or the TimeStampToken located there did not pass validation, this step shall be followed. If a validator had previously located any time stamp assertions, which were then maintained in a mapping of

sections.title: 14.8.2. Validating the TimeStampToken

summary.text: Requires validators to check the timeStampToken's signature algorithm, signature, messageImprint presence, imprint hash algorithm, imprint match against the claim (sigTst) or COSE signature field (sigTst2), TSA certificate trust chain, and that genTime falls within the TSA and CA certificates' validity, issuing informational codes such as timeStamp.untrusted, timeStamp.mismatch, timeStamp.malformed or timeStamp.outsideValidity and ignoring the time stamp on failure. Requires issuing timeStamp.trusted and timeStamp.validated when all checks pass, then checking genTime against the claim signing certificate chain to return claimSignature.insideValidity or reject with claimSignature.outsideValidity. Notes that a failed time stamp does not by itself reject the manifest, that time stamps stay valid after the TSA credential expires, and that TSA revocation status is not required. Requires validators to use the attested time when a trusted, validated time stamp is present, and otherwise to use the current time to return claimSignature.insideValidity or reject with claimSignature.outsideValidity.

sections.extract: All validators shall continue the process as follows: If the signature algorithm in the timeStampToken is not on the allowed or deprecated list in Section 12.3, “Digital Signatures”, then the validator shall issue a timeStamp.untrusted informational code and ignore the time stamp. Validate the signature in the timeStampToken, as described in RFC 5652, Section 5.6. If the signature is not valid, then the validator

sections.title: 14.8.3. Validating the "claimed time of signing"

summary.text: Permits a validator to check that the claimed time of signing in the iat protected header falls within the validity period of the signer's certificate and CA certificates and is no later than any trusted time stamp. Requires that a validator performing this check return the informational code timeOfSigning.insideValidity or timeOfSigning.outsideValidity accordingly.

sections.extract: A validator may choose to validate the "claimed time of signing" as attested by the value present in the iat protected header. If the iat header is present, the validator may validate that the attested time falls within the validity period of the signer’s certificate and all CA certificates up to the trust anchor, and not later than the time attested by any associated trusted time stamp. If the validator does the

sections.title: 14.9. Validate the Credential Revocation Information

summary.text: Describes determining the revocation status of the signer's certificate and CA certificates in the trust chain as important to deciding validity and trust. Recommends determining CA certificate status via the AIA extension and any included OCSP responses, and requires rejection with signingCredential.untrusted if a CA certificate was revoked at the trusted time stamp time or current time. For the signer's certificate, requires treating it as not revoked when revocation status is unsupported, and validating stapled rVals OCSP responses and any certificate status assertions in other manifests per Section 14.9.1, trying each until one passes. Recommends that an online validator query the OCSP responder per Section 14.9.2 if no revocation information is found in the C2PA Manifest Store.

sections.extract: Discovery of the revocation status of the signer’s certificate and all CA certificates that are part of the trust chain is important to determining whether a given certificate is considered valid and trusted. For CA certificates, the validator should determine revocation status as indicated in the Authority Information Access (AIA) extension as described in RFC 5280, section 4.2.2.1. The validator should make use of

sections.title: 14.9.1. Determining revocation through OCSP responses in the C2PA Manifest Store

summary.text: Requires a validator to decode OCSP responses per RFC 6960, including requirements 1 through 4 of section 3.2. Specifies that an accepted response establishes the certificate was not revoked at signing when the claim signature has a valid time stamp, a SingleResponse has status good with the current time no earlier than thisUpdate and the attested time before thisUpdate or within the (thisUpdate,nextUpdate) or (thisUpdate,producedAt + 24 hours) interval, and the signer is an authorized responder. Requires the validator then to issue signingCredential.ocsp.notRevoked or perform an online OCSP check, and to reject with signingCredential.ocsp.revoked if a response meets all conditions except that certStatus is revoked.

sections.extract: A validator shall decode OCSP responses per the requirements of RFC 6960, in particular requirements 1 through 4 of section 3.2. If an OCSP response is accepted, and if all of the following requirements are met, then this establishes that the relevant certificate was not revoked at the time of signing. The claim signature has an attested time provided by a valid signed time stamp. There exists a SingleResponse in

sections.title: 14.9.2. Determining revocation from online OCSP response

summary.text: Permits a validator to query the OCSP responder online when no stored response satisfies Section 14.9.1 or the claim signature lacks a time stamp, noting that such queries can reveal the asset being validated. Requires signingCredential.ocsp.skipped if the check is not performed and signingCredential.ocsp.inaccessible if no response is received. Specifies that an accepted response establishes non-revocation when the time stamp time (or current time if no valid time stamp) falls within (thisUpdate,nextUpdate), certStatus is good or revoked with removeFromCRL, and the signer is an authorized responder, or when a revoked status with another reason has a revocationTime after a valid attested time stamp falling within that interval. Requires signingCredential.ocsp.notRevoked in those cases, otherwise signingCredential.ocsp.unknown for an unknown status or rejection with signingCredential.ocsp.revoked.

sections.extract: If, for a given certificate, no OCSP response in the C2PA Manifest Store satisfies the conditions in Section 14.9.1, “Determining revocation through OCSP responses in the C2PA Manifest Store”, or if the claim signature does not have a time stamp, the validator may choose to query the OCSP responder, per RFC 6960, with the responder accessLocation found via RFC 6960, section 3.1.
