sections.title: 14.10. Validate the Assertions

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.10 Validate the Assertions; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.10.1. Validate the correct assertions for the type of manifest

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.10.1 Validate the correct assertions for the type of manifest; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.10.1.1. General

summary.text: States that, depending on the type of manifest, some assertions are required or forbidden, and requires a validator to check for required and not-permitted assertions.

sections.extract: Depending on the type of manifest, there are assertions that are either required or forbidden. A validator shall check for required and not-permitted assertions.

sections.title: 14.10.1.2. Standard Manifest Assertions

summary.text: Specifies the assertion checks for a standard manifest: there shall be exactly one hard binding assertion (c2pa.hash.data, c2pa.hash.boxes, c2pa.hash.collection.data, c2pa.hash.segment, the deprecated c2pa.hash.bmff.v2, or c2pa.hash.bmff.v3), otherwise rejection with claim.hardBindings.missing or assertion.multipleHardBindings. It also requires at most one c2pa.ingredient assertion with relationship parentOf (else manifest.multipleParents) and at least one actions assertion in created_assertions or gathered_assertions (else claim.actions.missing). Finally, a c2pa.created or c2pa.opened action must appear in the first actions assertion of exactly one of those two lists, else the manifest is rejected with assertion.action.malformed.

sections.extract: If it is a standard manifest: 1. Validate that there is exactly one hard binding to content assertion - either a c2pa.hash.data, a c2pa.hash.boxes, a c2pa.hash.collection.data, a c2pa.hash.segment, c2pa.hash.bmff.v2 (deprecated), or a c2pa.hash.bmff.v3. If no such assertion is present, the manifest shall be rejected with a failure code of claim.hardBindings.missing. If there is more than one such assertion, the

sections.title: 14.10.1.3. Update Manifest Assertions

summary.text: Specifies the assertion checks for an update manifest: exactly one ingredient assertion with relationship parentOf must be present, otherwise rejection with manifest.update.wrongParents. The manifest shall be rejected with manifest.update.invalid if it contains any hard binding assertions (c2pa.hash.data, c2pa.hash.boxes, c2pa.hash.collection.data, c2pa.hash.segment, c2pa.hash.bmff.v2, c2pa.hash.bmff.v3), thumbnail assertions, or c2pa.hash.multi-asset assertions. Any action in c2pa.actions or c2pa.actions.v2 assertions must use one of the values supported for update manifests, else the same failure code applies.

sections.extract: If it is an update manifest: 1. Validate that exactly one ingredient assertion is present and that its relationship is parentOf. If there is not (i.e., either it is missing, there are more than one, or the value of relationship is not parentOf), the manifest shall be rejected with a failure code of manifest.update.wrongParents. 2. Validate that there are no c2pa.hash.data, c2pa.hash.boxes, c2pa.hash.collection.data,

sections.title: 14.10.2. Preparing the list of redacted assertions

summary.text: Requires a validator processing a claim to gather the set of redacted assertions for each ingredient's manifest from the JUMBF URIs in its redacted_assertions field, and forbids a claim's redacted_assertions from referencing any of its own assertions. A note explains that assertions can be redacted at any point in the asset's provenance history, not only by the claim generator that first used the ingredient; further detail is in section 14.11.3.2 Performing explicit validation.

sections.extract: A validator, when processing a claim, shall gather the set of redacted assertions for each ingredient’s manifest (if present) based on each JUMBF URI listed in its redacted_assertions field. A claim’s redacted_assertions field shall never include a JUMBF URI to any of its own assertions. NOTE: Assertions can be redacted from ingredient assets at any point in the final asset’s provenance history, and not necessarily

sections.title: 14.10.3. Redacted Assertion Representation

summary.text: Specifies that a redacted assertion may either be removed entirely from the assertion store or keep its labelled assertion container with its content boxes replaced by a single UUID Content box carrying the C2PA Redaction UUID (CAA98EEE-9D4D-F80E-86AD-4DFFCA263973) and a DATA field of only zeros. A validator shall accept either representation as validly redacted.

sections.extract: A redacted assertion may be represented in the assertion store either by being removed entirely, or by having its labelled assertion container retained with the JUMBF Content boxes within it replaced by a single UUID Content box whose ID field has a value of CAA98EEE-9D4D-F80E-86AD-4DFFCA263973 (called the C2PA Redaction UUID) and whose DATA field contains only zeros (binary 0x00 values). A validator shall accept

sections.title: 14.10.4. Assertion Validation

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.10.4 Assertion Validation; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.10.4.1. General

summary.text: Defines the general validation procedure for each hashed_uri in a claim's created_assertions and gathered_assertions (or a v1 claim's assertions). Redacted assertions are treated as valid unless labelled c2pa.actions or c2pa.actions.v2 (rejected with assertion.action.redacted); other assertions must resolve within the same manifest (else assertion.outsideManifest or assertion.missing) and their computed hash must match (else assertion.hashedURI.mismatch, otherwise assertion.hashedURI.match is recorded). The claim shall also be rejected for malformed CBOR or non-conforming JSON (assertion.cbor.invalid or assertion.json.invalid), for assertions in the store that the claim does not reference (assertion.undeclared), and for redacted_assertions URIs pointing into the claim's own manifest (assertion.selfRedacted). Assertion metadata is not validated except that processStart must not be later than processEnd, else assertion.metadata.malformed.

sections.extract: Each assertion in the created_assertions and gathered_assertions fields of the claim (and in the assertions field of a v1 claim) is a hashed_uri structure. For each assertion, the validator shall first determine if the URI reference in the url field is in the list of redacted assertions. NOTE: Even though the assertions listed in the gathered_assertions field were not created by the claim generator, they are still

sections.title: 14.10.4.2. Specific Assertion Validation

summary.text: Requires the validator to check each assertion's label and perform the specific validation steps for listed types: c2pa.cloud-data, c2pa.external-reference, c2pa.actions or c2pa.actions.v2, c2pa.linked-resource-integrity, c2pa.metadata, c2pa.session-keys, c2pa.time-stamp and c2pa.alternative-content-representation; unlisted types need no further steps. A note says ingredient assertions are validated separately under section 14.11 Validate the Ingredients. Any hashed_uri or hashed_ext_uri field in a standard assertion shall be validated per section 14.10.4.3 Validation of References, except the activeManifest field of c2pa.ingredient.v3 and the externalResources entries of c2pa.linked-resource-integrity, which have their own procedures.

sections.extract: For each assertion, the validator shall check the assertion’s label and if it is listed below, the validator shall perform the specific validation steps for that assertion type. If the assertion’s label is not listed below, then that type of assertion does not require any additional validation steps beyond those already described. c2pa.cloud-data, Section 14.10.4.2.1, “c2pa.cloud-data validation”

sections.title: 14.10.4.2.1. c2pa.cloud-data validation

summary.text: Specifies validation of c2pa.cloud-data assertions: the label, size and location fields must be present, otherwise rejection with assertion.cloud-data.malformed. The claim shall be rejected with assertion.cloud-data.hardBinding if the external label is a hard binding or multi-asset hash label, with assertion.cloud-data.actions if an update manifest references an actions label, and with assertion.cloud-data.malformed if the label is an actions, cloud-data or ingredient label. The location field is validated per section 14.10.5.2 Validation of External References, and if retrieved, the JUMBF box label must match the label field or the claim is rejected with assertion.cloud-data.labelMismatch.

sections.extract: If the assertion’s label is c2pa.cloud-data: 1. Check that the assertion contains the following fields: label, size, and location. If any of those fields are missing, the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.cloud-data.malformed. 2. If the label field of the external assertion is any of the following values, the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.cloud-data.hardBinding. 1.

sections.title: 14.10.4.2.2. c2pa.external-reference validation

summary.text: Specifies validation of c2pa.external-reference assertions: a location field with a url field is required, and location must contain both or neither of alg and hash, otherwise rejection with assertion.external-reference.malformed. When hashed data is retrieved, a hash mismatch is reported as assertion.external-reference.hashMismatch. A label field naming an actions, cloud-data, external-reference, hard binding, multi-asset hash or ingredient label causes rejection with assertion.external-reference.malformed, and a retrieved JUMBF box whose label differs from the label field is reported as assertion.external-reference.labelMismatch.

sections.extract: If the assertion’s label is c2pa.external-reference: 1. Check that the assertion contains a location field with a url field. If it is missing, the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.external-reference.malformed. 2. If the location field contains one of alg or hash but not both, the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.external-reference.malformed. 3. If the location field

sections.title: 14.10.4.2.3. c2pa.linked-resource-integrity validation

summary.text: Specifies validation of c2pa.linked-resource-integrity assertions: the assertion must be in created_assertions (else assertion.linkedResourceIntegrity.notCreated) and its resources field must hold a non-empty externalResources array or a non-empty relativeResources array with an alg field (else assertion.linkedResourceIntegrity.malformed). Each well-formed entry receives exactly one terminal code, including a resourceUrl field: skipped if not retrieved, or match, inaccessible, sizeMismatch, formatMismatch or hashMismatch, none of which cause rejection. External entries need url, alg and hash and follow section 14.10.5.2 Validation of External References with the mismatch codes remapped to informational ones. Relative entries need uri and hash, the shared alg is checked per section 14.4.4 Algorithm validation, and a decoded uri containing a path segment of exactly .. causes rejection with assertion.linkedResourceIntegrity.invalidURI before retrieved data is checked for size, format and hash.

sections.extract: If the assertion’s label is c2pa.linked-resource-integrity: 1. Check that the assertion appears in the claim’s created_assertions array. If it does not, the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.linkedResourceIntegrity.notCreated. 2. Check that the assertion’s resources field is an object containing either a non-empty externalResources array, or a non-empty relativeResources array together with an

sections.title: 14.10.4.2.4. c2pa.actions validation

summary.text: Specifies validation of c2pa.actions and c2pa.actions.v2 assertions, noting that when, whenStart and whenEnd get syntax and consistency checks but shall not be compared to an external time source. An actions field is required, and in v2 when may not appear with whenStart or whenEnd and whenStart must not be later than whenEnd (else assertion.action.malformed); c2pa.created or c2pa.opened is only allowed as the first action of the first actions assertion. Actions c2pa.opened, c2pa.placed, c2pa.removed, c2pa.deleted, c2pa.transcoded and c2pa.repackaged must reference ingredient assertions with the expected relationship and manifest location, otherwise assertion.action.ingredientMismatch (with an informational assertion.action.ingredientLocationMismatch for a v2 claim whose ingredient is listed in a different field). It further covers c2pa.redacted needing a resolvable JUMBF URI (else assertion.action.redactionMismatch), validation of icon fields and relatedAssertions entries, and the requirement that c2pa.watermarked or c2pa.watermarked.bound actions be accompanied by a c2pa.soft-binding assertion (else assertion.action.softBindingMissing).

sections.extract: If the assertion’s label is c2pa.actions or c2pa.actions.v2: The when, whenStart, and whenEnd fields are claim generator provided timestamps annotate the time within which an action occurred. Validators shall apply the syntax and internal-consistency checks below but shall not compare these fields with an external time source. 1. Ensure that it has an actions field. sections.title: 14.10.4.2.5. c2pa.metadata validation

summary.text: States that c2pa.metadata needs no assertion-specific validation. Although generators are still required to limit metadata to the allowed list, validators should not reject assertions containing unlisted fields, to support forward compatibility, unlike earlier versions of the specification.

sections.extract: No assertion-specific validation is required for c2pa.metadata. Previous versions of this specification required validators to check metadata against the allowed list. While generators are still required to limit provided metadata to this set of fields, validators should not reject assertions containing unlisted fields, to support forward compatibility as the allowed list evolves. <a

sections.title: 14.10.4.2.6. c2pa.session-keys validation

summary.text: Requires a validator to ensure that the signerBinding signature of a c2pa.session-keys assertion is correct, by verifying it validates using the session key and that its payload is the Signer's end-entity certificate. Session keys are valid only if this signature validates successfully.

sections.extract: If the assertion’s label is c2pa.session-keys, the validator shall ensure that the signerBinding signature is correct (which indicates that the session key private key is known to the Signer). This is done by verifying that the signerBinding signature successfully validates (using the session key), and that the payload of the signature is the Signer’s end-entity certificate . sections.title: 14.10.4.2.7. c2pa.time-stamp validation

summary.text: Requires a validator to ensure that a c2pa.time-stamp assertion is well-formed CBOR consisting of a single map with at least one key/value pair, otherwise rejecting the claim with assertion.timestamp.malformed. Because the time stamp token is validated as described in section 14.8.2 Validating the TimeStampToken, the validator needs to store it and its associated C2PA Manifest identifier for later use.

sections.extract: If the assertion’s label is c2pa.time-stamp, the validator shall ensure that the assertion is well-formed CBOR consisting of a single map (Major type 5) with at least one key/value pair. If this is not the case, the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.timestamp.malformed. Since validation of the time stamp token is performed as described in Section 14.8.2, “Validating the TimeStampToken”, the

sections.title: 14.10.4.2.8. c2pa.alternative-content-representation validation

summary.text: Specifies validation of c2pa.alternative-content-representation assertions whose type is exif.originalPreservationImage: at most one such assertion may appear in the active manifest, and exactly one of multiAssetPartIndex or embeddedOriginalPreservationImage must be present, else rejection with assertion.alternativeContentRepresentation.malformed. A multiAssetPartIndex requires a c2pa.hash.multi-asset assertion and must be an in-bounds index into its parts array. An embeddedOriginalPreservationImage must be a hashed-uri-map with a hash field whose value matches the computed hash of the resolved data, else assertion.alternativeContentRepresentation.hashMismatch; if no failures occur, assertion.alternativeContentRepresentation.match is recorded.

sections.extract: If the assertion’s label is c2pa.alternative-content-representation, a validator shall perform the following steps: 1. If the type field is exif.originalPreservationImage, the validator shall proceed to the original preservation image representation validation defined in original-preservation-image-representation validation. original-preservation-image-representation validation 1. sections.title: 14.10.4.3. Validation of References

summary.text: Describes how hashed_uri and hashed_ext_uri references in standard assertions are validated, excluding the activeManifest field of c2pa.ingredient.v3 and the externalResources entries of c2pa.linked-resource-integrity. A retrieved hashed_ext_uri follows section 14.10.5.2 Validation of External References. For a hashed_uri, a missing url or unlocatable destination is a validation failure with hashedURI.missing; otherwise the algorithm is determined per section 14.4, and a missing hash field or a mismatch with the computed hash causes rejection with hashedURI.mismatch.

sections.extract: Some C2PA standard assertions support referencing other boxes in the C2PA Manifest via the use of a hashed_uri and hashed_ext_uri. For example, there can be various references in actions, ingredient, linked resource integrity, and thumbnail assertions. For all hashed_uri and hashed_ext_uri fields in standard assertions, except for the activeManifest field in c2pa.ingredient.v3 (for which special validation behaviour

sections.title: 14.10.5. External Data Validation

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.10.5 External Data Validation; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.10.5.1. General

summary.text: States that externally hosted data referenced by cloud data or hashed external reference assertions is not retrieved during standard validation; a validator shall first successfully validate the claim and shall not retrieve external data from a rejected claim. Because retrieval is optional, failure to retrieve or validate external data shall not cause rejection. A validator that does retrieve such data shall follow section 14.10.5.2 Validation of External References, may apply the countermeasures of section 14.10.5.3 Retrieval Security, and shall validate retrieved labelled assertions as if they were embedded.

sections.extract: A cloud data assertion or a hashed external reference assertion contains URI references to (and hashes of) externally hosted data. Those references are not retrieved and validated as part of standard validation. A validator shall first successfully validate a claim before attempting to retrieve the external data referenced. A validator shall not attempt to retrieve external data from a rejected claim. As the

sections.title: 14.10.5.2. Validation of External References

summary.text: Specifies the procedure for validating external data from cloud data or hashed external reference assertions. The validator resolves the url and aborts if it is missing, a countermeasure is applied, or retrieval fails; it then returns assertion.hashedURI.mismatch without providing the data if the retrieved representation's length differs from size or its Content-Type differs from the declared content type (from dc:format, defaulting to application/jumbf for cloud data, with content_type ignored). For a hashed_ext_uri, the hash is computed with the algorithm determined per section 14.4.3 For Hashed Ext URIs; a missing or mismatched hash yields assertion.hashedURI.mismatch, otherwise assertion.hashedURI.match is recorded and the data is provided to the application.

sections.extract: The following procedure shall be used to validate the external data referenced in a cloud data or hashed external reference assertion. Network retrieval performed as part of this procedure may apply the countermeasures described in Section 14.10.5.3, “Retrieval Security”. 1. Resolve the URI reference in the url field and retrieve its data. If the url field is not present, the validator aborts the attempt by applying

sections.title: 14.10.5.3. Retrieval Security

summary.text: Permits a validator performing network retrieval to apply the countermeasures in this section before and during each retrieval attempt, regardless of which assertion type triggered it. If retrieval is done by a platform the validator does not control and cannot apply the countermeasures, the validator may route retrieval through a component that can, such as a server-side service, or may decline to retrieve. A note gives a browser-based validator as an example and recalls that skipping optional retrieval does not cause a claim to be rejected.

sections.extract: A validator performing network retrieval under Section 14.10.5.2, “Validation of External References” (or any other clause that references this section) may apply the countermeasures described in this section before and during each retrieval attempt, regardless of which assertion type initiated the retrieval. Where network retrieval is performed on the validator’s behalf by a platform that the validator does not

sections.title: 14.10.5.3.1. Permitted schemes and identifiers

summary.text: Permits a validator to limit automated retrieval to the https URI scheme and to decline other schemes such as file or ftp and non-network identifiers, noting that unencrypted http is discouraged by industry practice. A validator may also reject a URI whose authority contains a userinfo subcomponent before attempting retrieval.

sections.extract: A validator may limit automated retrieval performed under this procedure to the https URI scheme, and may decline to dereference other schemes (such as file or ftp) and non-network identifiers. NOTE: Unencrypted http is discouraged by standard industry practice. A validator may reject a URI whose authority component contains a userinfo subcomponent (i.e. user:password@host) before a retrieval attempt is made. <a

sections.title: 14.10.5.3.2. Credential handling

summary.text: Permits a validator to omit ambient credentials such as cookies, Authorization headers, proxy credentials or client certificates from retrieval requests unless the operator has explicitly configured them for that specific origin. A validator may also withhold credentials attached for one origin from a different origin reached through a redirect.

sections.extract: A validator may omit ambient credentials — such as cookies, Authorization headers, proxy credentials, or client certificates — from a retrieval request unless the operator has explicitly configured those credentials for the specific origin (scheme, host, and port) being retrieved. A validator may also withhold credentials attached for one origin from a different origin reached by way of a redirect (see Section

sections.title: 14.10.5.3.3. Address validation and connection binding

summary.text: Permits a validator to resolve the target host before connecting and check each candidate IP address against an address policy, disallowing loopback, link-local, private-use, unique-local or other non-publicly-routable addresses unless the operator explicitly permits them, and aborting if all candidates are disallowed. The validator may also bind the connection to a checked address, verify the actual peer address before sending data, and treat any later name resolution, including by a library or proxy, as subject to the same policy. Where the operator configures a resolving proxy, these checks may be delegated to it, and the proxy's own address is not subject to the policy. Notes explain that operator configuration supports enterprise private networks and synthetic-address tunnelling services, that the restriction exists because the URI comes from the manifest author, and that retrieval can disclose the requested hostname, which encrypted DNS, a remote-resolving proxy, or not retrieving can reduce.

sections.extract: Before opening a connection, a validator may resolve the target host to one or more candidate IP addresses and check each candidate against an address policy. Under such a policy, unless the operator has explicitly configured the validator to permit a particular address or range, a validator may disallow a candidate address that is a loopback address (IPv4 127.0.0.0/8 or IPv6 ::1), a link-local address (IPv4

sections.title: 14.10.5.3.4. Redirect handling

summary.text: Permits a validator to limit the number of HTTP redirects it follows per validation operation and to refuse HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects, aborting retrieval if either occurs. Before sending a redirected request, a validator may apply the scheme, credential and address countermeasures of sections 14.10.5.3.1 to 14.10.5.3.3 to the redirect target exactly as for the initial request.

sections.extract: A validator may limit the number of HTTP redirects it will follow for a single validation operation (see Section 14.10.5.3.6, “Resource limits”), and may refuse to follow a redirect from an HTTPS URI to an HTTP URI. If the redirect limit is exceeded or a downgrade redirect is encountered, the validator may abort the retrieval. Before a redirected request is sent, a validator may apply the countermeasures in Section

sections.title: 14.10.5.3.5. Retrieved representation

summary.text: Defines the retrieved representation used for the size, media type and hash checks in section 14.10.5.2 Validation of External References as the response body bytes after removing HTTP transfer coding and any Content-Encoding, but before any character decoding, parsing, normalization or other transformation. Requires all three checks to be performed against this same representation.

sections.extract: For the purposes of the declared-size, media-type, and hash checks in Section 14.10.5.2, “Validation of External References”, the retrieved representation of a response consists of the response body bytes after removing any HTTP transfer coding (e.g. chunked transfer encoding) and any Content-Encoding (e.g. gzip, br, deflate), and before any character-set decoding, parsing, normalization, or other transformation of

sections.title: 14.10.5.3.6. Resource limits

summary.text: Defines a retrieval attempt as a single request-response exchange and a validation operation as the full process of resolving, retrieving, decoding and validating the data for one hashed_ext_uri, unhashed_ext_uri or cloud data location, including redirects. Permits a validator to enforce per-operation limits on redirects, encoded bytes read, decoded representation bytes, decompression nesting depth and an overall deadline, and per-claim limits on total retrieval attempts and concurrent operations. If an enforced limit is exceeded, the validator may abort and discard partial data; a note says the size field gives an a priori bound on decoded bytes usable as a read limit.

sections.extract: For the purposes of this section, a retrieval attempt is a single request-response exchange, including a request made to a redirect target, and a validation operation is the complete process of resolving, retrieving, decoding, and validating the data referenced by one hashed_ext_uri, unhashed_ext_uri, or cloud data location, including all redirects followed for that reference. A validator may enforce, for each

sections.title: 14.11. Validate the Ingredients

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.11 Validate the Ingredients; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.11.1. Explanation

summary.text: Requires a validator to perform the validation steps for the presented asset and its active manifest, rejecting the manifest with the indicated failure code if any step finds it invalid. Explains that an active manifest may list ingredients via ingredient assertions, some of which may have their own manifests with further ingredients.

sections.extract: A validator shall perform the validation steps for the asset being presented and its active manifest. If any of the steps conclude the active manifest is invalid, that manifest shall be rejected with the indicated failure code. An asset’s active manifest may list one or more ingredients, through the use of ingredient assertions. Some of those ingredients may have their own manifests associated with them, and some of

sections.title: 14.11.2. Processing Ingredient Manifests

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.11.2 Processing Ingredient Manifests; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.11.2.1. Standard Manifests in an ingredient

summary.text: Requires that, when processing a standard manifest, a validator validate each ingredient regardless of its relationship value, as described in section 14.11.3 Ingredient Assertion Validation.

sections.extract: When processing a standard manifest, a validator shall validate each ingredient (regardless of the value of its relationship field), as described below.

sections.title: 14.11.2.2. Update Manifests in an ingredient

summary.text: Requires that, for update manifests, the parentOf ingredient be validated as described in section 14.11.3 Ingredient Assertion Validation.

sections.extract: For update manifests, the parentOf ingredient of the update manifest shall be validated as described below.

sections.title: 14.11.2.3. Time Stamp Manifests in an ingredient

summary.text: Requires that any time stamp manifests found in an ingredient be ignored, noting that this feature is deprecated in favour of the time stamp assertion and the text is retained for historical purposes.

sections.extract: IMPORTANT: This feature has been deprecated in favour of the time stamp assertion. The information below is retained for historical purposes. Any time stamp manifests found in an ingredient shall be ignored.

sections.title: 14.11.3. Ingredient Assertion Validation

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.11.3 Ingredient Assertion Validation; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.11.3.1. Validation Overview

summary.text: Presents Figure 13, Ingredient Validation, a flowchart of the process for validating ingredient assertions in a C2PA Manifest, and notes that the text is authoritative where it differs from the figure.

sections.extract: Ingredient Validation Figure 13. Ingredient Validation The flowchart in Figure 13, “Ingredient Validation” describes the process of validating any ingredient assertions contained in a given C2PA Manifest. NOTE: If there are any discrepancies between the visual representation and the text, the text is considered authoritative.

sections.title: 14.11.3.2. Performing explicit validation

summary.text: Specifies explicit checks on ingredient assertions, each failing with assertion.ingredient.malformed: the relationship field must be present and be parentOf, inputTo or componentOf, and activeManifest and digitalSourceType must not both be present. If relatedAssertions is present it must be a non-empty array whose hashed URIs validate per section 14.10.4.3 and resolve to assertions in the same manifest that are not ingredient or actions assertions and whose label ends with .ingredient, ignoring any multiple-instance suffix. A referenced assertion that has been redacted causes the informational code assertion.redacted to be recorded.

sections.extract: If the relationship field is not present in an ingredient assertion, the assertion shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.ingredient.malformed. The value of the relationship field shall be one of the following: parentOf, inputTo, or componentOf. If the value of the relationship field is not one of these, the assertion shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.ingredient.malformed. If both an

sections.title: 14.11.3.3. Performing recursive validation

summary.text: Requires the validator to recursively validate all ingredient manifests, with results equivalent to the described depth-first algorithm. The algorithm collects lists of ingredient manifest hashed_uri tuples (activeManifest or c2pa_manifest plus claimSignature) and redacted assertion JUMBF URIs across the lineage, rejecting with claim.missing or assertion.selfRedacted where appropriate, skipping unresolvable, mismatched or zeroed ingredient assertions and returning any validationResults status codes. Each ingredient manifest with matching redacted assertions is then validated by the claim signature hash method, otherwise by either that method or the manifest hash method, with validationResults entries reconciled against the validation output. A v3 ingredient with activeManifest but no validationResults yields assertion.ingredient.malformed, and validators should ignore other manifests in the store that are not in the ingredient list, for compatibility with custom and future constructs.

sections.title: 14.11.3.3.1. Claim Signature Hash Validation Method

summary.text: Describes the claim signature hash validation method, a full validation of the ingredient's claim without evaluating content bindings. The claimSignature url is resolved (else ingredient.claimSignature.missing) and its hash compared with the hash field, rejecting with ingredient.claimSignature.mismatch if absent or unequal; on a match, ingredient.claimSignature.validated is issued and the signature, time stamp and revocation information are validated per sections 14.7 to 14.9. Redacted assertions with a matching manifest label that contain anything other than zero bytes cause rejection with assertion.notRedacted, and non-redacted assertions other than hard bindings are validated per section 14.10. Under this method the validator shall not record hash mismatch codes for activeManifest, and notes explain that only c2pa.ingredient.v3 has a claimSignature field, so redactions in manifests referenced by deprecated ingredient assertions cause validation to fail.

sections.extract: This method includes a full validation of the ingredient’s claim, like that performed for the active manifest, except that content bindings are not evaluated: 1. Resolve the URI reference in the url value of the claimSignature field to obtain the ingredient’s claim signature box. sections.title: 14.11.3.3.2. Manifest Hash Validation Method

summary.text: Describes the manifest hash validation method, a faster option for an ingredient manifest unchanged by redaction when the validator trusts the previous claim generator's results. The activeManifest url is resolved (else ingredient.manifest.missing), its hash computed per section 14.4 and section 9.4.2.3, and compared with the hash field; a missing or unequal hash causes rejection with ingredient.manifest.mismatch, while a match fully validates the ingredient and issues ingredient.manifest.validated.

sections.title: 14.12. Validate the Asset’s Content

summary.text: Requires the asset's content to be validated using the hard binding in the active manifest if it is a standard manifest, or, for an update manifest, by following the chain of parentOf ingredients to the first standard manifest. If no standard manifest is found or it has no hard binding in created_assertions, the active manifest's claim shall be rejected with claim.hardBindings.missing. Notes that an asset may consist of multiple parts with their own hashes, per section 16.3.5 Multi-Asset Hash, which may be validated separately.

sections.extract: The asset’s content shall be validated using the hard binding in the active manifest if the active manifest is a standard manifest. If the active manifest is an update manifest, the hard binding shall be found in the parentOf ingredient’s manifest, or if that manifest is also an update manifest, by following the chain of parentOf ingredients to the first standard manifest. sections.title: 14.12.1. Validating a data hash

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.12.1 Validating a data hash; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.12.1.1. General

summary.text: Specifies validation of a c2pa.hash.data assertion: overlapping or negative exclusion ranges cause rejection with assertion.dataHash.malformed, and when update manifests are present the C2PA Manifest Store exclusion length and later range starts are adjusted for the store's current length. The hash is computed over the asset bytes outside the exclusion ranges; an exclusion running past the end of the asset, a missing hash field, or non-permitted data within the manifest store exclusion causes rejection with assertion.dataHash.mismatch, and an unlisted alg causes algorithm.unsupported. Additional exclusions beyond the manifest store and padding produce the informational code assertion.dataHash.additionalExclusionsPresent, pad and pad2 fields are ignored, and success yields assertion.dataHash.match. If the hash does not match, a multi-asset hash assertion is validated if present, otherwise the manifest is rejected with assertion.dataHash.mismatch.

sections.extract: Once a standard manifest (and its bindings) has been located, the exclusion range(s) shall be extracted from the c2pa.hash.data assertion. If the ending byte offset of one exclusion range (start + length) is greater than the starting byte offset of the next exclusion range in the array, or a start or length value is negative, then the manifest shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.dataHash.malformed. If

sections.title: 14.12.1.2. Hashing of JPEG 1 files

summary.text: Specifies that in JPEG 1 files the file format extras include APP11 markers and their segment length bytes, and requires a validator to match the total exclusion range length against the total length of all APP11 segments holding the C2PA Manifest to detect tampering. A note says APP11 segments used for other purposes, such as JPEG 360 or JPEG Privacy and Security, are not included.

sections.extract: In JPEG 1 files, the file format extras described above would include any APP11 markers and their respective segment length bytes for APP11 segments. Because the segment lengths are inside the exclusion range, a validator shall match the total length of the exclusion range with that of the total length of all APP11 segments representing the C2PA Manifest to ensure that the length was not tampered with. sections.title: 14.12.1.3. Hashing of Unstructured Text

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.12.1.3 Hashing of Unstructured Text; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.12.1.3.1. Validating a text data hash

summary.text: Specifies how validators shall validate a c2pa.hash.data hard binding for unstructured text with an embedded C2PATextManifestWrapper. The validator locates all valid wrappers (accepting decoded streams of at least manifestLength + 13 bytes and ignoring trailing padding), identifies the wrapper whose byte range, including padding, matches the exclusions, and rejects with assertion.dataHash.malformed if none matches. It then removes the wrapper bytes, normalizes the remaining text to NFC, encodes it as UTF-8, hashes it with the alg of the assertion, and records assertion.dataHash.match on a match or rejects with assertion.dataHash.mismatch otherwise.

sections.extract: For assets consisting of unstructured text with an embedded C2PATextManifestWrapper, validators shall perform the following when validating a c2pa.hash.data hard binding: 1. Locate all valid C2PATextManifestWrapper instances as described in Locating the manifest in unstructured text. 1. sections.title: 14.12.1.3.2. Validation Result Codes

summary.text: Lists the standard result codes for text validation: assertion.dataHash.match for success, assertion.dataHash.mismatch for a hash mismatch indicating tampering, and assertion.dataHash.malformed for a malformed data hash assertion such as invalid exclusion ranges.

sections.extract: Standard result codes for text validation: assertion.dataHash.match: Data hash validation succeeded assertion.dataHash.mismatch: Data hash does not match, indicating tampering assertion.dataHash.malformed: The data hash assertion is malformed (e.g., invalid exclusion ranges)

sections.title: 14.12.1.3.3. Partial Text Extraction

summary.text: Explains that partially copied unstructured text may have a truncated or absent C2PATextManifestWrapper that cannot be decoded, so the asset is treated as if no manifests were located. A validator may indicate to the user that the content appears to be a fragment of a larger asset.

sections.extract: If unstructured text carrying a manifest is only partially copied, the C2PATextManifestWrapper may be truncated or absent. A truncated or absent wrapper cannot be decoded, so the asset is treated as if no manifests were located, consistent with the manifest store location procedure. A validator may indicate to the user that the content appears to be a fragment of a larger asset. <a

sections.title: 14.12.1.4. Hashing of Structured Text

summary.text: Requires that for structured text assets the data hash be computed over the raw file bytes with the manifest block excluded via the exclusion range, following the general data hash procedure of section 12.2.2 Hard Bindings. A note explains that no Unicode normalization is applied because structured text files are byte-stable and NFC could cause false mismatches for legitimate NFD content, and that ASCII delimiters make the manifest block boundaries unambiguous.

sections.extract: For structured text assets, the data hash shall be computed over the raw bytes of the file with the manifest block excluded via the exclusion range in the data hash assertion. The validator shall follow the general data hash validation procedure defined in Section 12.2.2, “Hard Bindings”. NOTE: Structured text hashing operates on the raw bytes of the file without Unicode normalization. Structured text files are

sections.title: 14.12.1.5. Hashing of ONNX files

summary.text: Requires that for ONNX files the data hash be computed over the raw bytes of the serialized ModelProto with the Base64-encoded c2pa:manifest value excluded, following section 12.2.2 Hard Bindings. A validator shall verify that exactly one StringStringEntryProto with key c2pa:manifest exists in ModelProto.metadata_props, treating the asset as having no manifests if there is more than one, and shall verify that the exclusion range matches the offset and length of the Base64-encoded manifest value.

sections.extract: For ONNX files, the data hash shall be computed over the raw bytes of the serialized ModelProto with the Base64-encoded c2pa:manifest value bytes excluded via the exclusion range in the data hash assertion. The validator shall follow the general data hash validation procedure defined in Section 12.2.2, “Hard Bindings”. A validator shall verify that exactly one StringStringEntryProto entry with a key of c2pa:manifest

sections.title: 14.12.1.6. Hashing of SafeTensors files

summary.text: Requires that for SafeTensors files the data hash be computed over the complete file (8-byte header length, JSON header and tensor data) with the Base64-encoded c2pa:manifest value excluded, following section 12.2.2 Hard Bindings. A validator shall verify that exactly one c2pa:manifest key exists in the __metadata__ object, treating the asset as having no manifests if there is more than one, and shall reject the asset with assertion.dataHash.malformed if the header length field does not match the actual JSON header length.

sections.extract: For SafeTensors files, the data hash shall be computed over the raw bytes of the complete file (8-byte header length field + JSON header + tensor data) with the Base64-encoded c2pa:manifest value bytes excluded via the exclusion range in the data hash assertion. The validator shall follow the general data hash validation procedure defined in Section 12.2.2, “Hard Bindings”. A validator shall verify that exactly one

sections.title: 14.12.2. Validating a BMFF-hash

summary.text: Specifies validation of BMFF hashes: rendered content shall be validated against its hard binding per section 12.2.2, falling back to a multi-asset hash if present, and any failure or missing bound content shall be clearly signalled to the user and continue to be reported. For streamed or progressively downloaded content, not-yet-available portions are not failures, but each portion shall be validated before rendering and its sequence checked, with unexpected discontinuities signalled and Merkle location values required to start at zero and increment by one; content not rendered as intended, such as fast-forward, may be signalled as unvalidatable. With an update ContentProvenanceBox, the active manifest is searched there first and the parentOf chain followed to the first non-update manifest, whose BMFF hash is validated. The manifest is rejected with assertion.bmffHash.malformed for missing or empty exclusions, fragmented assets with both hash and merkle, or overlapping or negative subset ranges; extra exclusions yield assertion.bmffHash.additionalExclusionsPresent, pad fields are ignored, success yields assertion.bmffHash.match, and a mismatch defers to a multi-asset hash assertion if present.

sections.extract: For any portions of an asset rendered for presentation to a user, including but not limited to audio, video, or text, the corresponding hard binding corresponding to the rendered content shall be validated in accordance with Section 12.2.2, “Hard Bindings”. sections.title: 14.12.2.1. Non-fragmented asset using Merkle tree

summary.text: Specifies Merkle tree validation for non-fragmented BMFF assets: without fixedBlockSize or variableBlockSizes the whole mdat payload is one leaf, with fixedBlockSize it is split into fixed blocks (the last block should be truncated to the payload end), and with variableBlockSizes it is split per that array, which must match count and the payload size. Having both block size fields, or a count smaller than the computed leaf nodes, causes rejection with assertion.bmffHash.malformed. Leaf hashes that do not match merkle-map.hashes cause rejection with assertion.bmffHash.mismatch, and when count exceeds the number of hashes the auxiliary uuid C2PA box is required, else assertion.bmffHash.malformed.

sections.extract: If the bmff-hash-map.merkle field is present, the validator shall validate the Merkle tree. If the merkle-map.fixedBlockSize and merkle-map.variableBlockSizes fields are not present, the whole payload of the mdat is treated as a single leaf node for hash calculation. sections.title: 14.12.2.2. Fragmented asset using Merkle tree

summary.text: Requires that for fragmented BMFF assets with a merkle field the validator validate the Merkle tree, rejecting the manifest with assertion.bmffHash.malformed if the auxiliary uuid C2PA box is missing and with assertion.bmffHash.mismatch if the hash computed from that box and leaf node does not match the corresponding entry in merkle-map.hashes.

sections.extract: If the bmff-hash-map.merkle field is present, the validator shall validate the Merkle tree. If the auxiliary uuid C2PA box doesn’t exist as described in Section A.5.3, “Auxiliary 'c2pa' Boxes for Large and Fragmented Files”, then the manifest shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.bmffHash.malformed. sections.title: 14.12.3. Validating a general box hash

summary.text: Specifies validation of a c2pa.hash.boxes assertion: the boxes field must be present (else assertion.boxesHash.malformed), boxes must appear in the asset in the listed order (else assertion.boxesHash.mismatch), and unlisted boxes cause assertion.boxesHash.unknownBox. The hash algorithm is taken from the box-hash-map, box-map or Claim alg in that order, with algorithm.unsupported if none is valid; exclusion ranges are relative to the box given by boxIndex and must exist, not overlap and not be negative (else assertion.boxesHash.malformed), and missing names fields are also malformed. Hashes are computed over each box or range of named boxes, skipping exclusions and boxes marked excluded; data in the manifest store exclusion other than the store and padding, exclusions running past a box, or a missing or mismatched hash cause assertion.boxesHash.mismatch, with fallback to a multi-asset hash if present. Extra exclusions yield assertion.boxesHash.additionalExclusionsPresent, pad fields are ignored, and success yields assertion.boxesHash.match.

sections.extract: Once a standard manifest (and its bindings) has been located, the list of boxes to be validated shall be extracted from the boxes field of the box-map structure stored in the c2pa.hash.boxes assertion. If no such field is present, then the manifest shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.boxesHash.malformed. The boxes shall appear in the asset in the same order that they appear in the boxes array,

sections.title: 14.12.3.1. JPEG 1 Special Handling

summary.text: Requires a validator of a JPEG 1 asset to check that each box marked with the C2PA identifier is an APP11 containing part or all of the C2PA Manifest Store, identified as a JUMBF superbox labelled c2pa with type UUID 63327061-0011-0010-8000-00AA00389B71. An APP11 not part of the store and not in the hashed boxes list causes rejection with assertion.boxesHash.unknownBox.

sections.extract: When validating a JPEG 1 asset, a validator shall check that each box identified with the special C2PA box identifier is indeed an APP11 containing some or all of the C2PA Manifest Store. The C2PA Manifest Store is identified by it being a JUMBF superbox with a label of c2pa and a JUMBF type UUID of 63327061-0011-0010-8000-00AA00389B71 as described in Section 11.5, “Serialization”. If an APP11 that is not part of

sections.title: 14.12.3.2. JPEG-XL Special Handling

summary.text: States that in JPEG-XL the C2PA Manifest Store is a top-level JUMBF box, and requires the box containing it to be identified with the special C2PA box identifier; the store is recognised as a JUMBF superbox labelled c2pa with type UUID 63327061-0011-0010-8000-00AA00389B71.

sections.extract: When validating JPEG-XL the C2PA Manifest Store is a top level JUMBF box (JUMB). The box containing the C2PA Manifest Store shall be identified with the special C2PA box identifier. The C2PA Manifest Store is identified by it being a JUMBF superbox with a label of c2pa and a JUMBF type UUID of 63327061-0011-0010-8000-00AA00389B71 as described in Section 11.5, “Serialization”.

sections.title: 14.12.3.3. Font Special Handling

summary.text: Requires a validator of a font to check that the box for the font's C2PA table is present and determine whether it holds an embedded manifest, a remote manifest URI or both. Font tables not covered by any box cause rejection with assertion.boxesHash.unknownBox.

sections.extract: When validating a font, a validator shall check that the box corresponding with the font’s C2PA table is present, and determine whether it contains an embedded manifest, a remote manifest URI or both. If any font tables are present which are not covered by any box, then the manifest shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.boxesHash.unknownBox.

sections.title: 14.12.4. Validating a multi-asset hash

summary.text: Specifies that if standard hard binding validation fails and a multi-asset hash assertion is in created_assertions, the validator shall validate it; more than one such assertion, a missing or empty parts array, or a part lacking a valid locator and hashAssertion causes rejection with assertion.multiAssetHash.malformed. Byte-offset locators need non-negative byteOffset and length, and bmffBox locators must reference a present box. A missing non-optional part causes assertion.multiAssetHash.missingPart while optional parts are skipped, and overlapping parts or parts not covering every byte cause assertion.multiAssetHash.malformed. Each part is hashed with its referenced method using offsets relative to the part start, with truncation or mismatch causing assertion.multiAssetHash.mismatch; if all parts validate, assertion.multiAssetHash.match is recorded and no hard binding failure codes are recorded.

sections.extract: If the standard validation of the hard binding in the standard manifest fails, and the standard manifest contains a multi-asset hash assertion in created_assertions, then the validator shall proceed to validate the multi-asset hash assertion. If more than one multi-asset hash assertion is present, then the manifest shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.multiAssetHash.malformed. Validation of the

sections.title: 14.12.5. Validating a collection data hash

summary.text: Heading that opens section 14.12.5 Validating a collection data hash; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 14.12.5.1. General

summary.text: Specifies validation of a c2pa.hash.collection.data assertion by iterating over its uris array, rejecting with assertion.collectionHash.malformed if uris is missing or any entry lacks uri or hash. Each uri shall be checked before use and rejected with assertion.collectionHash.invalidURI if it contains . or ..; each retrieved asset is hashed over all its bytes, with a mismatch causing assertion.collectionHash.mismatch and a match adding assertion.collectionHash.match. Any listed file not found causes rejection with assertion.collectionHash.incorrectFileCount.

sections.extract: Validation of a collection data hash assertion (c2pa.hash.collection.data) that has been located in a standard manifest shall be performed by iterating over the array of uris in the collection-data-hash-map. If there is no uris field present, then the manifest shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.collectionHash.malformed. Follow the procedure in Section 14.4, “Determining the hashing algorithm” to

sections.title: 14.12.5.2. Extras for ZIP

summary.text: States that for ZIP files the collection data hash includes a zip_central_directory_hash field hashing every central directory header and the end of central directory record with the same algorithm as the hash field. A validator shall check that this field is present and matches, rejecting the manifest with assertion.collectionHash.mismatch otherwise.

sections.extract: In a ZIP file with an associated C2PA Manifest, the collection data hash contains the additional zip_central_directory_hash field. As described earlier, this field contains a hash of every "central directory header" in the ZIP Central Directory as well as the "end of central directory record" (which is the last part of a ZIP file). The hash algorithm used for this field is the same as the one used for the hash field

sections.title: 14.12.5.3. Hashing of WARC files

summary.text: Specifies that for WARC files the collection data hash covers every record except the C2PA manifest record, each hashed over its uncompressed bytes. Because WARC has no central directory, a validator shall reject with assertion.collectionHash.mismatch if any two non-manifest records share a WARC-Record-ID, and shall verify that records and uris entries correspond one-to-one by matching uri to WARC-Record-ID, rejecting with the same code otherwise, so that appended or duplicated records cannot leave the manifest valid. Compressed records shall be decompressed under an implementation-defined maximum size and rejected with assertion.collectionHash.mismatch if they exceed it or if the decompressed length differs from Content-Length, which a note explains bounds work from maliciously crafted records.

sections.extract: For WARC files, the collection data hash covers every record other than the C2PA manifest record, and each record’s hash is computed over its uncompressed bytes, as described in Section A.10.3, “Hashing”. A WARC file has no central directory that fixes the complete set of records present, so the collection data hash on its own binds only the records it lists. sections.title: 14.12.6. Validating a segment hash

sections.title: 14.12.6.1. General

summary.text: Specifies validation of a c2pa.hash.segment assertion over the file read in binary mode. The manifest is rejected with assertion.segmentHash.malformed if version is missing or unrecognised, if hash, segmentStart or segmentEnd is missing or segmentEnd is less than segmentStart, if predecessorSentinel lacks start, length or hash, or if sentinelLength presence does not match whether the sentinel line references the store externally (required) or inline (forbidden). The sentinel line must begin at segmentEnd, and the hash over bytes [segmentStart, segmentEnd) must match, otherwise assertion.segmentHash.mismatch; on success assertion.segmentHash.match is added.

sections.extract: Validation of a segment hash assertion (c2pa.hash.segment) that has been located in a standard manifest, as described in Section 14.5.2.5, “Special Considerations for Append-Only Text Files”, shall be performed over the file read in binary mode. If the version field is absent, or contains a value that the validator does not recognise, then the manifest shall be rejected with a failure code of

sections.title: 14.12.6.2. Coverage of the asset

summary.text: Requires that the checkpoints in a file together cover every byte. For the active checkpoint, the end boundary (segmentEnd plus sentinelLength, or plus the actual sentinel line length including its line ending) must equal the file length, the first checkpoint without predecessorSentinel must have segmentStart of 0, and every other checkpoint's segmentStart must equal predecessorSentinel.start plus predecessorSentinel.length; any failure causes rejection with assertion.segmentHash.partialCoverage. A note says these checks ensure every byte up to the active sentinel line falls in exactly one segment or sentinel line, with no gaps.

sections.extract: The checkpoints present in a file shall together cover every byte of it, so that content cannot be added, removed or replaced without a covering checkpoint. For the active checkpoint only, the validator shall verify that the sentinel line carrying its manifest ends at the end of the file, so that no content has been appended without a covering checkpoint. sections.title: 14.12.6.3. Validating the chain of checkpoints

summary.text: Describes validating the chain of checkpoints, where each later checkpoint records its predecessor's sentinel line position and digest and references its manifest as a parentOf ingredient. Starting from the active checkpoint, for each checkpoint with predecessorSentinel the validator shall hash the referenced bytes (rejecting with assertion.segmentHash.predecessorMismatch on mismatch), obtain the preceding manifest store from them, and validate its segment hash assertion per sections 14.12.6.1 and 14.12.6.2; a checkpoint without predecessorSentinel completes the chain. If an earlier checkpoint's externally stored manifest cannot be retrieved, the validator shall report manifest.inaccessible and treat that and all earlier segments as unverified, but shall not reject the active checkpoint on that basis alone.

sections.extract: Each checkpoint after the first records the position and digest of the sentinel line of the checkpoint that precedes it, and references that checkpoint’s manifest as a parentOf ingredient. Beginning with the active checkpoint, the validator shall, for each checkpoint whose segment hash assertion contains a predecessorSentinel field: 1.
