sections.title: 15. Live Media

summary.text: Heading that opens section 15 Live Media; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 15.1. Introduction

summary.text: Introduces the C2PA Live Media specification as supporting live, streaming and dynamic packaging workflows where content is created or packaged in real time, and outlining how to manage assertions for tracks in live sessions to ensure integrity and authenticity. Notes clarify that it covers live streaming and dynamic packaging and is not limited to video, provided the packaging is BMFF or delivery uses Enhanced RTMP (V2). States that this version applies to ISO BMFF content, ISO/IEC 23000-19 content, and Enhanced RTMP (V2) contributions via section 15.5 Verifiable Segment Info method, while being agnostic of manifest and delivery protocols, and does not support MPEG-2 Transport Streams.

sections.extract: The C2PA Live Media specification is designed to support the unique requirements of live media workflows, streaming workflows and dynamic packaging, where content is created and distributed in real-time, or packaged in a just-in-time manner. This specification outlines how to manage assertions related to tracks (video, audio, subtitles, etc) in live sessions, ensuring the integrity and authenticity of the content as

sections.title: 15.2. Compatibility With Previous Versions

summary.text: States that beginning with version 2.5 the term live video was renamed live media to reflect broader scope, with live video now considered a subset. Identifiers originally defined with livevideo nomenclature, including CDDL rule and file names, assertion labels and validation failure codes, are retained without renaming for compatibility.

sections.extract: Beginning with version 2.5 of the C2PA specification, "live video" was renamed to "live media" to reflect the broader scope of this specification. The term "live video" may still be used in some contexts, but it is now considered a subset of live media. IMPORTANT: Various identifiers, including CDDL rule and file names, assertion labels, and validation failure codes, that were originally defined with "livevideo"

sections.title: 15.3. Architecture

summary.text: Heading that opens section 15.3 Architecture; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 15.3.1. C2PA Manifest transport

summary.text: Describes live media manifest transport as building on BMFF embedding with two key requirements: content hashing shall use a standard bmff-hash-map targeting a segment (or the method of section 15.5.3 for Enhanced RTMP (V2)), and any C2PA Manifest Store in a live stream shall be in a uuid box per section A.5.1, or for Enhanced RTMP (V2) in a c2paManifest pair in a VideoPacketType.Metadata or AudioPacketType.Metadata message. The uuid box holding a manifest store may appear in any segment and is called the C2PA Manifest Box. Defines dynamically packaged content as prepared just-in-time on request, treats live media and dynamically packaged content as interchangeable terms, and notes that live streams are always dynamically packaged but not vice versa.

sections.extract: The live media architecture builds upon this specification’s support for BMFF-based asset embedding, adding mechanisms to support real-time content validation. The two key parts of that are (1) any hashing of content shall be done using a standard bmff-hash-map (where the target of the hash is a segment) or, for content contributed over Enhanced RTMP (V2), as described in Section 15.5.3, “Carriage over Enhanced RTMP

sections.title: 15.3.2. Segment-based validation

summary.text: States that live or dynamically packaged streams require each segment to be validated independently, so each segment must carry its own content hash. Describes two signing methods, either of which can be used and validators need not support both: section 15.4 Per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method and section 15.5 Verifiable Segment Info method, the latter using a verifiable-segment-info in an emsg box or E-RTMP Metadata message together with session keys. Other C2PA-defined live media binding schemes may be used provided they compute segment hashes with a standard bmff-hash-map and embed or reference the manifest store via a uuid box per section A.5.1.

sections.extract: Live media, or dynamically packaged, streams require the validation of each segment of the stream independently of other segments. As such, the hash of each segment’s content needs to be provided as part of that segment. Two different methods for signing that information are described, enabling a given claim generator to choose the most appropriate one for its needs. Either method can be used, and validators are not

sections.title: 15.3.3. C2PA Manifest binding in an initialization segment

summary.text: Requires that, where an initialization segment is used, it contain a uuid box whose bmff-hash-map includes the moov box, cryptographically linking it to the media segments. In broadcast push scenarios the initialization segment may be repeated periodically and the uuid box need not be in every copy. A note explains the binding ensures the manifest corresponds to the specific media, preventing replay attacks and content substitution.

sections.extract: For those use cases that require (or desire) the presence of an initialization segment, it shall contain a uuid box, whose bmff-hash-map includes the moov box to establish a cryptographic relationship between the initialization segment and the media segments. For the subset of live media streams that are in a broadcast 'push' streaming scenario (e.g., over-the-air broadcast television without a pull mechanism), the

sections.title: 15.4. Per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method

summary.text: Heading that opens section 15.4 Per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 15.4.1. Description

summary.text: Describes the per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method, which a live media stream may use: each media segment shall contain a C2PA Manifest Box in a uuid box per section A.5.1, whose active manifest shall contain a c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertion with a hash covering the segment and no merkle field, plus a live media segment assertion, and may contain other relevant assertions. Claim generators may embed additional per-segment validation values derived from segment hashes, such as anchor-point chaining values. A note says this method does not need session keys, verifiable-segment-info-map or emsg boxes and can be used independently of the Verifiable Segment Info method.

sections.extract: A live media stream may use per-segment C2PA Manifest Boxes to provide per-segment validation. When using this approach, each media segment shall contain a C2PA Manifest Box carried in a uuid box as defined in Section A.5.1, “The 'uuid' Box for C2PA”. The active C2PA Manifest for each segment shall contain a BMFF hash assertion (c2pa.hash.bmff.v3) with a hash field that covers the bytes of that segment and with no

sections.title: 15.4.2. Live Media Segment Assertion

summary.text: Requires a live media segment assertion labelled c2pa.livevideo.segment in each segment's manifest when using the per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method, containing a sequenceNumber identifying the segment and a streamId identifying the whole stream (any unique string, such as a UUID or URL). It shall also contain a continuityMethod field indicating how cryptographic continuity between segments is ensured; the only defined value is c2pa.manifestId, which requires a previousManifestId field holding the previous segment's manifest identifier. Implementers may define other continuity methods and fields, named using labels as described in section 8.2 Labels.

sections.extract: When using the per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method, a live media segment assertion shall be included in the C2PA Manifest of each segment. This assertion, which provides metadata about the segment and its relationship to the live media stream, shall have a label of c2pa.livevideo.segment. The live media segment assertion shall contain a sequenceNumber field that provides a unique identifier for the segment. It

sections.title: 15.4.2.1. Schema and Example

summary.text: Gives the CDDL schema for the live media segment assertion via the livevideo-segment-map rule, with sequenceNumber, streamId, continuityMethod and optional additional fields, and the livevideo-segment-map-manifestId rule adding previousManifestId when continuityMethod is c2pa.manifestId; the complete normative schema is in section G.8.1 Live Media Segment. Also provides a CBOR diagnostic notation example of such an assertion.

sections.extract: The schema for this type is defined by the livevideo-segment-map rule in the following CDDL Definition (see Section G.8.1, “Live Media Segment” for the complete normative schema): ; assertion used to carry live media segment information ; this assertion shares sequenceNumber semantics with ; verifiable-segment-info-map livevideo-segment-map = { ; monotonically increasing sequence number for each segment

sections.title: 15.5. Verifiable Segment Info method

summary.text: Heading that opens section 15.5 Verifiable Segment Info method; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 15.5.1. Description

summary.text: Defines the verifiable-segment-info as a COSE_Sign1_Tagged structure giving concise per-segment information so each live media segment can be validated independently, used in workflows that sign segment information with session keys. Its payload is a CBOR-serialized segment-info-map that shall be present and not detached, signed by a private session key, with alg (and optionally iat) in the protected header and the session key kid in the unprotected header. The segment-info-map shall contain sequenceNumber (matching mfhd.sequence_number or the ISO/IEC 23009-9 indexing rules, and matching the live media segment assertion when both methods are used), manifestId identifying the current or still-active manifest, and bmffHash, a bmff-hash-map of the segment with no merkle field and an exclusion for /emsg boxes with value urn:c2pa:verifiable-segment-info. It may also contain an optional manifestUri hashed-ext-uri from which a manifest can be retrieved.

sections.extract: The Verifiable Segment Info Map (verifiable-segment-info) is a structure designed to provide concise per-segment information for a live media stream allowing for each segment to be validated independently. It enables the validation of each segment’s integrity and authenticity during playback, ensuring that the content has not been tampered with. It is used in workflows which are using Section 15.5.5, “Session Keys”

sections.title: 15.5.2. Use in an emsg box

summary.text: Requires that, in workflows using the verifiable-segment-info method, a verifiable-segment-info be present in the emsg box of each segment, noting this does not apply to workflows relying only on per-segment C2PA Manifest Boxes. Specifies the emsg field values: version 0, scheme_id_uri urn:c2pa:verifiable-segment-info, value fseg, presentation_time_delta 0, timescale and event_duration covering the segment, a session-unique id, and message_data holding the encoded verifiable-segment-info. Gives the CDDL schema for verifiable-segment-info and segment-info-map, with the complete normative schema in section G.8.2 Verifiable Segment Info.

sections.extract: When using the verifiable-segment-info in a live media workflow, a verifiable-segment-info shall be present in the emsg box of each segment of a live media stream to verify the integrity of the content during playback. NOTE: This requirement applies only to workflows that chose the verifiable-segment-info method and does not apply to workflows that rely solely on C2PA Manifest Boxes embedded in each segment. The

sections.title: 15.5.3. Carriage over Enhanced RTMP (E-RTMP)

summary.text: Describes carriage over Enhanced RTMP (V2), a message-based streaming protocol used for live contribution that does not use ISO BMFF packaging. For such content, rtmp-verifiable-segment-info is carried in a VideoPacketType.Metadata or AudioPacketType.Metadata message instead of an emsg box, with an rtmp-segment-info-map payload whose sequenceNumber and manifestId have the same meaning as before and whose segmentHash, an rtmp-hash-map, replaces bmffHash. A note says AudioPacketType.Metadata is not yet defined by Enhanced RTMP (V2) and its use assumes it will be added.

sections.extract: Enhanced RTMP (V2) is a message-based, continuously multiplexed streaming protocol commonly used for live contribution ("first mile") streaming, and does not package content using ISO BMFF. For content contributed over Enhanced RTMP (V2), rtmp-verifiable-segment-info is carried in an E-RTMP VideoPacketType.Metadata message (for the video track) or AudioPacketType.Metadata message (for an audio track) instead of an

sections.title: 15.5.3.1. Logical segment

summary.text: Defines a logical segment for Enhanced RTMP (V2) content: tracks are identified by media type and trackId (non-multitrack messages belong to track 0, and an absent trackId equals 0), and a segment is scoped to one track, with the carrying Metadata message required to belong to that track. A video or audio segment shall begin at the tag header of the first frame after the previous segment and consist of complete frames followed by one or more Metadata messages carrying rtmp-verifiable-segment-info. Publishers shall send Metadata messages on the same chunk stream as the track's coded frames, with a timestamp equal to the segment's last frame, which a note says guarantees unambiguous ordering. Consecutive Metadata messages belong to the segment they close, boundaries shall not split frames, sequenceNumber shall increase by 1 per segment per track, and each session key shall sign for only one track.

sections.extract: Content contributed over Enhanced RTMP (V2) may include multiple tracks of the same media type (for example, multiple audio tracks), identified by trackId when Enhanced RTMP (V2) multitrack support is used. For the purposes of this clause, a track is identified by its media type together with its trackId; audio and video trackId values are independent of each other, and an audio or video message that does not use

sections.title: 15.5.3.2. Segment hash computation

summary.text: Specifies that segmentHash in an rtmp-segment-info-map shall be computed with the alg algorithm over the concatenation, in transmission order, of each coded-frame packet's RTMP message timestamp (32-bit unsigned big-endian), composition time offset (24-bit signed big-endian, or 0 if absent) and coded media data. Only the segment's track packet from a Multitrack message is included, Aggregate Message contents are treated as individually transmitted with normalized timestamps, and no other bytes are included. Notes clarify that control messages, data messages, codec configuration packets and all Metadata messages do not contribute, that rewriting timestamps or composition offsets invalidates the hash, and that the TimestampOffsetNano ModEx data is not covered and so cannot be relied upon by a validator.

sections.extract: The segmentHash field of an rtmp-segment-info-map shall be computed, using the algorithm identified in its alg field, over the concatenation, in transmission order, of the following fields of each coded-frame packet of the segment: 1. the RTMP message timestamp of the message carrying the packet, as a 32-bit unsigned big-endian integer; 2. the composition time offset of the packet, as a 24-bit signed big-endian

sections.title: 15.5.3.3. Initialization data binding

summary.text: Requires a manifest delivered in a c2paManifest pair to use as its hard binding a data hash assertion without exclusions, computed over the E-RTMP initialization data, defined as the concatenated codec configuration payloads from each track's most recent SequenceStart packet (or legacy sequence header), video tracks before audio and by ascending trackId. Publishers shall send each track's codec configuration on that track's chunk stream and before the binding c2paManifest, sending a new c2paManifest before dependent frames if configuration changes. A validator shall validate this hard binding when it validates the first segment whose manifestId identifies that manifest, against the configuration most recently received before that segment's closing c2paSegmentInfo. Notes explain this mirrors binding to the moov box, that onMetaData is excluded because intermediaries rewrite it, and that multiple message streams on one connection share one manifest and so must not reuse a media type and trackId combination.

sections.extract: A C2PA Manifest delivered in a c2paManifest [name, value] pair shall contain, as its hard binding, a data hash assertion without an exclusions field, whose hash is computed over the E-RTMP initialization data. The E-RTMP initialization data is the concatenation of the codec configuration payloads (for example, [AVCDecoderConfigurationRecord], [HEVCDecoderConfigurationRecord] or [AacSequenceHeader], as defined by

sections.title: 15.5.3.4. AMF carriage

summary.text: Requires AMF3 object encoding in VideoPacketType.Metadata and AudioPacketType.Metadata messages, with the c2paSegmentInfo and c2paManifest values carried as native AMF3 ByteArray. c2paSegmentInfo holds the binary rtmp-verifiable-segment-info in the Metadata messages closing each segment; several may appear for one segment, for example during key rotation, and the segment is valid if at least one validates. c2paManifest holds a binary C2PA Manifest Store that shall include a c2pa.session-keys assertion, sent for the first manifest and whenever the active manifest changes, and should be on the video track unless an audio track needs its own manifest. Gives the CDDL schema for rtmp-segment-info-map (normative schema in section G.8.3 Enhanced RTMP Segment Info) and a CBOR diagnostic example.

sections.extract: Within a VideoPacketType.Metadata or AudioPacketType.Metadata message, AMF3 object encoding shall be used, and the value of each of the following [name, value] pairs, when present, shall be carried as a native AMF3 ByteArray: c2paSegmentInfo The binary-encoded rtmp-verifiable-segment-info, whose payload is an rtmp-segment-info-map, present in the Metadata message(s) that close each segment of the track carrying it.

sections.title: 15.5.3.5. Capability negotiation

summary.text: Requires C2PA Manifest support over E-RTMP to be negotiated in the connection handshake using the C2PA bit (0x10) of CapsExMask: a supporting client shall set it in the capsEx property of its connect Command Object and set objectEncoding to 3, and a supporting server shall set it in the Info Object of its _result. An endpoint shall not send c2paSegmentInfo or c2paManifest unless both sides signaled support, and a non-signaling endpoint should not expect them. Receivers shall ignore unrecognized pairs in Metadata messages and continue processing the rest; a note says negotiation avoids depending on legacy endpoint behaviour.

sections.extract: Because E-RTMP is also used by endpoints that do not support this specification, support for C2PA Manifests shall be negotiated during the connection handshake using the C2PA bit (0x10) of CapsExMask, as defined by Enhanced RTMP (V2). A client that supports C2PA Manifests shall set this bit in the capsEx property of the Command Object of its connect command, and shall set the objectEncoding property of that same

sections.title: 15.5.3.6. Reconnection

summary.text: States that an Enhanced RTMP (V2) reconnection does not affect a stream's C2PA state (active manifest, session keys and per-track sequenceNumber), so segments on the new connection shall continue each track's sequenceNumber. After reconnecting, a publisher shall resend the active manifest in a c2paManifest pair after each track's codec configuration and before the first coded frame. Notes explain that this supports moving to a different server instance, and that segments cannot span a reconnection, so a publisher can send each track's current c2paSegmentInfo before disconnecting to avoid unvalidatable frames.

sections.extract: The C2PA state of a stream (the active C2PA Manifest, its session keys and the sequenceNumber of each track) is not affected by an Enhanced RTMP (V2) reconnection (for example, in response to a NetConnection.Connect.ReconnectRequest): segments sent on the new connection shall continue the sequenceNumber of each track. After reconnecting, a publisher shall send the active C2PA Manifest again in a c2paManifest [name,

sections.title: 15.5.4. C2PA Manifest Updates

summary.text: Requires that when a new segment needs different assertions, such as changed provenance or replacement of expiring session keys, a new C2PA Manifest Store be provided, embedded in a C2PA Manifest Box, linked externally, or for E-RTMP via a c2paManifest pair in a Metadata message. The new manifest shall apply to all subsequent segments until another is provided, which a note says allows dynamic updates while maintaining integrity and authenticity.

sections.extract: When different assertions are required for a new segment (for example, to indicate different provenance or replace expiring session keys), a new C2PA Manifest Store shall be provided, either embedded in the segment via a C2PA Manifest Box or linked externally, or for E-RTMP-delivered segments, via a c2paManifest [name, value] pair in a VideoPacketType.Metadata or AudioPacketType.Metadata message. The new manifest

sections.title: 15.5.5. Session Keys

summary.text: Heading that opens section 15.5.5 Session Keys; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 15.5.5.1. Description

summary.text: Describes session keys as asymmetric key pairs that may use any algorithm allowed for claim generator X.509 certificates; they shall be generated at the start of a live media session, may also be delivered in later manifests, are each used for a limited period to enable rotation, and should be updated when provenance changes. Public keys are delivered in a C2PA Manifest, with the initial set in the initialization segment's manifest or, for E-RTMP, in a c2paManifest sent before the referencing c2paSegmentInfo. For an unknown session key, a receiver should check the segment's C2PA Manifest Box, then the manifestUri, and shall fall back to the initialization segment's manifest; for E-RTMP it shall use the c2paManifest matching manifestId and should try manifestUri if needed. The receiver shall ensure the retrieved manifest's identifier matches manifestId, and an externally hosted manifest needs to remain at its URI for as long as the content is provided.

sections.extract: Session keys are asymmetric key pairs. Any of the cryptographic algorithms allowed for claim generator X.509 certificates may be used. When using session-specific keys, they shall be generated at the start of a live media session, but may also be generated and delivered via updated manifests in later segments (either initialization or other segments). Each session key is used for a limited period, which enables key

sections.title: 15.5.5.2. Session Keys Assertion

summary.text: Describes the session keys assertion as the means of carrying one or more public session keys inside a C2PA Manifest, and points to the Session Keys Assertion section for its full description.

sections.extract: A session keys assertion is used to carry one or more public session keys inside a C2PA Manifest. The session keys assertion is described in Session Keys Assertion.

sections.title: 15.6. Live Media Architecture Diagram

summary.text: Introduces Figure 14, Live Media Architecture, which shows the general scheme of the data structures that can be used in a live media workflow and how each connects to the others.

sections.extract: Figure 14, “Live Media Architecture” shows the general scheme of all the various data structures that can be used in a live media workflow and how each is connected to the others. Live Media Architecture Figure 14. Live Media Architecture

sections.title: 15.7. Live Media Generation Process

summary.text: Heading that opens section 15.7 Live Media Generation Process; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 15.7.1. Per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method

summary.text: Specifies that, with the per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method, each segment's C2PA Manifest is constructed as described in Section A.5, Embedding manifests into BMFF-based assets, except that the bmff-hash-map hashes only that segment's bytes. Requires that a Live Media Segment Assertion (Section 15.4.2) be included in the manifest to provide metadata about the segment.

sections.extract: When using the per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method, the C2PA Manifest of each segment is constructed in the same way that is described in Section A.5, “Embedding manifests into BMFF-based assets”, but with the bmff-hash-map only hashing the bytes of that segment. In addition, a Section 15.4.2, “Live Media Segment Assertion” shall be included in the manifest to provide metadata about the segment. <a

sections.title: 15.7.2. Verifiable Segment Info method

summary.text: Describes the two steps of generating a live media stream with the Verifiable Segment Info method. In session key generation, one or more session keys, each with its own createdAt, validityPeriod and minSequenceNumber, are included in the C2PA Manifest in the C2PA Manifest Box that shall be present in the initialization segment(s), or in an E-RTMP VideoPacketType.Metadata or AudioPacketType.Metadata message; minSequenceNumber indicates the earliest segment that should be signed with that key, supporting overlap for key rotation. In signing the box hash, each BMFF/CMAF segment shall have an emsg box containing the verifiable-segment-info, a segment-info-map signed by a session key that carries a sequenceNumber against out-of-order attacks and a bmff-hash-map hashing the segment, and an updated manifest may be included in the segment or referenced via manifestUri. Notes explain that over Enhanced RTMP (V2) each track uses its own session key and an rtmp-verifiable-segment-info with an rtmp-segment-info-map is carried in Metadata messages, and that longer streams rotate session keys through subsequent initialization segments.

sections.extract: When using the Verifiable Segment Info method, there are two main steps involved in generating the live media stream. Session Key Generation At the start of a live media session, one or more session keys are generated, each with its own createdAt, validityPeriod, and minSequenceNumber. These session keys are included in the C2PA Manifest in the C2PA Manifest Box that shall be present in the initialization

sections.title: 15.8. Live Media Validation Process

summary.text: Heading that opens section 15.8 Live Media Validation Process; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 15.8.1. Initial/Common Validation Steps

summary.text: Specifies the initial validation steps common to live media segments. An initialization segment containing an mdat box fails with livevideo.init.invalid; a BMFF/CMAF segment with neither a C2PA Manifest Box nor a conforming emsg box, or an E-RTMP segment not closed by Metadata messages carrying a conforming c2paSegmentInfo, fails with livevideo.segment.invalid. A C2PA Manifest Box found in a segment shall be validated per Chapter 14, Validation, failing with livevideo.manifest.invalid if it does not validate. For Enhanced RTMP (V2) content, the validator shall have obtained the C2PA Manifest identified by the manifestId of the rtmp-segment-info-map (else livevideo.init.invalid), shall validate it with its hard binding checked against the E-RTMP initialization data, and shall fail the segment with livevideo.init.invalid if any coded frame's most recent codec configuration is not the one bound by that manifest.

sections.extract: If the segment being validated is an initialization segment, the validator shall look for the presence of an mdat box. If an mdat box is found, the validation shall fail with a failure code of livevideo.init.invalid. If a BMFF/CMAF segment contains neither a C2PA Manifest Box nor an emsg box that meets the requirements defined above, the validation of that segment shall fail with a failure code of

sections.title: 15.8.2. Per-segment C2PA Manifest Box Validation

summary.text: Lists the tests a validator shall perform when the C2PA Manifest in a segment's C2PA Manifest Box contains a live media segment assertion. The sequenceNumber must exceed that of the previous segment (unless it is the first) and the streamId must match the previous segment's, otherwise livevideo.assertion.invalid; continuityMethod must be present, otherwise livevideo.continuityMethod.invalid. If continuityMethod is "c2pa.manifestId", a previousManifestId field is required (else livevideo.continuityMethod.invalid) and must match the previous segment's manifestId (else livevideo.segment.invalid), and any other continuity method the validator does not recognize or support fails with livevideo.continuityMethod.invalid.

sections.extract: If the C2PA Manifest present in the C2PA Manifest Box contains a live media segment assertion, the validator shall perform the following tests: Unless the segment is the first segment, ensure that the sequenceNumber field in the live media segment assertion is greater than the sequenceNumber of the previous segment. If it is not, the validation of that segment shall fail with a failure code of

sections.title: 15.8.3. Verifiable Segment Info Validation

summary.text: Specifies how a validator processes the Verifiable Segment Info method: public session keys from a session keys assertion are extracted and stored, and a key that does not conform or whose signerBinding signature fails is invalid and causes livevideo.sessionkey.invalid. A non-initialization segment with a conforming emsg box but no valid session keys fails with livevideo.segment.invalid; otherwise the validator uses the kid from the unprotected header to find the key, retrieving the manifest via manifestUri if needed, and fails with livevideo.segment.invalid if the key is missing or the signature does not verify. The segment-info-map check also fails with livevideo.segment.invalid if the sequenceNumber does not increase, is below the key's minSequenceNumber, the BMFF/CMAF presentation time is outside the key's validity period, or the hash does not match bmffHash. The validator should also check that the certificate that signed the manifest providing the current session key is still valid, failing with livevideo.sessionkey.invalid if it is not.

sections.extract: If the C2PA Manifest present in the C2PA Manifest Box contains a session keys assertion, the public session keys shall be extracted and stored for use in validating subsequent segments. If any public session key does not conform to the requirements described in Session Keys Assertion, the validation of that segment shall fail with a failure code of livevideo.sessionkey.invalid. Similarly, if signature validation

sections.title: 15.8.4. Verifiable Segment Info Validation over Enhanced RTMP

summary.text: Specifies that for content contributed over Enhanced RTMP (V2) the Verifiable Segment Info validation steps apply, with the Metadata message carrying c2paSegmentInfo used in place of the emsg box and the rtmp-segment-info-map segmentHash field used in place of bmffHash, and session keys delivered in c2pa.session-keys in a c2paManifest metadata message. Lists the errors that cause livevideo.segment.invalid when parsing the rtmp-segment-info-map: a non-increasing sequenceNumber within a track, a sequenceNumber below the key's minSequenceNumber, validation time outside the key's createdAt plus validityPeriod window, a hash mismatch with segmentHash, a key identified by kid already used for a different track, or a Metadata message that does not belong to the track identified by its mediaType and trackId.

sections.extract: For content contributed over Enhanced RTMP (V2), the validation steps described in Verifiable Segment Info Validation apply, with the VideoPacketType.Metadata or AudioPacketType.Metadata message carrying c2paSegmentInfo used in place of the emsg box, and the `rtmp-segment-info-map’s segmentHash` field (see Section 15.5.3, “Carriage over Enhanced RTMP (E-RTMP)”) used in place of bmffHash. Session keys are delivered

sections.title: 16. C2PA Standard Assertions

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16 C2PA Standard Assertions; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.1. Introduction

summary.text: Introduces the standard set of assertions for C2PA implementations, noting that example JUMBF URIs are shortened for illustration. Requires all assertions to have a label per Section 8.2, Labels, and to be versioned per Chapter 5, Versioning; standardized assertions use the JSON, CBOR or Embedded File JUMBF content types from ISO 19566-5:2023, entity-specific assertions may use others, and the Codestream content type shall not be used. Unless otherwise stated, standard assertions shall be serialized as CBOR complying with the Core Deterministic Encoding Requirements of RFC 8949 with CDDL schemas, while JSON assertions use JSON Schema. Explains that the assertions are grouped into functional clusters, and that Metadata About Assertions and Regions of Interest are supporting structures used by assertions rather than assertions themselves.

sections.extract: This section of the document lists the standard set of assertions for use by C2PA implementations, describing their syntax, usage, etc. To keep things simple, all example JUMBF URIs have been shortened for illustrative purposes - full URIs are necessary in the actual data. All assertions shall have a label as described in Section 8.2, “Labels” and shall be versioned as described in Chapter 5, Versioning. All C2PA

sections.title: 16.2. Standard C2PA Assertion Summary

summary.text: Lists the standard C2PA assertions in Table 3, grouped by function (content binding and integrity, provenance and workflow, ingredient, content description and referencing, trust and validation adjuncts, policy and disclosure), giving each type's assertion labels, schema and serialization. Examples include c2pa.hash.data, c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 (with c2pa.hash.bmff removed and c2pa.hash.bmff.v2 deprecated), c2pa.actions.v2, c2pa.ingredient.v3, c2pa.metadata (JSON-LD), c2pa.session-keys and c2pa.ai-disclosure.

sections.title: 16.3. Content Binding & Integrity

summary.text: Describes the content binding and integrity assertions as those that bind a manifest to an asset's content and let a Manifest Consumer detect tampering, using either cryptographic hashes of the asset's bytes or soft (perceptual) bindings.

sections.extract: These assertions bind a manifest to the content of an asset and enable a Manifest Consumer to detect tampering, using either cryptographic hashes of the asset’s bytes or soft (perceptual) bindings.

sections.title: 16.3.1. Data Hash

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.3.1 Data Hash; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.3.1.1. Description

summary.text: Describes the data hash assertion as the most common hard binding for non-BMFF-based assets, recommending the general box hash assertion for box-like formats not compatible with BMFF. The optional alg field shall name an allowed algorithm (otherwise the Claim's alg applies), the hash goes in the hash field, and excluded ranges shall be listed in exclusions in increasing start order without overlap. Exclusion ranges shall begin and end within one logical unit without overlapping its header or length fields (except freebox or pad data), and the claim generator shall ensure they contain only C2PA Manifest Store content or asset metadata and cannot materially affect interpretation of the asset. The deprecated url field shall not be added and shall be ignored by consumers, and the assertion shall be labelled c2pa.hash.data and shall not appear in a cloud data or external reference assertion nor be used with a compressed manifest.

sections.extract: The most common way to uniquely verify the integrity of portions of a non-BMFF-based asset is via the hard bindings (i.e., cryptographic hash) present in data hash assertions. However, for those formats that are "box like" but not compatible with BMFF, the general box hash assertion is recommended. The alg field, if present, shall be a string that is one of the allowed hash algorithms as defined in Section 12.1,

sections.title: 16.3.1.2. Schema and Example

summary.text: Specifies the CDDL schema for the data hash assertion (the data-hash-map rule, with optional exclusions, alg, pad2, name and deprecated url, and required hash and pad), with the full normative schema in Section G.4.1, and gives a CBOR diagnostic example. Requires exclusion start and length values to use preferred (shortest) serialization normally, but to be written as 32-bit integers when they are not yet known. Requires pad to be present as a zero-filled byte string and pad2, if present, to be zero-filled, with Section 11.7, Multiple Step Processing, describing how to fill in values and adjust padding.

sections.title: 16.3.1.3. Special consideration for JPEG 1

summary.text: Requires that, when hashing a JPEG 1 file into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, the APP11 marker (FFEB) and segment length (Lp) of all APP11 segments containing the JUMBF data be included in the exclusion range. Notes that these APP11 segments are contiguous, so a single range is required.

sections.extract: When hashing a JPEG 1 (.jpg) file into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, the APP11 marker (FFEB) and the segment’s length (Lp) of all APP11 segments containing the JUMBF data shall be included in the exclusion range. NOTE: All the APP11 segments containing the C2PA Manifest JUMBF are contiguous so that only a single range is required.

sections.title: 16.3.1.4. Special consideration for PNG

summary.text: States that, when hashing a PNG file into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, it is important to include the Length and the 'caBX' chunk type of the chunk containing the JUMBF data in the exclusion range.

sections.extract: When hashing a PNG (.png) file into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, it is important that the Length and the 'caBX' (representing the chunk type) of the chunk containing the JUMBF data be included in the exclusion range.

sections.title: 16.3.1.5. Special considerations for TIFF-based

summary.text: Recommends that, when hashing a TIFF-based asset into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, the count field of the C2PA Manifest Store's IFD Entry be included in the exclusion ranges, to support Update Manifests that could change the size of the embedded C2PA Manifest Store.

sections.extract: When hashing a TIFF-based asset into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, the count field of the C2PA Manifest Store’s IFD Entry (representing the length of the JUMBF data) should be included in the exclusion ranges. This is to support Update Manifests, which could change the size of the embedded C2PA Manifest Store.

sections.title: 16.3.1.6. Special considerations for RIFF-based

summary.text: Recommends that, when hashing a RIFF-based asset into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, the size field of the top-level RIFF chunk (the four bytes at offset 4) be included in the exclusion ranges. Explains that this supports Update Manifests, since this size field covers the whole file and is rewritten whenever the C2PA Manifest Store size changes.

sections.extract: When hashing a RIFF-based asset into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, the size field of the top-level RIFF chunk (the four bytes at offset 4) should be included in the exclusion ranges. sections.title: 16.3.2. BMFF-Based Hash

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.3.2 BMFF-Based Hash; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.3.2.1. Description

summary.text: Requires that portions of a BMFF-based asset to be identified with a hard binding be described using BMFF-based hash assertions labelled c2pa.hash.bmff.v3. All Merkle trees used shall be balanced binary trees of minimum depth, with NULL padding only at the rightmost positions and each level more than half full. Notes that earlier versions documented c2pa.hash.bmff and c2pa.hash.bmff.v2, and requires validators to ignore any c2pa.hash.bmff assertions. The assertion shall not appear in a cloud data or external reference assertion, and the deprecated url field shall not be added by claim generators and shall be ignored by consumers.

sections.extract: Portion(s) of a BMFF-based asset that a claim generator wishes to uniquely identify with a hard binding (i.e., cryptographic hash) shall be described using BMFF-based hash assertions. A BMFF-based hash assertion shall have a label of c2pa.hash.bmff.v3. All Merkle trees used in BMFF-based hash assertions shall be balanced binary trees with the minimum depth necessary to accomodate leaf nodes, where NULL padding is

sections.title: 16.3.2.2. Hash Computation

summary.text: Specifies how the BMFF hash is computed: alg selects an allowed algorithm or defaults to the Claim's alg; non-fragmented MP4 needs hash, merkle or both, fragmented MP4 validated by Merkle tree needs only merkle, and live media segments need only hash. All file bytes are hashed except boxes or subsets matching exclusions entries, with box headers following the box's inclusion or exclusion, subset offsets measured from the box start and ordered without overlap, and in v2 and v3 each non-excluded root box contributing its 8-byte big-endian absolute offset concatenated with its data (the offset omitted for Merkle hashes when both hash and merkle are present). Defines exclusion matching by xpath, length, version, flags (with exact) and data, restricts xpath to a strict abbreviated full-path subset of BMFF 4cc nodes, and requires non-leaf nodes to be plain container boxes, with the box holding an embedded manifest always excluded. Requires 'free' boxes to replace or reserve space for excluded boxes, requires post-embed offsets to be hashed, and describes three ways to achieve this: pre-inserted 'free' boxes, a two-pass approach, or placing Update Manifests at the end of the file using box_purpose values original and update.

sections.extract: The alg field, if present, shall be a string that is one of the allowed hash algorithms as defined in Section 12.1, “Hashing”, and that algorithm shall be used to compute the hash. If the alg field is not present, then the hashing algorithm shall be determined by the value of the alg field in the Claim. sections.title: 16.3.2.3. Schema and Example

summary.text: Specifies the CDDL schema shared by the c2pa.hash.bmff.v2 (deprecated) and c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertions through the bmff-hash-map rule, with the complete normative schema in Section G.4.2, BMFF Hash. The map carries required exclusions plus optional alg, hash, merkle, name, deprecated url and sequenceNumber, with exclusions-map entries defined by xpath and optional length, data, subset, version, flags and exact, and merkle-map entries carrying uniqueId, localId, count, optional alg and initHash, hashes, and optional fixedBlockSize or variableBlockSizes for piecewise mdat validation. Gives CBOR diagnostic examples for a monolithic MP4, for fragmented MP4 files and for non-fragmented MP4 with a Merkle tree, plus pseudo-code for computing the BMFF-based hash and a suggested example of hashing for the Merkle map.

sections.extract: The schema for the c2pa.hash.bmff.v2 (deprecated) and c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertions are defined by the bmff-hash-map rule in the following CDDL Definition (see Section G.4.2, “BMFF Hash” for the complete normative schema): bmff-hash-map = { "exclusions": [1* exclusions-map], ; A string identifying the cryptographic hash algorithm used to compute this ; hash, taken from the C2PA hash algorithm identifier list. sections.title: 16.3.2.4. Exclusion list profiles

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.3.2.4 Exclusion list profiles; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.3.2.4.1. General

summary.text: States that this section describes a set of pre-defined, named profiles of extension lists.

sections.extract: This section describes a set of pre-defined, named, profiles of extensions lists.

sections.title: 16.3.2.4.2. Basic profile

summary.text: States that typical untimed media such as still photos and timed media such as videos, fragmented or not, need only include the mandatory exclusions listed in the Exclusion List Requirements.

sections.extract: Typical untimed media (e.g., still photos) and timed media (e.g., videos with or without audio tracks, whether fragmented or not) need only include the mandatory exclusions listed in Exclusion List Requirements.

sections.title: 16.3.2.6. Validation

summary.text: Describes validating a chunk of fragmented BMFF content: first validate the merkle-map initHash over the corresponding initialization segment, then locate the matching entry in the merkle-map hashes array and check it against the chunk's data hash, deriving it if needed with the Merkle proof from the chunk's bmff-merkle-map. Explains with Figure 16 that the c2pa-specific manifest box in each track's initialization segment contains the Manifest Store, which must be identical across multiple initialization segments, and that the active manifest's c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertion holds a merkle array with one merkle-map per track.

sections.extract: Validating a given chunk requires first validating the merkle-map field’s initHash over the corresponding initialization segment and then locating the correct entry in the merkle-map field’s hashes array and validating it against the hash of the chunk’s data, and if needed, deriving that hash using the Merkle proof from the hashes specified in the chunk’s bmff-merkle-map. summary.text: Lists the steps to verify an example chunk m+3: use the uniqueId and localId from the chunk's bmff-merkle-map to find the matching merkle-map in the init segment's c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertion, and verify the init segment by comparing its hash (using the assertion's exclusions and the merkle-map alg) to initHash. Then hash the chunk to derive D0,2, combine it with the proof hashes D0,3 and D1,0 from the chunk's bmff-merkle-map to derive D2,0, and treat the chunk as verified if the derived D2,0 equals the stored D2,0 in the merkle-map hashes and the initialization segment was verified.

sections.title: 16.3.3. General Box Hash

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.3.3 General Box Hash; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.3.3.1. Description

summary.text: Recommends that claim generators use a general box hash assertion, labelled c2pa.hash.boxes, as a hard binding for non-BMFF box formats such as JPEG 1, PNG or GIF; it is an array of structures each listing one or more boxes and a hash over them (including any data between them). Boxes shall appear in asset order, including the C2PA Manifest box, and unlisted or out-of-order boxes cause rejection during validation. Describes the excluded flag (letting validators ignore a whole box, with an accurate hash or the single byte 00 recommended) and the exclusions byte ranges (with boxIndex, ordered, non-overlapping, confined to one box and to manifest or metadata content), where excluded set to true takes precedence over exclusions. Requires each instance of repeated box types to be listed separately, defines alg fallback from box-hash-map to box-map to Claim, and requires the C2PA Manifest Store box to be listed alone with name C2PA and hash 00 as a single box even when split across JPEG APP11 segments. The optional pad and pad2 shall be zero-filled, and the assertion shall not appear in a Cloud Data or External Reference assertion.

sections.extract: A claim generator should use a general box hash assertion to verify the integrity, with a hard binding (i.e., cryptographic hash), of assets whose formats use a non-BMFF-based box format such as JPEG 1, PNG, or GIF. A general box hash assertion shall have a label of c2pa.hash.boxes. Such an assertion consists of an array of structures, each one listing one or more boxes (by their name/identifier) and a hash that

sections.title: 16.3.3.2. Special handling of multi-part assets

summary.text: Defines a logical box labelled c2pa.after for multi-part formats where part data follows the primary part's box-based data; if present it shall be listed last and its hash shall cover from the byte after the last box to the end of the physical file. Requires that only the whole-asset hard binding assertion may include a c2pa.after box, while a hash assertion for an individual part shall cover only that part.

sections.extract: To support file formats that consist of multiple parts (as described in Section 16.3.5, “Multi-Asset Hash”), one additional logical box is defined for cases where the data of one or more parts comes after the box-based data of the primary part. This box shall be labelled c2pa.after (for arbitrary data beyond the end of the box structure). The c2pa.after box, if present, shall be the last box listed, and its hash

sections.title: 16.3.3.3. Handling for specific formats

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.3.3.3 Handling for specific formats; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.3.3.3.1. JPEG 1-specific Handling

summary.text: Specifies JPEG 1 handling for general box hash: non-C2PA APP11 boxes shall be included in the hashed boxes, APP11 boxes holding the C2PA Manifest Store shall be identified as C2PA, and all other boxes shall use the symbols from ISO 10918-1:1994, Table B.1. Notes that the manifest store is recognizable as a JUMBF superbox labelled c2pa with the given type UUID, and that SOS and RST[n] boxes include their following entropy-coded segments. Explains that CIPA Multi-Picture Format files can be supported by listing all boxes of each Individual Image in sequence, but that if the file is treated as a multi-part asset the c2pa.after box shall be used for parts after the first image's EOI.

sections.extract: When working with JPEG 1, the APP11 box is used for standards other than C2PA (i.e., JPEG 360). In those situations, all non-C2PA APP11 boxes shall be included in the list of hashed boxes. The APP11 boxes containing the C2PA Manifest Store shall be identified by C2PA. All other boxes shall be identified by the symbol found in ISO 10918-1:1994, Table B.1. The C2PA Manifest Store can be identified by it being a JUMBF

sections.title: 16.3.3.3.2. PNG-specific Handling

summary.text: Explains that a PNG file always begins with an 8-byte header, and that to include it the special value PNGh is used as the first box in the list, with hashing starting from the first byte of the image.

sections.extract: A PNG file always begins with an 8 byte header (89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A). To include it, use the special value PNGh as the first box in the list of boxes and start hashing from the first byte of the image.

sections.title: 16.3.3.3.3. TIFF-specific Handling

summary.text: Notes that general box hash support for TIFF, documented in previous versions, has been removed in favor of the data hash because TIFF's indirection and structure make box hashing awkward, inefficient and prone to interoperability issues.

sections.extract: NOTE: Previous versions of this specification documented use of general box hash with TIFF. However, the use of indirection and other characteristics of the TIFF structure make box hashing awkward, inefficient, and prone to interoperability issues, so it has been decided to remove the general box hash support for TIFF, in favor of the data hash.

sections.title: 16.3.3.3.4. GIF-specific Handling

summary.text: Specifies GIF handling for general box hash: hashing a box with a Packed Fields attribute also hashes the optional data it indicates, such as Local or Global Color Tables. Requires boxes with a block label to be named "<Block Label>" and extension blocks to be named "<Extension Introducer><Extension Label>", with the header named "GIF89a", Table Based Image Data "TBID" and the Logical Screen Descriptor "LSD", and gives examples such as "3B" for the trailer and "21FE" for a Comment Extension.

sections.extract: The hash of a box containing a 'Packed Fields' attribute will also hash the optional data indicated by that attribute. For example, the Image Descriptor will include the Local Color Table block, and the Logical Screen Descriptor will include the Global Color Table block, if they exist. For all boxes containing a block label, the naming convention shall be as follows: "<Block Label>". For all extension blocks, the

sections.title: 16.3.3.3.5. RIFF-specific Handling

summary.text: Describes the nested RIFF chunk structure of L0 RIFF chunks, L1 sub-chunks and LIST chunks that nest further chunks, and specifies how they map to general box hash boxes. Each L0 chunk shall be a 12-byte box named by its media type identifier, each non-LIST L1 chunk a box named by its chunk identifier, and each LIST L1 chunk a box named by its list type identifier, with L1 boxes spanning from byte 0 through any padding byte. All L2 and deeper chunks shall be hashed as part of their LIST L1 chunk, and padding bytes shall be treated as part of, and hashed with, the preceding chunk.

sections.extract: RIFF file chunks may be nested in a tree structure of arbitrary depth. The root of this structure consists of one or more L0 chunks, each with the chunk identifier of RIFF. These RIFF chunks are defined with the following structure: Bytes 0-3: Chunk identifier, always RIFF. Bytes 4-7: Chunk length (minus 8 bytes for the chunk identifier and chunk length fields). Bytes 8-11: Media type identifier. Bytes 12-n: Chunk

sections.title: 16.3.3.3.6. Font-specific Handling

summary.text: Specifies that font tables, including the C2PA table, correspond directly to hash boxes enumerated in table directory order, with the table directory itself not hashed and checkSumAdjustment treated as zero when hashing the box containing the head table. Leaves the grouping of tables into boxes to the claim generator, noting that one table per box helps hashes survive re-packaging while combined boxes may not validate after a format transformation. States that, because font consumers shall not react to unrecognized tables, existing infrastructure expects the head table's checkSumAdjustment to incorporate the final content of the C2PA table.

sections.extract: The tables of a font correspond directly to the hash boxes, including the C2PA table. Tables are always enumerated in the order they appear in the font’s table directory. Note that the table directory itself is not part of the hashed content, and therefore not covered by any box. The checkSumAdjustment value shall be treated as zero (0) when computing the hash for the box containing the head table. The grouping, or

sections.title: 16.3.3.3.7. Ogg-specific Handling

summary.text: Specifies that, for hashing an Ogg file, each logical bitstream is treated as a single box comprising all its Pages in order, with the C2PA Manifest Store box being the bitstream identified in Section A.3.7, Embedding manifests into OGG Vorbis. Requires each non-C2PA bitstream's box name to be Stream-[bitstream_serial_number], using the ASCII base-10 value of the serial number read as a 32-bit little-endian unsigned integer, so that serial number \x01\x00\x00\x00 yields "Stream-1".

sections.extract: In an Ogg file, the structure consists of one or more logical bitstreams, and the data for each stream is held in Ogg Pages. For the purpose of hashing, each logical bitstream is treated as a single 'box', which includes every Page, in order, with the same bitstream_serial_number. The C2PA Manifest Store 'box' is the logical bitstream identified in Section A.3.7, “Embedding manifests into OGG Vorbis”. The box-name

sections.title: 16.3.3.4. Schema and Example

summary.text: Specifies the CDDL schema for the general box hash through the box-map rule (boxes and optional alg) and box-hash-map (names, optional alg, hash, optional excluded, exclusions, pad and pad2), with box-exclusions-map entries of start, length and optional boxIndex, and refers to Section G.4.4, Boxes Hash, for the complete normative schema. Gives CBOR diagnostic examples for JPEG 1, PNG, GIF, TTF and JXL. Requires exclusion start and length values to use preferred (shortest) serialization normally, but to be written as 32-bit integers when not yet known.

sections.title: 16.3.4. Collection Data Hash

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.3.4 Collection Data Hash; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.3.4.1. Description

summary.text: Requires that, when a C2PA Manifest is known in advance to refer to a collection of assets rather than a single asset, the collection data hash assertion be used to specify the hard bindings for the assets in the collection. Notes that each folder of an AI/ML training data set can be described as a separate ingredient of the full data set's manifest. The assertion shall be labelled c2pa.hash.collection.data and shall not appear in a cloud data assertion.

sections.extract: In workflows where it is known in advance that the C2PA Manifest will refer to a collection of assets, instead of a single asset, the collection data hash assertion shall be used as the method to specify the hard bindings (i.e., cryptographic hashes) for the assets in the collection. NOTE: It is possible to describe each folder of the training data set of an AI/ML model by having each folder be a separate ingredient

sections.title: 16.3.4.2. Schema and Example

summary.text: Specifies the CDDL schema for the collection data hash assertion through the collection-data-hash-map rule, which holds a uris array of hashed URI entries, a required alg and an optional zip_central_directory_hash, and also allows URN-based record identifiers per RFC 8141; the complete normative schema is in Section G.4.5, Collection Data Hash. Gives CBOR diagnostic examples for a list of remote URLs, a list of relative file URIs and relative paths inside an EPUB.

sections.title: 16.3.4.3. Fields

summary.text: Defines the collection data hash fields: uris is an array of uri-hashed-data-map values representing the collection, and alg, if present, shall name an allowed hash algorithm used for every member, otherwise the Claim's alg applies. Each entry shall have a uri that is a valid relative URI resolved against the manifest's location (except for container formats whose members use a native absolute URI, such as a WARC-Record-ID, where the uri shall be that identifier), and claim generators shall validate or sanitize URIs so that neither . nor .. appear. The uri shall not contain a query component, though a fragment is permitted, because it names a static hashed content item. The hash field holds the hash over all bytes of the content item with no exceptions, and the remaining fields are identical to those of an ingredient assertion.

sections.extract: The uris field consists of an array of uri-hashed-data-map values that represents a collection of assets. The alg field, if present, shall be a string that is one of the allowed hash algorithms as defined in Section 12.1, “Hashing”, and that algorithm shall be used to compute the hash of each member of the collection. If the alg field is not present, then the hashing algorithm shall be determined by the value of the

sections.title: 16.3.4.4. Hashing the members of the collection

summary.text: Requires each file in the collection to be hashed individually with the algorithm in the alg field, with the result stored in the hash field of the uri-hashed-data-map for that file's uri. States that not every file in a hierarchy needs to be included, noting that this also gives an adversary an opening to add files without invalidating the binding.

sections.extract: Each file in the collection shall be hashed individually using the specific hash algorithm defined in the alg field. The resultant hash value shall be stored in the hash field of the uri-hashed-data-map associated with the uri to the file. Not all files in a given hierarchy are required to be included in a hashed collection. NOTE: While this is useful in cases where there are files present that aren’t necessary to

sections.title: 16.3.5. Multi-Asset Hash

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.3.5 Multi-Asset Hash; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.3.5.1. Description

summary.text: Describes file formats composed of multiple parts that are each valid files, such as CIPA Multi-Picture Format, Android Ultra HDR, ISO 21496 HDR and Android Motion Photo. Explains that existing hard binding assertions cannot separately verify each part's integrity or record parts' own C2PA Manifests, and that the multi-asset hash assertion provides this. Also notes the case of an optional part that may be removed by a workflow without a trusted signer while the rest of the file remains verifiable.

sections.extract: There exist a number of file formats that are composed of multiple parts, where each part is itself a valid file format, such as when multiple individual images are aggregated into a single file. Some examples include: CIPA Multi-Picture Format (MPF) Android Ultra HDR format (which uses MPF) ISO 21496 HDR (which uses MPF) Android Motion Photo format (which doesn’t use MPF, but can exist alongside MPF in the same

sections.title: 16.3.5.2. Details

summary.text: Requires the multi-asset hash assertion to be labelled c2pa.hash.multi-asset; although it contains hashes and modifies hard binding handling, it is not considered a hard binding, it shall not appear in a cloud data or external reference assertion, and it should not be used with a compressed manifest. Every part, including the primary part, shall be a part-hash-map in the parts array, listed in file order, contiguous, non-overlapping and covering every byte, with a location locator giving either byteOffset and length or a bmffBox whose payload (excluding header) is the part. The hashAssertion field shall be a hashed URI to a standard hard binding assertion whose label has .part and any multiple instance identifier appended (e.g. c2pa.hash.data.part__2), with absolute offsets computed relative to the part's start. The optional boolean field defaults to false, and a part's own C2PA Manifest that is not self-contained is recommended to be stored in the asset's Manifest Store and referenced through a componentOf ingredient.

sections.extract: A multi-asset hash assertion shall have a label of c2pa.hash.multi-asset. Although it contains hashes and modifies the handling of the hard binding, it is not considered a hard binding. A multi-asset hash assertion shall not appear in a cloud data assertion nor an external reference assertion. A multi-asset hash assertion should not be used with a compressed manifest. NOTE: It is not clear if there exists a

summary.text: Specifies the CDDL schema for the multi-asset hash assertion through the multi-asset-hash-map rule, whose parts array holds part-hash-map entries with a location (either a byte range or a bmffBox), a hashAssertion hashed URI and an optional optional flag; the full normative schema is in Section G.4.6, Multi-Asset Hash. Gives a CBOR diagnostic example of a two-part 33,333-byte asset with c2pa.hash.boxes.part and c2pa.hash.data.part assertions for the parts and an overall c2pa.hash.boxes assertion using c2pa.after, and illustrates its use for an HDR gain map in Figure 17.

sections.title: 16.3.6. Segment Hash

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.3.6 Segment Hash; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.3.6.1. Description

summary.text: Describes the problem of append-only files such as application logs, event logs and JSON Lines streams, where a single hard binding over the whole file would be invalidated by the next line written. Explains that a segment hash assertion binds a manifest to one bounded segment, the bytes added since the previous checkpoint, and records the position and length of the sentinel line carrying its manifest plus a digest of the preceding checkpoint's sentinel line so history cannot be rewritten without breaking the chain. Refers to Section A.3.17, Embedding manifests into append-only text files, for how checkpoints are written.

sections.extract: Files that are written only by appending complete lines to the end of the file, such as application logs, event logs and JSON Lines streams, grow continuously and cannot be re-signed as a whole each time content is added. For these assets a single hard binding over the complete file would be invalidated by the next line written. A segment hash assertion binds a manifest to one bounded segment of such a file — the

sections.title: 16.3.6.2. Details

summary.text: Requires the segment hash assertion to be labelled c2pa.hash.segment; it is a hard binding to be used only for assets described in Section A.3.17, and it shall not appear in a cloud data or external reference assertion. The version field shall be 1, alg (if present) shall name an allowed algorithm used for both hash and predecessorSentinel.hash (else the Claim's alg), segmentStart and segmentEnd mark the segment up to the start of the sentinel line (segmentStart being 0 for the first checkpoint), and hash covers [segmentStart, segmentEnd). The sentinelLength field shall be present when the sentinel line references the manifest store by external URI and absent when it embeds it inline, because the inline length cannot be known at signing time. The predecessorSentinel field shall be present for every checkpoint after the first, locating and hashing the preceding sentinel line, and absent for the first.

sections.extract: A segment hash assertion shall have a label of c2pa.hash.segment. It is a hard binding, and shall be used only for the assets described in Section A.3.17, “Embedding manifests into append-only text files”. The version field shall be present and shall have a value of 1 for this version of this specification. An assertion that declares a version a validator does not recognise will be rejected during validation as

summary.text: Specifies the CDDL schema for the segment hash assertion through the segment-hash-map rule, with version 1, optional alg, hash, segmentStart, segmentEnd, optional sentinelLength, optional predecessorSentinel and optional metadata, and a predecessor-sentinel-map whose start, length and hash fields are required together; the full normative schema is in Section G.4.7, Segment Hash. Gives a CBOR diagnostic example using the offsets and hashes of the second checkpoint from Section A.3.17.6, Test vectors.
