sections.title: 16.3.7. Soft Binding

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.3.7 Soft Binding; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.3.7.1. Description

summary.text: Requires that a soft binding a claim generator provides for an asset's content be described using a soft binding assertion labelled c2pa.soft-binding. Deprecates the never-used url field in favor of the asset reference assertion, so claim generators shall not add it and consumers shall ignore it. Also deprecates the extent field within scope in favor of the region field, so claim generators shall not add it and consumers should ignore it; in both cases the field still counts as part of the content validated per Section 14.10.4, Assertion Validation.

sections.extract: If a claim generator will be providing a soft binding for the asset’s content, it shall be described using a soft binding assertion. The types of soft bindings which may be created and stored in such an assertion are described in Section 16.3.7, “Soft Binding”. A previous version of this specification provided a url field to provide a pointer to where the hashed data may be located, but it was never used. This field

sections.title: 16.3.7.2. Schema and Example

summary.text: Specifies the CDDL schema for the soft binding assertion through the soft-binding-map rule, with alg, blocks, optional pad, pad2, name, alg-params, bindingMetadata, deprecated url and metadata; each soft-binding-block-map has a scope (deprecated extent, timespan in milliseconds or region) and a value, and the full normative schema is in Section G.5.12, Soft Binding. Gives a CBOR diagnostic example using the phash algorithm with two timespan blocks.

sections.extract: The schema for this type is defined by the soft-binding-map rule in the following CDDL Definition (see Section G.5.12, “Soft Binding” for the complete normative schema): ; Align regions-of-interest object structure in soft-binding assertions with ; that used for other purposes ; # include regions-of-interest ; The data structure used to store one or more soft bindings across some or all ; of the asset's content

sections.title: 16.3.7.3. Requirements

summary.text: Requires the soft binding algorithm to be given in the alg field and the blocks it was applied over to be listed in blocks, and recommends that any extra algorithm parameters be placed in alg-params. Allows the scope field to contain either a region (a region-map from Section 16.9.2, Regions of Interest) or a timespan in milliseconds from the start of the content, and requires pad and pad2, if present, to be zero-filled byte strings.

sections.extract: The soft binding algorithm used shall be present as the value of the alg field, and the blocks over which it was applied shall be listed in the blocks field. If the algorithm used requires any additional parameters, they should be present as the value of alg-params. The scope field may contain either a region or timespan field to describe the portion of digital content that the soft binding has been computed over.

sections.title: 16.3.7.3.1. bindingMetadata

summary.text: Allows a soft binding assertion to include a bindingMetadata key carrying pre-defined and custom algorithm- or workflow-specific fields, with custom fields required to follow entity-specific namespacing (e.g. com.litware.someFieldName). States that a C2PA Validator should not use this information when validating the soft binding but may use it for logging or informational purposes, since the normative validation information is in the other assertion fields and the algorithm's entry in the Soft Binding Algorithm List.

sections.extract: A soft binding assertion may include a bindingMetadata key that provides for the specification of some algorithm or workflow-specific information via some pre-defined as well as custom fields (and their associated values). Custom fields shall conform to the same syntax as entity-specific namespacing, e.g. com.litware.someFieldName. NOTE: This is useful for providing extra information that would be useful to a

sections.title: 16.3.7.4. Soft Binding Algorithm List

summary.text: Describes the soft binding algorithm list, a machine-readable JSON document maintained by the C2PA at https://sbal.c2pa.org, as the list of recommended values for the alg field, which should match an entry's alg. Entries marked deprecated shall not be used to create soft binding assertions, and resolving with them is discouraged; validators should not resolve such bindings. Gives the JSON schema for entries and requires each entry's alg to follow namespacing and represent the owner, each algorithm version to have its own entry, type to be watermark or fingerprint, and supported media types to be given as encodedMediaTypes or decodedMediaTypes based on IANA types. Requires entryMetadata with a description and dateEntered, a required contact email and a required informationalUrl to a page describing the algorithm, including the algorithm-specific format of alg-params and value.

sections.extract: The soft binding algorithm list is a machine readable list of recommended values for the alg field. The value of the alg field should correspond to the alg field of an algorithm present in that list. The format of alg-params and value fields are algorithm specific and described via a human readable information page referenced by informationalUrl within the entry for alg in the list. The list is maintained as a JSON

sections.title: 16.3.7.5. Soft Binding Resolution API

summary.text: Describes the soft binding resolution API as a Web API for retrieving C2PA Manifest stores from an endpoint given a soft binding value, a manifest identifier or an asset. States that a soft binding algorithm list entry may list resolution API URIs in softBindingResolutionApis, any of which may be used, and points to the separate API specification.

sections.extract: The soft binding resolution API is a Web API providing a standard way of retrieving C2PA Manifest stores from a soft binding resolution API endpoint given a soft binding value, a manifest identifier, or an asset. The soft binding algorithm list entry may contain a list of URIs of soft binding resolution APIs in the softBindingResolutionApis field. If several URIs are given then any may be used for a soft binding

sections.title: 16.3.7.5.1. Validating Soft Binding Matches

summary.text: Describes using soft bindings to discover the active manifest in a manifest repository for an asset whose C2PA Manifest is absent or invalid, requiring discovery to use one or more algorithms identified in the C2PA Soft Binding Algorithm List. Requires that, if the located manifest contains soft binding assertions, the matcher ensure all of them match the soft bindings used for discovery. A soft binding assertion matches when both its alg and value match those used, with matching performed as the specified algorithm prescribes.

sections.extract: A common use for soft bindings is to discover the active manifest, from a manifest repository, for an asset whose C2PA Manifest is absent or invalid. Discovery of the C2PA Manifest shall be performed using one, or a combination of, algorithms identified by the alg field within the C2PA Soft Binding Algorithm List. The list is maintained as a JSON document by the C2PA at the following location: https://sbal.c2pa.org

sections.title: 16.4. Provenance & Workflow

summary.text: Describes the provenance and workflow assertions as those recording how an asset came to be, namely the actions performed on it and its relationships to other assets and external resources.

sections.extract: These assertions record how an asset came to be - the actions performed on it and its relationships to other assets and external resources.

sections.title: 16.4.1. Actions

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.4.1 Actions; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.4.1.1. Description

summary.text: Describes the actions assertion as an array of actions on the asset's content, each stating what happened and optionally when and with what software, with array order unspecified except as noted in Section 16.4.1.2. Distinguishes the deprecated v1 (c2pa.actions) from v2, which shall be labelled c2pa.actions.v2 and may derive actions from a templates array, and notes that actions are modelled after XMP ResourceEvents. Requires each action value to be a pre-defined or entity-specific action name. Lists the pre-defined c2pa. actions in Table 4 with their meanings and whether each is a perceptible or non-editorial transformation (for example c2pa.created, c2pa.opened, c2pa.edited, c2pa.modified, c2pa.redacted, c2pa.watermarked.bound, with c2pa.color_adjustments, c2pa.removed and c2pa.watermarked deprecated), noting that perceptible means an action can produce a perceptible change, and lists the font. actions in Table 5, which replace the deprecated c2pa.font prefix.

sections.extract: An actions assertion provides information on edits and other actions taken that affect the asset’s content. There will be an array of actions - each action declaring what took place on the asset and (optionally) when it took place, along with possible other information such as what software performed the action. Except where noted in Section 16.4.1.2, “Mandatory presence of at least one actions assertion”, the order

sections.title: 16.4.1.2. Mandatory presence of at least one actions assertion

summary.text: Requires at least one actions assertion in the created_assertions of a standard C2PA Manifest's Claim. For an asset created de novo the first c2pa.actions assertion shall begin with a c2pa.created action carrying an appropriate digitalSourceType (http://c2pa.org/digitalsourcetype/empty when there is no digital content); for an asset created by opening an existing asset as a parentOf ingredient it shall begin with c2pa.opened, with a matching c2pa.ingredient.v3 assertion referenced in the action's parameters ingredients. Notes that this does not apply to Update Manifests and that c2pa.opened needs no digitalSourceType, and requires that a manifest's actions contain no more than one c2pa.created or c2pa.opened action. Gives examples of a generative AI video, an image built from a template with placed photos, and a newsroom edit of a camera-captured photo.

sections.extract: There shall be at least one actions assertion present in the created_assertions array of the Claim of a standard C2PA Manifest. Furthermore: If the asset was created de novo (for example, as a result of performing a File → New operation in a creative tool, capturing a photo or video, or generating the media by a generative AI model), then the actions array in the first c2pa.actions assertion in the

sections.title: 16.4.1.3. All actions included

summary.text: Requires the claim generator to set the allActionsIncluded boolean in actions-map-v2, where true states that all actions performed are described and false states that unrecorded actions may have occurred; manifest consumers should interpret an omitted field as indicating that unrecorded actions may have been performed, and the field was optional in previous versions. Requires allActionsIncluded to be true when an asset is opened only to record c2pa.opened and immediately re-saved without other changes. Notes that external reference assertions with a hashed location can provide bound data about a process and be linked to actions via relatedAssertions.

sections.extract: The generator shall set the actions-map-v2 field, allActionsIncluded, which has a boolean value. If allActionsIncluded has a value of true, then the claim generator is stating that all actions performed on the asset are described in the actions assertion(s). If allActionsIncluded has a value of false, then the claim generator is stating that additional, unrecorded actions may have been performed. Manifest consumers

sections.title: 16.4.1.4. Fields in the actions assertion

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.4.1.4 Fields in the actions assertion; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.4.1.4.1. Description

summary.text: Allows an action to include a free-text description field explaining what the action does, most useful for non-standard actions but also usable to add information to a standard action, such as "Paintbrush tool" for c2pa.edited.

sections.extract: An action may include a free-text description, in the description field, of what an action does. This is most useful for non-standard actions, however, it may also be used as a way to provide additional information about a standard action. For example, a c2pa.edited action could have a description that says "Paintbrush tool".

sections.title: 16.4.1.4.2. Reason

summary.text: Requires that the reason field, if present, contain one of the standard values c2pa.PII.present, c2pa.invalid.data, c2pa.trade-secret.present or c2pa.government.confidential, or a custom value following entity-specific namespacing. Notes that only redaction-focused c2pa values are defined so far, and requires that a c2pa.redacted action's reason field contain the rationale for the redaction.

sections.extract: If present, the reason field shall contain one of these standard values, or a custom value which conforms to the same syntax as entity-specific namespacing, for the rationale behind the action: c2pa.PII.present; c2pa.invalid.data; c2pa.trade-secret.present; c2pa.government.confidential. NOTE: Although the reason field can be used for any actions, only redaction-focused c2pa values are defined at this time. When

sections.title: 16.4.1.4.3. When

summary.text: Allows an action to include a when field for the time of the action, which shall be a CBOR date/time and shall be interpreted as whenStart and whenEnd sharing the same absolute value; claim generators should use when for a single exact time. A v2 action may instead use whenStart (generator-lower-bound-time-type) and whenEnd (generator-upper-bound-time-type) as defined in Section 8.9, with whenStart not later than whenEnd when both are present, and when shall not appear together with either of them. Notes that these are claim-generator-provided timestamps and that UTC-based times should be used.

sections.extract: Also present may be the date and time when the action took place in the when field. If included, the value of the when field shall be compliant with CBOR date/times (RFC 8949, 3.4.1). Claim generators should use when for a single, exact action time. It shall be interpreted as equivalent to whenStart and whenEnd both having the same absolute value. A v2 action may instead include whenStart, whenEnd, or both.

sections.title: 16.4.1.4.4. SoftwareAgent

summary.text: Describes the softwareAgent field identifying the software or hardware that performed an action, a text string in v1 and a generator-info-map in v2. When multiple softwareAgents are used, softwareAgentIndex shall reference the agent by its 0-based index in the softwareAgents array, and an action shall have only one of softwareAgent or softwareAgentIndex. Notes that these fields help when the agent differs from the claim generator and that the earlier actors field was removed in version 2.0.

sections.extract: The software or hardware used to perform the action can be identified via the softwareAgent field. In a v1 action, this is a simple text string. However, for v2, softwareAgent uses the richer generator-info-map structure as described in Section 10.2.3.2, “Generator Info Map”. When multiple softwareAgents are used, as described in Section 16.4.1.6.2, “SoftwareAgents”, then the softwareAgentIndex field shall be used

sections.title: 16.4.1.4.5. Digital Source Type

summary.text: Allows an action to include a digitalSourceType whose value shall be an IPTC-defined term or one of the C2PA values http://c2pa.org/digitalsourcetype/empty (effectively empty content) or http://c2pa.org/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicData (model-derived data in a data format rather than a media type). Notes its common use with c2pa.created to indicate how media was created, and states that for trained algorithmic assets one or more ingredients may be added to describe the inputs and referenced from a c2pa.placed or c2pa.created action.

sections.extract: An action may include a digitalSourceType key, whose value shall be one of the terms defined by the IPTC or a C2PA specific value from the list below: http://c2pa.org/digitalsourcetype/empty Media whose digital content is effectively empty, such as a blank canvas or zero-length video. http://c2pa.org/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicData Data that is the result of algorithmically using a model derived from

sections.title: 16.4.1.4.6. Unique Identifiers for Actions

summary.text: Describes how to identify a specific action instance, either implicitly or explicitly. Recommends implicitly using the JUMBF URI of the actions assertion and, for a specific action, appending &cbor= with a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) path such as /actions/1, observing all JSON Pointer rules. Suggests a custom parameters key such as com.fabrikam.actionId for an explicit identifier.

sections.extract: Where a unique identifier for an instance of a specific action is required, it can be either determined implicitly or through explicit declaration. Implicitly, each action can be identified and its unique identifier assembled according to the following recommendation: Use the JUMBF URI of that actions assertion, which includes the unique manifest ID and a path to the actions assertion. For example:

sections.title: 16.4.1.4.7. Changes

summary.text: Explains that an action may apply to only part of an asset, such as a range of video frames or an image area; in v1 this was a text string, while in v2 it is a changes field holding an array of region-map objects from Section 16.9.2, Regions of Interest.

sections.extract: The action may be specific to only a portion of an asset - such as a range of frames in a video or a specific area on an image. In v1, the value was a simple text string. For v2, they are identified using a changes field, whose value is an array of region-map objects (as defined in Section 16.9.2, “Regions of Interest”).

sections.title: 16.4.1.4.8. Parameters

summary.text: Describes the parameters key for action-specific pre-defined and custom fields, with custom fields required to follow entity-specific namespacing, and the optional multipleInstances field, whose absence means it is unknown whether the action was repeated. Requires c2pa.opened and c2pa.placed actions to hold hashed JUMBF URIs to related ingredient assertions in ingredient (v1) or ingredients (v2), allows a c2pa.deleted action to reference a componentOf ingredient whose content it fully removes, and recommends regionOfInterest metadata when only part of an ingredient is relevant. Requires sourceLanguage and targetLanguage in c2pa.translated to be BCP 47 codes and the redacted field of c2pa.redacted to hold the JUMBF URI of the redacted assertion, and allows an optional machine-readable name field that sub-classifies the action. Gives an example c2pa.created action for a Generative AI image referencing two ingredients.

sections.extract: An action may include a parameters key that provides for the specification of some action-specific information via some pre-defined as well as the open-ended inclusion of any custom fields (and their associated values). Custom fields shall conform to the same syntax as entity-specific namespacing, e.g. com.litware.someFieldName. NOTE: This is useful for providing extra information that would be useful to a specific

sections.title: 16.4.1.4.9. Related Assertions

summary.text: Allows an action's parameters to include relatedAssertions, an array of one or more hashed JUMBF URIs to related assertions in the same C2PA Manifest. Entries shall not reference actions or ingredient assertions (c2pa.actions, c2pa.actions.v2, c2pa.ingredient, c2pa.ingredient.v2 or c2pa.ingredient.v3), and Manifest Consumers may use them to present additional context. Notes that this lets an action reference, for example, an assertion metadata assertion.

sections.extract: An action may include a relatedAssertions key in the parameters object. If present, the value shall be an array of one or more hashed JUMBF URIs identifying assertion(s) that are related to the action. Each entry in relatedAssertions shall reference an assertion in the same C2PA Manifest as the action. The related assertion(s) provide additional information about, or are otherwise related to, the action. Entries in

sections.title: 16.4.1.5. Watermarking

summary.text: Requires that a c2pa.watermarked.bound action be accompanied by a soft binding assertion describing the inserted watermark, which the action should reference through relatedAssertions in its parameters. Notes that c2pa.watermarked is deprecated in favor of c2pa.watermarked.bound and c2pa.watermarked.unbound.

sections.extract: When using a c2pa.watermarked.bound action, a soft binding assertion shall also be included in the C2PA Manifest to describe the inserted watermark. The c2pa.watermarked.bound action should reference one or more of these corresponding soft binding assertions using the relatedAssertions field in the parameters object of that action. NOTE: The c2pa.watermarked action is deprecated in favour of the more specific

sections.title: 16.4.1.6. Action Templates

summary.text: Heading that opens section 16.4.1.6 Action Templates; it carries no text of its own.

sections.title: 16.4.1.6.1. Templates

summary.text: Describes v2 action templates, which a C2PA Manifest Consumer combines with actions of the same name, or with all actions when the template's action is *, merging multiple applicable templates starting with * and then in array order. Requires the consumer to take template values and overlay the action's own values, replacing any with the same name, and illustrates this with examples and Figure 18, Actions Template Flow. Template parameters are merged key by key with the action's parameters, the action's values taking precedence, or used unchanged if the action has none. The templateParameters key is deprecated in favor of parameters, and consumers shall treat its pairs as parameters using the same precedence rules.

sections.extract: The elements of the templates array, in a v2 action, are described using a combination of common elements about actions, along with some template-specific values. These values are combined by a C2PA Manifest Consumer with actions of the same name, or with all actions (if the value of the action field is the special * value), to get a full picture of an action. If there are multiple templates that apply to the same

sections.title: 16.4.1.6.2. SoftwareAgents

summary.text: Describes the softwareAgents field, an array of generator-info-map objects that can list multiple software or hardware agents, each referenced by index through the softwareAgentIndex field of an action or template. Gives a CBOR diagnostic example of six actions referencing two agents.

sections.extract: If multiple softwareAgents were used, they can be listed in the softwareAgents field instead. This field is an array of generator-info-map objects, each of which describes a different software or hardware which can then be referenced by its index via the softwareAgentIndex field of a given action or template. Example 7. Software Agents example An example of specifying multiple agents across multiple actions, in CBOR

sections.title: 16.4.1.6.3. Icons

summary.text: Allows a template to include an icon, a raster or vector image the Manifest Consumer can use to represent the action, but requires icons to appear only in templates for entity-specific actions. The icon value, if present, shall be a hashed URI to an embedded data assertion (labelled c2pa.icon and following the multiple-instance label rules) or a cloud data assertion, matching the structure of the icon field in the Claim's Generator Info Map. Recommends that Manifest Consumers also support the data box approach from earlier versions.

sections.extract: A template may also include an icon - an image (raster or vector) that can be used in the C2PA Manifest Consumer’s user experience to provide some graphic representation of the action. Since a Manifest Consumer will know about all the defined actions, such icons shall only be present in templates for entity-specific actions. The value of the icon field, if present, shall be a hashed URI. This hashed URI shall be to

sections.title: 16.4.1.7. Localizations

summary.text: Requires that, if an actions assertion's metadata contains a localization dictionary for a template, those localizations also apply to every action based on that template.

sections.extract: If the metadata of an actions assertion contains a localization dictionary for a template, then the localizations shall also apply to any action based on that template.

sections.title: 16.4.1.8. Related Actions

summary.text: Describes the v2 related field for listing additional actions related to a primary action, usually occurring at the same time. Recommends that each related action include only the fields that differ from the primary action, with a C2PA Manifest Consumer merging the values with the primary action, as with a template, to get the full picture.

sections.extract: When a series of actions are related to each other, usually taking place at the same time, it can be useful to associate them accordingly. The related field, in the v2 action, provides a place to list the additional actions that are related. Each related action should be a subset of the primary action, only including those fields that differ. Just as with an action template, the values are merged with those of the

sections.title: 16.4.1.9. Asset Renditions

summary.text: Describes using the actions assertion to signal a claim creator's intent when creating asset renditions for different connectivity, resolution and other environments. The presence of only c2pa.published, c2pa.transcoded and c2pa.repackaged actions signals that the signer asserts no editorial changes to the digital content occurred between the ingredient(s) and this asset, and a single parentOf ingredient further signals that the asset was derived directly from that parent.

sections.extract: Asset renditions are a common occurrence when distributing media on the internet. These renditions are often created for the purpose of delivering media to consumers in differing connectivity, screen resolution, and other environments. We can use the actions assertion to help consuming actors understand the intention of certain claim creators to create asset renditions. The presence of only c2pa.published,

sections.title: 16.4.1.10. Soft Binding Lookup

summary.text: Allows a claim generator performing c2pa.opened or c2pa.placed with an asset lacking a C2PA Manifest to use a soft binding lookup to find its manifest, and recommends adding any located manifest as the ingredient assertion's activeManifest. If it does so, the ingredient assertion shall also contain softBindingsMatched set to true and a softBindingAlgorithmsMatched array with at least one entry, indicating to consumers that a lookup was used. Notes that validation failures are to be expected in the ingredient assertion because recovered manifests usually carry non-matching hard bindings, and gives a CBOR diagnostic example.

sections.extract: When performing either a c2pa.opened or c2pa.placed action with an asset that does not contain a C2PA Manifest, the claim generator may use a soft binding lookup to find the C2PA Manifest for that asset. If successful, the claim generator should add the located C2PA Manifest as the value of the activeManifest field in the ingredient assertion. If it does so, then the ingredient assertion shall also contain a

sections.title: 16.4.1.11. Removing Previous Ingredients

summary.text: Allows a claim generator to use a c2pa.deleted action when a deletion removes all the content of an ingredient previously recorded with a componentOf relationship, indicating it should no longer be considered part of the asset. If that ingredient assertion is also redacted, a c2pa.redacted action should be used as well and the c2pa.deleted action should reference the redacted ingredient assertion.

sections.extract: When a deletion includes all of the content of a given ingredient, a claim generator may use a c2pa.deleted action to indicate that the previously composed asset ingredient (recorded in a previous manifest as an ingredient assertion with a componentOf relationship) has been removed from the content, and should not be considered part of the current asset. A claim generator or user may also wish to redact that

sections.title: 16.4.1.12. Relationship Between Actions and Ingredients

summary.text: Summarises the requirements that link actions assertions, which record what happened to an asset, with ingredient assertions, which record the other assets or data involved, noting that adding one often requires a matching entry in the other and that c2pa.opened and c2pa.placed actions must reference their ingredient assertions. It gives further examples: a c2pa.created action may reference inputTo ingredients such as Generative AI inputs, and a c2pa.deleted action may reference a componentOf ingredient and should be paired with c2pa.redacted when that ingredient assertion is also redacted.

sections.extract: Actions and ingredients are closely related concepts: an actions assertion records what happened to an asset, while an ingredient assertion records the other asset(s) or data involved in that history. The requirements linking the two are described throughout this section and Section 16.5, “Ingredient”; this section summarizes them for ease of reference. In many cases, adding an ingredient to a C2PA Manifest requires

sections.title: 16.4.1.12.1. Digital Source Type

summary.text: Explains that an ingredient's digitalSourceType can be inferred from its active manifest if it has one, or otherwise carried in the ingredient assertion itself, that an ingredient assertion shall not contain both activeManifest and digitalSourceType, and that an ingredient may declare no digitalSourceType at all.

sections.extract: The digitalSourceType of an ingredient can be established in one of two ways, depending on whether the ingredient has an active manifest: If the ingredient has an active manifest, its digitalSourceType could be inferred from information provided by that manifest, as described in Section 16.4.1.4.5, “Digital Source Type”. If the ingredient does not have an active manifest, the ingredient assertion itself may carry a

sections.title: 16.4.1.13. Deprecated Actions

summary.text: Lists eight deprecated actions (c2pa.copied, c2pa.formatted, c2pa.version_updated, c2pa.printed, c2pa.managed, c2pa.produced, c2pa.saved and c2pa.removed), which shall no longer be written into c2pa.actions or c2pa.actions.v2 assertions but may appear in pre-existing manifests.

sections.extract: The following actions were part of previous versions of this specification and have since been deprecated: c2pa.copied; c2pa.formatted; c2pa.version_updated; c2pa.printed; c2pa.managed; c2pa.produced; c2pa.saved; c2pa.removed. They shall no longer be written into c2pa.actions or c2pa.actions.v2 assertions but may appear in pre-existing C2PA Manifests.

sections.title: 16.4.1.14. Schema and Example

summary.text: Gives the CDDL schemas for the actions assertions, with c2pa.actions defined by the deprecated actions-map rule and c2pa.actions.v2 by actions-map-v2, plus the generated list of predefined action names (c2pa.* and font.* actions, with a pattern allowing custom names). The v2 schema defines a required actions array and allActionsIncluded flag, optional templates, softwareAgents and metadata, and per-action fields such as softwareAgent, description, digitalSourceType, exact or ranged timing (when, or whenStart and whenEnd), changes, related, reason (required for c2pa.redacted) and parameters including redacted, ingredients, relatedAssertions, sourceLanguage, targetLanguage, name and multipleInstances. It also gives a CDDL for font-specific action parameters (Unicode ranges and variable-font instance settings such as weight, width, italic, slant and optical size) and a CBOR diagnostic example of a v2 actions assertion with a filtered and a cropped action.

sections.extract: The schema for c2pa.actions is defined by the actions-map rule, and the schema for c2pa.actions.v2 is defined by the actions-map-v2 rule in the following CDDL Definition (see Section G.5.1, “Actions” for the complete normative schema): CDDL for Action choices ; DO NOT EDIT — generated from actions.yaml ; Run generateActions.sh to regenerate. ; Structural definitions are in actions.cddl $action-choice /=

sections.title: 16.4.2. External Reference

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.4.2, External Reference; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.4.2.1. Description

summary.text: Defines the external reference assertion (label c2pa.external-reference), which points to data stored remotely, either advisory and changeable via an unhashed-ext-uri-map or cryptographically bound at signing via a hashed-ext-uri-map, in a required location field with an optional label when the target is a complete assertion; it should appear in gathered_assertions and shall not reference actions, hash, cloud-data, external-reference or ingredient assertions. Referenced data shall be treated as optional and should not be retrieved during manifest validation, unhashed retrieved data shall be treated as advisory unless independently verified, and the size field should be omitted when the referenced data may change.

sections.extract: There are use cases where storing the data for an assertion remotely, such as in the cloud, is better than embedded inside the asset, especially for those cases where that data may change over time. Additionally, it may be important to reference non-assertion-based data stored externally. To address those needs, a specific type of assertion serves as an external reference to the location of that information. An

sections.title: 16.4.2.2. Process Evidence

summary.text: States that the hashed variant of an external reference assertion may point to externally stored creation-process evidence, identified through the data_types field using the predefined values c2pa.types.audit-log and c2pa.types.version-history (or entity-specific types following namespace syntax), with processStart and processEnd in metadata describing the process where applicable.

sections.extract: The hashed variant of an external reference assertion may be used to reference externally-stored creation-process evidence. The data_types field on the hashed-ext-uri-map location identifies the kind of evidence using an asset-type-map. The following pre-defined values are available: c2pa.types.audit-log A structured log of creation-phase events collected by a local or remote observer during the creation process.

sections.title: 16.4.2.3. Schema and Example

summary.text: Gives the CDDL for the external reference assertion as two rules, external-reference-map with an unhashed location and hashed-external-reference-map with a hashed location, each also allowing optional label, description and metadata fields. It also defines the unhashed-ext-uri-map (url plus optional dc:format, size and data_types) and the hashed-ext-uri-map, which additionally requires alg and hash. CBOR diagnostic examples show unhashed references to a remote c2pa.metadata assertion, an arbitrary blob and changing JSON data, and hashed references to an audit log and a version history.

sections.extract: The schema for this type is defined by the external-reference-map and hashed-external-reference-map rules in the following CDDL Definition (see Section G.5.8, “External Reference” for the complete normative schema): ; Assertion that references assertion data stored externally by URI (no hash) external-reference-map = { ; specifies the location and type of the remote data "location": unhashed-ext-uri-map, ; label for

sections.title: 16.4.3. Linked Resource Integrity

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.4.3, Linked Resource Integrity; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.4.3.1. Description

summary.text: Defines the linked resource integrity assertion (label c2pa.linked-resource-integrity), which provides hash coverage, akin to W3C Subresource Integrity, for external resources referenced by container formats, using a resources field holding either an externalResources array of hashed absolute URLs or a relativeResources array with a shared alg; it shall appear only in created_assertions, and relative URIs shall be resolved against the asset's location, or treated as unresolvable when that location is unknown. The optional allURIsIncluded flag, when true, says every fetched or embedded reference the signer can enumerate at signing time is covered, excluding navigational links, the manifest itself and transitively discovered resources, while an absent value should be read as meaning more references may exist; validators are not required to retrieve resources, so hash checking is optional.

sections.extract: Many container formats embed URI references to external resources (for example, scripts and stylesheets in HTML, or texture files in MaterialX scenes) but provide no native mechanism to hash-bind those dependencies. A linked resource integrity assertion provides cryptographic hash coverage for such externally referenced resources, supplying the equivalent of W3C Subresource Integrity (Subresource Integrity Level 2)

sections.title: 16.4.3.2. Schema and Example

summary.text: Gives the CDDL for the linked resource integrity assertion, where linked-resource-integrity-map holds resources as either an external-resources-map or a relative-resources-map (with its own alg), plus optional allURIsIncluded and metadata. It also defines the hashed-ext-uri-map and the uri-hashed-data-map, whose relative URI type permits no scheme or authority and leaves rejection of percent-encoded traversal to validation. Two CBOR diagnostic examples show an HTML asset with two fully covered external resources and a MaterialX scene with one relative texture and partial coverage.

sections.extract: The schema for this type is defined by the linked-resource-integrity-map rule in the following CDDL Definition (see Section G.5.15, “Linked Resource Integrity” for the complete normative schema): ; One or more external resources with cryptographic hashes, used when the ; container format only supports absolute references to external resources. external-resources-map = { "externalResources": [1* $hashed-ext-uri-map],

sections.title: 16.4.4. Asset Reference

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.4.4, Asset Reference; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.4.4.1. Description

summary.text: Defines the asset reference assertion (label c2pa.asset-ref), which records via URIs one or more locations, a single asset or a directory of collection-hashed assets, where a copy of the asset may be obtained, with the metadata time stamp giving a basis for judging link freshness.

sections.extract: This assertion is used to indicate one or more locations where a copy of the asset may be obtained. Such locations shall each be described using an asset reference assertion. The location shall be expressed via a URI. The URI may be to either a single asset or it may reference a directory. In the latter case, it serves to provide the location for a collection of assets, that would be hashed via a collection data

sections.title: 16.4.4.2. Schema and Example

summary.text: Gives the CDDL for the asset reference assertion, where asset-ref-map holds a required references array whose entries pair a reference containing a uri with an optional human-readable description, plus optional metadata. A CBOR diagnostic example lists one web location and one IPFS location.

sections.extract: The schema for this type is defined by the asset-ref-map rule in the following CDDL Definition (see Section G.5.5, “Asset Reference” for the complete normative schema): ; The asset reference assertion (ARA) describes where a copy of the asset may be ; obtained. asset-ref-map = { "references": [1* ara-reference-block-map] ; additional information about the assertion ? "metadata": $assertion-metadata-map, }

sections.title: 16.4.5. Repository Receipt

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.4.5, Repository Receipt; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.4.5.1. Description

summary.text: Defines the repository receipt assertion (label c2pa.repository-receipt), which may record proof that a C2PA Manifest Repository ingested a manifest and shall appear only in an update manifest, with a body that is a JSON-LD object including @context. Its repository object shall give the repository's base uri and a canonical manifestId, and its anchor object shall give a uri where the proof can be verified and a repository-defined proof object, with optional repository-specific parameters.

sections.extract: There are use cases where a receipt may be desired in order to prove that a C2PA Manifest has been ingested by a C2PA Manifest Repository. Such use cases include providing non-repudiation of ingestion, establishing that a manifest was present in a repository at a particular time, or supporting workflows in which an external service attests to registration of the manifest. Such a receipt may be recorded via a

sections.title: 16.4.5.2. Repository Receipt Assertion Schema and Example

summary.text: Gives the JSON Schema for the repository receipt assertion payload, requiring @context, an @type fixed to org.c2pa.repository-receipt, a repository object (uri and manifestId) and an anchor object (uri and proof, with optional parameters). An example JSON object shows a receipt from a repository with an anchor URI, a view parameter and a proof value.

sections.extract: The JSON schema for the repository receipt assertion payload is defined in the following: { "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema", "$id": "https://c2pa.org/schemas/repository-receipt.json", "title": "C2PA Repository Receipt", "description": "Receipt showing that a C2PA Manifest Store was ingested by a repository and associated with an external proof of ingestion.", "type": "object",

sections.title: 16.5. Ingredient

summary.text: Introduces the ingredient assertion, which describes an asset used in creating, or otherwise related to, the asset described by the manifest, together with its relationship to that asset and a reference to its own provenance data.

sections.extract: This assertion describes an ingredient - an asset used in the creation of, or otherwise related to, the asset described by the manifest - together with its relationship to that asset and a reference to its own provenance data.

sections.title: 16.5.1. Description

summary.text: Explains that ingredients record the provenance of assets composed into, derived from or rendered from other assets, and also describe assets or data used as input to processes such as AI/ML training or inference. It names three versions of the assertion, deprecated c2pa.ingredient and c2pa.ingredient.v2 and the current c2pa.ingredient.v3, which shall be the label used and addresses validating ingredients after redaction, with the usual multiple-instance labelling applying.

sections.extract: When assets are composed together, for example placing an image into a layer in an image editing tool or an audio clip into a video in a video editing tool, it is important that information about any claim from the placed asset be recorded into the new asset to provide a way to understand the entire history of the new composed asset. This is also true when an existing asset is used to create a derived asset or asset

sections.title: 16.5.2. Establishing unique identifiers

summary.text: Specifies that an ingredient containing a C2PA Manifest takes its unique identifier from the manifest label of its active manifest, making instanceID unnecessary, while an instanceID supplied by the claim generator shall be determined as specified for non-C2PA assets, and may be supplied even when a manifest exists.

sections.extract: If the ingredient being added contains a C2PA Manifest, then its unique identifier shall be taken from the manifest label of the JUMBF superbox containing the ingredient’s active C2PA Manifest, and it is not necessary to provide the optional instanceID field of the ingredient assertion. When the claim generator provides the optional instanceID field of the ingredient assertion, then the value of the unique

sections.title: 16.5.3. Relationship

summary.text: Requires each ingredient's relationship to be described as parentOf (the asset is derived from or a rendition of it, also used with update manifests), componentOf (it is one part of a composed asset) or inputTo (it was input to a computational process such as an AI/ML model). In Standard Manifests a claim generator adding an ingredient shall ensure a c2pa.actions assertion exists and add c2pa.opened for parentOf or c2pa.placed for componentOf, and a parentOf or componentOf ingredient assertion shall be listed in the same claim field (created_assertions or gathered_assertions) as the actions assertion referring to it.

sections.extract: When adding an ingredient, its relationship to the current asset shall be described. The possible values of the relationship field and their meanings are shown in Table 6, “Ingredient Relationships”. Table 6. Ingredient Relationships Value; Meaning parentOf; The current asset is a derived asset or asset rendition of this ingredient. This relationship value is also used with update manifests. componentOf; The current

sections.title: 16.5.4. Title

summary.text: Specifies that dc:title, if present, shall be a human-readable ingredient name taken from XMP or a filesystem name, but claim generators should not set it when the information is available in the ingredient's active manifest.

sections.extract: If present, the value of dc:title shall be a human-readable name for the ingredient, which may be taken either from the asset’s XMP or the asset’s name in a local or remote (e.g., cloud-based) filesystem. However, claim generators should not set this value if the information is available in the ingredient’s active C2PA Manifest.

sections.title: 16.5.5. Format

summary.text: Specifies that dc:format, if present, shall be the ingredient's IANA media type, that claim generators should provide it with a valid value, and that multi-file ingredients such as an AI/ML data set shall use multipart/mixed.

sections.extract: If present, the value of dc:format shall be the IANA Media Type for the ingredient. It is recommended that a claim generator should provide this field and it shall contain a valid value. When describing a multi-file ingredient, such as the data set of an AI/ML model, the dc:format field shall be set to multipart/mixed.

sections.title: 16.5.6. Schema and Example

summary.text: Gives the CDDL for the ingredient assertion in its current v3 form (ingredient-map-v3) and the deprecated v2 and v1 forms, along with the format-string pattern and the relationship values parentOf, componentOf and inputTo. The v3 map requires only relationship and offers optional fields including dc:title, dc:format, validationResults, instanceID, data, dataTypes, either activeManifest or digitalSourceType but not both, relatedAssertions, claimSignature, thumbnail, description, informationalURI, softBindingsMatched, softBindingAlgorithmsMatched and metadata. A CBOR diagnostic example shows a parentOf ingredient with a thumbnail, related assertion, active manifest, claim signature and validationResults including ingredientDeltas.

sections.extract: The CDDL Definition for this type is shown below (see Section G.5.4, “Ingredient” for the complete normative schema, including all versions): ; Version 3 (v3) of the ingredient assertion ; Assertion that describes an ingredient used in the asset ingredient-map-v3 = { ? "dc:title": tstr, ; name of the ingredient ? "dc:format": format-string, ; Media Type of the ingredient ; The relationship of this ingredient to the

sections.title: 16.5.7. Description field

summary.text: Allows an ingredient to carry a free-text description field about what it is or is used for, which should be produced by the claim generator rather than contain user-provided information, user descriptions instead going in a custom assertion.

sections.extract: An ingredient may include a free-text description, in the description field, of what an the ingredient is or is used for. If present, the content of this field should be produced by the claim generator, and should not contain user-provided information. NOTE: A user-provided ingredient description can be specified using a custom assertion.

sections.title: 16.5.8. Ingredient Data

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.5.8, Ingredient Data; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.5.8.1. Standard Usage

summary.text: Explains that an ingredient's own data, important for uses such as Generative AI, can be supplied through the data field, as a hashed-uri to an embedded data assertion or a hashed-ext-uri-map to external data, and that claim generators should weigh size since embedded data is carried into future manifests unless redacted. Where data can be neither embedded nor linked, such as a private AI model, an asset type in data_types can describe it, and examples show prompt, public model and private model ingredients.

sections.extract: In certain use cases, such as Generative AI, it may be important to have ingredients where the data of the ingredient is provided - either embedded into the C2PA Manifest or via a URL that references the data. This is accomplished through the data field in the ingredient, which uses a hashed-uri to point to an embedded data assertion or a hashed-ext-uri-map to point to an external reference. NOTE: Previous versions

sections.title: 16.5.8.2. Multi-file Ingredients

summary.text: Recommends that an ingredient made of multiple files, such as an AI/ML training data set, include its C2PA Manifest in the ingredient assertion and that the data set's manifest include an asset reference assertion pointing to where the files are found.

sections.extract: In some cases, an ingredient may be represented as a set of multiple files, such as the training data set for an AI/ML model. It is recommended that in those instances that the C2PA Manifest be included in the ingredient assertion and that the C2PA Manifest for the full data set include an asset reference assertion that references where to find those files. NOTE: This method is well suited for when working with a

sections.title: 16.5.9. Informational URI

summary.text: Specifies that a URL to a web page about an ingredient, such as AI/ML model details, should go in the informationalURI field, which is not an authenticated link to the ingredient's content and was named informational_URI in deprecated versions.

sections.extract: When it is necessary to provide a URL to a web page with information about the ingredient, such as detailed information about an AI/ML model, it should be placed as the value of the informationalURI field of the ingredient assertion. NOTE: The informationalURI is not an authenticated link to the content of the ingredient itself, but something more generally of interest to a human user. NOTE: Older (and deprecated)

sections.title: 16.5.10. Thumbnails

summary.text: Specifies that a thumbnail recording an ingredient's state at import shall be added as a thumbnail assertion referenced by hashed-uri, and also added to relatedAssertions when newly created in the active manifest, while Manifest Consumers should still support the earlier data box approach.

sections.extract: When adding an ingredient, it may be useful to also include a thumbnail of the ingredient to help establish the state of the ingredient at the time of import. For that purpose, a thumbnail shall be added as a thumbnail assertion and referenced herein via a hashed-uri reference. If a new thumbnail assertion is created in the active manifest, it shall also be added to the relatedAssertions field. Manifest Consumers

sections.title: 16.5.11. Related Assertions

summary.text: Allows the claim generator to use the ingredient's relatedAssertions field, an array of hashed JUMBF URIs to non-ingredient, non-action assertions in the same manifest, to mark assertions that are about the ingredient rather than the current asset, though such assertions should appear in the ingredient's own manifest where possible. Each referenced assertion shall have a label ending in .ingredient (for example c2pa.ai-disclosure.ingredient or com.litware.metadata.ingredient) following the usual multiple-instance rules, and an example shows an inputTo ingredient referencing an AI disclosure assertion.

sections.extract: In cases where there are other assertions in the active manifest that should be understood as being about an ingredient rather than about the current asset, the claim generator may reference those assertions using the relatedAssertions field of the ingredient assertion. The value of this field shall be an array of one or more hashed JUMBF URIs, each referencing an assertion, in the same C2PA Manifest, that is

sections.title: 16.5.12. Existing manifests

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.5.12, Existing manifests; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.5.12.1. General

summary.text: Requires the claim generator to copy every validated C2PA Manifest from an ingredient's Manifest Store that is not already in the asset's store, subject to the copying rules or user or configuration direction. It should also copy unvalidated manifests and unrecognised JUMBF boxes and superboxes, to stay compatible with custom assertions and future constructs.

sections.extract: If the ingredient has an existing C2PA Manifest Store, then all C2PA Manifests in the ingredient’s C2PA Manifest Store that have undergone validation, and that do not already exist in the asset’s C2PA Manifest Store, shall be copied by the claim generator into the asset’s C2PA Manifest Store, except as outlined in Section 16.5.13, “Copying existing manifests” or when directed not to do so (for example via user input

sections.title: 16.5.13. Copying existing manifests

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.5.13, Copying existing manifests; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.5.13.1. Determining the need

summary.text: Sets out the procedure a claim generator shall follow to decide whether to copy each manifest from an ingredient's Manifest Store: validate the ingredient (optionally stopping on failure if so directed), compare manifest URNs with those already in the asset's store, and on a URN match compare manifest box hashes, not copying when they match. When hashes differ only because of redaction it keeps the existing manifest, replaces it, or redacts it to the union of both redaction sets depending on where redactions were applied, and in all other cases it copies the ingredient's manifest, re-labelled with a new URN.

sections.extract: To determine whether or not an existing manifest from the ingredient’s C2PA Manifest Store needs to be copied into the asset’s C2PA Manifest Store, the claim generator shall: 1. Validate the ingredient per the process described in Section 16.5.13.4, “Ingredient validation”. In case of validation failures, the claim generator may skip the rest of these steps if directed to do so (for example, via user input or via

sections.title: 16.5.13.2. Examples

summary.text: Gives two examples of manifest copying in which claim generator D imports ingredient B (carrying manifest A) and then ingredient C carrying a redacted manifest A, which D uses to overwrite its copy of A. In the second, the version of A from C fails validation, so D copies it under a new URN instead, with a note that non-manifest JUMBF boxes need not be copied.

sections.extract: EXAMPLE: Consider a claim generator D that is importing ingredients. It begins by importing ingredient B, which itself has an ingredient Manifest A. After validating both manifests, claim generator D copies Manifests B and A into Asset D 's C2PA Manifest Store. Then it imports ingredient C, which also includes a redacted version of Manifest A. After validating Manifest C and the redacted Manifest A, it compares the

sections.title: 16.5.13.3. Adding manifest references to the ingredient assertion

summary.text: Requires that when an ingredient's active manifest has been copied into the asset's store, hashed_uri references to its manifest box and claim signature box be stored in the ingredient assertion's activeManifest and claimSignature fields. An ingredient added without a manifest may instead carry a digitalSourceType drawn from the values allowed for actions, an ingredient assertion shall not contain both activeManifest and digitalSourceType, and an example shows a componentOf ingredient marked as trained algorithmic media.

sections.extract: If the active manifest of the ingredient has been copied into the asset’s C2PA Manifest Store, then a URI reference to the ingredient’s active C2PA Manifest box shall be stored as the value of the activeManifest field in the ingredient assertion, and an additional URI reference to the active Manifest’s C2PA Claim Signature box shall be stored as the value of claimSignature. For a C2PA Manifest present in the C2PA

sections.title: 16.5.13.4. Ingredient validation

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.5.13.4, Ingredient validation; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.5.13.4.1. General

summary.text: Requires the claim generator, when an ingredient assertion references a C2PA Manifest, to validate the ingredient and record all success, informational and failure codes in validationResults or validationStatus for use in future validations. A recorded failure is treated as an explicit statement that an actor knowingly chose to proceed despite errors, and claim generators are advised to raise warnings prominently.

sections.extract: In addition, when the ingredient assertion references a C2PA Manifest, the claim generator shall also act as a validator, performing validation of the ingredient as described in validation steps. The result of that validation - all success codes, informational codes, and failure codes - shall be used in populating the ingredient assertion’s validationResults or validationStatus field as described below. This field

sections.title: 16.5.13.4.2. V2 ingredient assertions (DEPRECATED)

summary.text: Describes validationStatus in deprecated v2 ingredient assertions, optional and possibly empty without c2pa_manifest, and otherwise an array of status-map objects each with a code, an optional success boolean, an optional explanation and a url that should point to the failing claim, signature or assertion. Custom status codes are permitted but shall follow entity-specific namespace syntax and include a success boolean.

sections.extract: In a v2 ingredient assertion with no c2pa_manifest field, the validationStatus field is optional, but if present may contain an empty array. In a v2 ingredient assertion with c2pa_manifest field, each object in the validationStatus array consists of a code field whose value describes the validation status of a specific part of the manifest along with an optional success field whose boolean value indicates whether

sections.title: 16.5.13.4.3. V3 ingredient assertions

summary.text: Requires a v3 ingredient assertion with activeManifest to carry validationResults, which may also appear without it, for example when a remote manifest could not be retrieved, and which shall hold full results for the ingredient's active manifest plus ingredientDeltas giving, for each manifest-bearing ingredient assertion in the ingredient's store, its ingredientAssertionURI and validationDeltas omitting statuses already recorded (compared on type, code and url). Each status-map shall contain a code and may contain a url and explanation, custom codes shall follow entity-specific namespace syntax, and a worked example and a manifest.inaccessible example illustrate usage. The results map may also carry a SemVer specVersion and either the deprecated trustListUri or trustListUris, whose objects shall each give the uri and type (such as c2pa.trustList or c2pa.tsaTrustList) of a trust list where a trust anchor matched, with an optional identifier that for ETSI-formatted lists shall be the list's sequence number.

sections.extract: In a v3 ingredient assertion with an activeManifest field, the validationResults field shall be present. It may also be present when an activeManifest field is not present — for example, to record that the claim generator was unable to establish the ingredient’s active manifest at all, such as a remote manifest that could not be retrieved (see Section 14.5.3.1, “By Reference”). NOTE: The ability for

sections.title: 16.5.14. Ingredient Metadata

summary.text: Explains that an ingredient assertion's metadata field may carry information such as generation time to help Manifest Consumers judge provenance. When only part of an ingredient is used, metadata should include a regionOfInterest describing the parts used, as an example with temporal and track regions shows.

sections.extract: As described in assertion metadata, the metadata field of the ingredient assertion may contain metadata about the ingredient, such as the date and time when it was generated or other data that may help Manifest Consumers to make informed decisions about the provenance or veracity of the assertion data. One common use for the metadata field is when only a portion of an ingredient is used in the creation or editing of

sections.title: 16.5.15. Soft Bindings

summary.text: Requires that when an active manifest includes as a parentOf ingredient a manifest found through a soft binding lookup, the ingredient assertion shall set softBindingsMatched to true and list in softBindingAlgorithmsMatched the algorithm names, as identified in the C2PA Soft Binding Algorithm List, used to find it.

sections.extract: An active manifest may include a C2PA Manifest as an ingredient (via a parentOf relationship) that was discovered using a soft binding lookup. If the Claim Generator does include such a C2PA Manifest, then it shall include a softBindingsMatched field indicating true, and a softBindingAlgorithmsMatched field containing an array of strings (of soft binding algorithm names that were used to discover the ingredient C2PA

sections.title: 16.6. Content Description & Enrichment

summary.text: Introduces the content description and enrichment assertions, which carry extra information about an asset or alternative representations of its content, such as thumbnails, metadata, format-specific details and externally stored data.

sections.extract: These assertions carry additional information about an asset or alternative representations of its content, such as thumbnails, metadata, format-specific details, and externally stored data.

sections.title: 16.6.1. Thumbnail

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.6.1, Thumbnail; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.6.1.1. Description

summary.text: States that a thumbnail assertion gives an approximate visual representation of the asset at a specific lifecycle event, of which there are two, ingredient import and claim creation, each with its own label; the extracted list appears garbled, splitting this into two bullets that do not each name an event.

sections.extract: A thumbnail assertion provides an approximate visual representation of the asset at a specific event in the lifecycle of an asset. There are currently two specific events: ingredient import and claim creation; each using a unique label for the assertion.

sections.title: 16.6.1.1.1. Claim Thumbnails

summary.text: Specifies that a thumbnail made at claim creation shall be labelled c2pa.thumbnail.claim, with at most one per manifest, and that the older convention of adding the media type to the label is deprecated.

sections.extract: For thumbnails created at claim creation time, the thumbnail assertion shall have the label c2pa.thumbnail.claim. There shall be no more than one thumbnail assertion with this label in a C2PA Manifest. Previous versions of this specification required that the IANA registry media type of the thumbnail be included in the label name (e.g., c2pa.thumbnail.claim.png). This naming convention has been deprecated. <a

sections.title: 16.6.1.1.2. Ingredient Thumbnails

summary.text: Specifies that importing an ingredient should reference its own manifest-stored thumbnail, or, where none exists, a new thumbnail should be generated and stored as an ingredient thumbnail assertion whose label shall start with c2pa.thumbnail.ingredient, follow multiple-instance rules, and be added to the ingredient's relatedAssertions. It notes that earlier conventions of media-type suffixes and a _1 suffix with a single underscore for the first instance are deprecated.

sections.extract: When importing an ingredient (see Section 10.3.2.2, “Adding Ingredients”), one should reference that ingredient’s own manifest-stored thumbnail. However, some ingredients may not include a thumbnail assertion, or even a manifest. In that case, a new thumbnail of the ingredient should be generated, and an ingredient thumbnail assertion created in the active manifest. An ingredient thumbnail assertion shall have a

sections.title: 16.6.1.1.3. Technical Details

summary.text: States that a thumbnail assertion is an embedded data assertion distinguished by a special label for this use.

sections.extract: A thumbnail assertion is an embedded data assertion but with a special label identifying this specific use case.

sections.title: 16.6.2. Alternative Content Representation

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.6.2, Alternative Content Representation; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.6.2.1. General

summary.text: Defines the alternative content representation assertion, which shall have the label c2pa.alternative-content-representation and refers to digital content different from the primary asset, with parameters that depend on the file format as specified in the following sections.

sections.extract: This assertion is used to refer to an alternative digital content that is different from the primary asset, and to provide functionality depending on the referenced digital content. It shall have a label of c2pa.alternative-content-representation. This assertion has the parameters depending on the file format specification. Individual specifications are specified in the following sections. <a

sections.title: 16.6.2.2. Original Preservation Image

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.6.2.2, Original Preservation Image; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.6.2.2.1. Description

summary.text: Describes using the alternative content representation assertion to reference an Exif Original Preservation Image (OPI), the unprocessed capture-time image, either where it sits in the asset's MPF, located by its index in the parts array of the multi-asset hash assertion, or moved into the manifest, as typically happens when the format changes from Exif or the file becomes an ingredient. A moved OPI shall be recorded unchanged as an embedded data assertion, edits preserving the OPI should add a new assertion, removal shall be recorded with c2pa.deleted or by redaction rules, and a manifest shall not contain more than one such assertion labelled exif.originalPreservationImage.

sections.extract: This type is used to reference "Original Preservation Image(OPI)" in Exif. The OPI is introduced for recording authenticity of the image at the time of capture in which subsequent post image processing is not applied, along with metadata that describes image properties. This enables users to recognize the difference between the image at the time of capture and the main image developed through the image processing by

sections.title: 16.6.2.2.2. Schema and Example

summary.text: The schema defines the c2pa.alternative-content-representation assertion in CDDL as either an original-preservation-image-representation (type exif.originalPreservationImage, with parameters multiAssetPartIndex or embeddedOriginalPreservationImage) or a generic-representation with a namespaced type and free-form parameters. It requires the type to be exif.originalPreservationImage and the parameters to reference the original preservation image either by its part index in an MPF asset or by a hashed URI to an embedded data assertion in the manifest, but not both, with CBOR examples of each case.

sections.title: 16.6.3. Asset Type

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.6.3, Asset Type; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.6.3.1. Description

summary.text: The asset type assertion, labelled c2pa.asset-type.v2 and limited to one per manifest, gives extra context on how to parse or process an asset beyond a single Media Type, and replaces the deprecated c2pa.asset-type assertion. Its optional dc:format field holds the IANA Media Type, and its optional types field is an array of asset-type-map entries whose type value comes from the asset type or model type tables or an entity-specific namespace, with an optional version. Table 7 lists asset type values such as c2pa.types.dataset, c2pa.types.generator and serialization formats, and Table 8 lists AI/ML model type values from c2pa.types.model.caffe to c2pa.types.model.xgboost.

sections.extract: The asset type assertion provides a way to more completely describe an asset, specifically additional context on how to parse or otherwise process it. This assertion allows for specifying an IANA Media Type value and/or additional type information, since many assets have formats that cannot be completely described by a single Media Type value. The asset type assertion shall have a label of c2pa.asset-type.v2. There

sections.title: 16.6.3.2. Schema and Example

summary.text: The CDDL defines the asset-types map, with optional dc:format, a types array of asset-type-map entries (each a type choice plus an optional SemVer version) and optional metadata. A CBOR example describes a TensorFlow 2.11.0 model stored in the SavedModel format.

sections.extract: The schema for this type is defined by the asset-types rule in the following CDDL Definition (see Section G.5.6, “Asset Type” for the complete normative schema): ; The asset type assertion provides a way to describe the type or format of an ; asset, specifically additional context on how to parse or otherwise process ; it. It can also be used to describe externally referenced or related assets ; such as AI/ML

sections.title: 16.6.3.3. Details on selection of a value for type

summary.text: When an asset's exact type is in the IANA application or text registries it should be recorded in dc:format, and an asset type assertion may combine a Dublin Core format with a C2PA standard or custom type. Table 9 lists common dc:format values such as application/json and text/csv, IANA structured suffixes like +json are also supported, and Table 10 adds two non-IANA formats, application/x-hdf5 and application/x-7z-compressed.

sections.extract: If an asset’s exact type is specified in the IANA registry application type or IANA registry text type, including JSON, CSV, and XML types, this information should be included in the asset type assertion dc:format field. For example, if the asset is a CSV formatted text file, the dc:format field would be text/csv. An asset type assertion may contain both a Dublin Core format and a C2PA standard or custom asset type

sections.title: 16.6.4. Font Information

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.6.4, Font Information; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.6.4.1. Description

summary.text: The Font Information assertion, labelled font.info with at most one per manifest, adds basic font metadata such as name, format, creator attribution and licensing so it can be validated cryptographically.

sections.extract: A Font Information assertion is used to ensure that basic font metadata, such as the name, format, creator attribution, and licensing, are added to the asset in a manner which may be validated cryptographically. A Font Information assertion shall have a label of font.info, and there shall be at most one Font Information assertion per manifest.

sections.title: 16.6.4.2. Schema and Example

summary.text: The CDDL defines font-info-map, with required fields fullName, familyName, style, weight, postScriptName (restricted to a printable ASCII pattern), format (TrueType or OpenType) and copyrightNotice, plus optional version, versionUrl, releaseDate, copyrightHolder, copyrightYears, designers, designFoundry, sourceFoundry and identifier. Supporting rules define the allowed styles, a weight map with a class name and a value from 1 to 1000, an entity map with name and URL, and a designer map with person, foundry, contribution and start and end dates. Two CBOR examples follow, a basic one and an extended one showing the optional fields.

sections.title: 16.6.5. Depthmap

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.6.5, Depthmap; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.6.5.1. Description

summary.text: A depthmap assertion gives a 3D description of a captured scene, either as a pre-computed depth map or as data such as stereo images from which one can be computed; its label shall start with c2pa.depthmap followed by a part naming the depth map type, and the depth data shall be captured optically rather than inferred from a single 2D image.

sections.extract: A depthmap assertion provides a 3D description of the scene being captured by a camera. A depthmap assertion may contain a pre-computed depth map, or data which can later be used to compute a depth map by downstream ingestion or viewing software (e.g., left/right stereo images). All depthmap assertions shall have a label that starts with c2pa.depthmap and be followed by a third section that identifies the type of

sections.title: 16.6.5.2. GDepth Depthmap

summary.text: The GDepth depthmap assertion, labelled c2pa.depthmap.GDepth, encodes a pre-computed depth map using the GDepth format, and its data schema shall always mirror the published GDepth schema, with a note that splitting data beyond 64KB is not a concern.

sections.extract: A GDepth depth map assertion leverages the well-established GDepth format to encode a pre-computed depth map. A GDepth depthmap assertion shall have a label of c2pa.depthmap.GDepth. The schema for the data stored in this assertion shall always mirror the schema at https://developers.google.com/depthmap-metadata/reference. NOTE: There are no concerns with splitting up the GDepth data when it grows beyond 64KB, as

sections.title: 16.6.5.3. Schema and Example

summary.text: The CDDL defines depthmap-gdepth-map, with GDepth fields for format (RangeInverse or RangeLinear), near and far values, MIME type and base64 depth data, plus optional units, measure type, confidence image, device manufacturer, model, software and original image width and height. A CBOR example is given, and the block states that GDepth:Format, GDepth:Near, GDepth:Far, GDepth:Mime and GDepth:Data shall be present in every GDepth assertion.

Current valid values are 'RangeInverse'

sections.title: 16.6.6. Embedded Data

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.6.6, Embedded Data; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.6.6.1. Description

summary.text: The embedded data assertion replaces the deprecated data box concept, which could not be redacted, with a standard assertion holding data in a JUMBF Embedded File box; its label shall start with c2pa.embedded-data, and some other assertions such as c2pa.thumbnail.claim are technically equivalent under their own labels.

sections.extract: In previous versions of this specification, a concept of a data box as a special type of JUMBF box was used as a way to enable the arbitrary embedding of data into a C2PA Manifest, such as for thumbnails, icons and inputTo ingredients. It was determined that doing this via a new type of box introduced unnecessary complexities and missing functionality - such as the inability to redact data boxes. Accordingly, that

sections.title: 16.6.6.2. Technical Details

summary.text: The Embedded File Description box of an embedded data assertion shall carry an IANA media type (structured suffixes allowed) and may carry a file name, shall not set the External bit, and its Binary Data box shall hold file bytes matching that media type.

sections.extract: Since the embedded data assertion is based on a JUMBF Embedded File content type box, it’s Embedded File Description box shall contain an IANA media type (e.g., image/png) as the value of the MEDIA TYPE field, and may contain a file name as the value of the FILE NAME field. It shall not have the External toggle bit set. NOTE: IANA structured suffixes

sections.title: 16.6.7. Cloud Data

summary.text: Heading that opens Section 16.6.7, Cloud Data; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: 16.6.7.1. Description

summary.text: The cloud data assertion, labelled c2pa.cloud-data, references a remotely stored C2PA assertion packaged as JUMBF (media type always application/jumbf) through a hashed URI, so the remote data must be static, and its contents shall be treated as optional and should not be fetched during manifest validation. It shall not refer to actions, hashing, ingredient or other cloud data assertions (a list of labels is given), and its size field shall give the referenced data's size while the size and dc:format fields of the hashed external URI map shall be omitted.

sections.extract: A cloud data assertion references a remotely-stored C2PA assertion packaged as JUMBF. NOTE: For other externally stored data, whether assertion or non-assertion, see the external reference assertion. For privacy and reliability reasons, data referenced through a cloud data assertion shall be considered optional: their contents should not be retrieved as part of manifest validation. A validator may retrieve the

sections.title: 16.6.7.2. Schema and Example

summary.text: The CDDL defines cloud-data-map with a label, a size of at least 1, a hashed external URI location, an optional content_type and optional metadata, followed by a CBOR example pointing to a remote c2pa.metadata assertion.
