sections.title: A.5.5. Exclusion List Requirements

summary.text: For c2pa.hash.bmff.v2 and v3 assertions, the whole C2PA 'uuid' box and the 'mfra' box shall always be excluded and 'ftyp' should not be, with earlier mandatory exclusions dropped as insecure. When both hash and merkle fields are present, an 'mdat' subset exclusion at offset 16 with length 0 shall also appear, and bytes beyond a box's end shall never be hashed.

sections.extract: For all c2pa.hash.bmff.v2 (deprecated) and c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertions, the entries in Example 20, “Always excluded boxes” shall always appear on the exclusion list. Other entries are allowed but not required. The entire 'uuid' C2PA box shall be excluded. (The 'data' field is ensuring that other 'uuid' boxes are not excluded.) Example 20. Always excluded boxes xpath = "/uuid" data = [ { offset = 8, data =

sections.title: A.5.6. Timed-media streams that are neither audio nor video

summary.text: Non-audio, non-video timed-media streams, such as caption text, that are to be made tamper evident shall be handled like audio and video streams.

sections.extract: Timed-media streams that are neither audio nor video, such as text streams for captions, that the claim generator wishes to make tamper evident shall be handled the same way as audio and video streams.

sections.title: A.5.7. External references

summary.text: Externally referenced content in BMFF boxes such as 'dref', 'url' or 'urn' that is to be tamper evident shall not have its referencing box excluded and shall have a separate cloud data assertion for each reference.

sections.extract: Externally referenced content declared inside BMFF boxes, such as in a 'dref', 'url', or 'urn' box, that the claim generator wishes to make tamper evident shall not exclude the referencing box and shall include a separate cloud data assertion for each external reference to be hashed.

sections.title: A.5.8. Size requirements

summary.text: If adding C2PA boxes pushes a BMFF file using 32-bit sizes or offsets past 4 gigabytes, the manifest creator is responsible for converting to suitable sizes and offsets, such as replacing 'stco' with 'co64', before creating the manifest.

sections.extract: If a BMFF-based asset uses 32-bit sizes or offsets in any box(es), e.g. the 'stco' box, and adding boxes to conform to this specification will push the file size over 4 gigabytes, it is the responsibility of the manifest creator to edit the file to use appropriate sizes and offsets, e.g. by replacing the 'stco' box with a 'co64' box, before creating the manifest. <a

sections.title: A.6. Embedding manifests into ZIP-based formats

summary.text: Heading that opens Section A.6, Embedding manifests into ZIP-based formats; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: A.6.1. General

summary.text: Notes that many file formats, including EPUB, Office Open XML, Open Document and OpenXPS, are ZIP archives with a specific content organisation.

sections.extract: Because of its longevity and being an openly published specification, many command file formats are really ZIP archives, but with a specific organization of the content files. This includes formats such as EPUB, Office Open XML, Open Document and OpenXPS.

sections.title: A.6.2. Hashing

summary.text: Heading that opens Section A.6.2, Hashing; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: A.6.2.1. Hashing the Entries

summary.text: ZIP-based formats shall be hashed with a collection data hash covering every entry except the manifest, each hash taken over the local file header, compressed or encrypted content and any data descriptor, using the algorithm named in alg.

sections.extract: A ZIP-based file format shall be hashed using a collection data hash, where each entry contained in the ZIP (except the C2PA Manifest itself) shall be included. The hash of each entry in the collection is computed over the entry’s local file header followed by the compressed and/or encrypted content, and any data description if present. The hash algorithm used shall be specified in the alg field of the collection

sections.title: A.6.2.2. Hashing the ZIP Central Directory

summary.text: Each central directory header and the end of central directory record shall be hashed in sequence, skipping the crc-32 field of the manifest's header, with the result stored in zip_central_directory_hash of the collection-data-hash-map, whose CDDL (uris, alg and the optional central directory hash) is given. A two-pass approach shall be used, first writing a zero-filled content_credential.c2pa and hashing the central directory, then completing and writing the manifest, and that file shall be stored uncompressed, unencrypted and with a general purpose bit flag of 0.

sections.extract: As described in 4.3.12 of the ZIP AppNote, the Central Directory is an array of central directory headers - one per entry in the ZIP archive. It is stored at the end of the ZIP archive and used to locate the entries in the ZIP archive and necessary information/metadata about them. It is immediately followed by the End of Central Directory record (ZIP AppNote, 4.3.16), which contains information about the ZIP archive

sections.title: A.6.3. Placement of the Manifest Store

summary.text: The Manifest Store shall be stored uncompressed and unencrypted as META-INF/content_credential.c2pa in the ZIP archive. In OPC packages such as Office Open XML and OpenXPS, the claim generator shall declare application/c2pa for it in [Content_Types].xml, through a Default or Override element, before computing the collection data hash.

sections.extract: The C2PA Manifest Store shall be stored in the META-INF directory of the ZIP archive with a filename of content_credential.c2pa and a media type as recommended for external manifests. The file shall be stored (compression method 0) and not encrypted. When the ZIP-based format is an Open Packaging Conventions (OPC) package, such as Office Open XML or OpenXPS, OPC requires every part of the package to have a content

sections.title: A.6.4. Digitally signing ZIP-based formats

summary.text: Heading that opens Section A.6.4, Digitally signing ZIP-based formats; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: A.6.4.1. EPUB

summary.text: Because EPUB signatures follow XML DigSig and cannot sign the ZIP Central Directory, EPUB native signing shall happen before the C2PA Manifest is added.

sections.extract: EPUB’s digital signatures are based on W3C XML DigSig Core, where each file that is signed is listed in the element of the element. In addition, no support exists for signing the ZIP Central Directory. As such, EPUB native signing shall take place before the introduction of the C2PA Manifest.

sections.title: A.6.4.2. Office Open XML

summary.text: Because OOXML signatures follow XML DigSig and cannot sign the ZIP Central Directory, OOXML native signing shall happen before the C2PA Manifest is added, and the same applies to OpenXPS.

sections.extract: OOXML’s digital signatures are based on W3C XML DigSig Core, where each file that is signed is listed as a <Reference> element in the <Manifest> element of the <Signature> element. In addition, no support exists for signing the ZIP Central Directory. As such, OOXML native signing shall take place before the introduction of the C2PA Manifest. NOTE: OpenXPS is based on the same Open Packaging Convention (OPC) standard

sections.title: A.7. Embedding Manifests into HTML

summary.text: Heading that opens Section A.7, Embedding Manifests into HTML; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: A.7.1. General

summary.text: HTML can associate a Manifest Store through an inline script element or, preferably, an external link element, both using application/c2pa in the head. There shall be at most one association per document, elements outside the head shall be ignored, and multiple manifest elements in the head shall cause the asset to be treated as having no manifests.

sections.extract: HTML supports two methods for associating a C2PA Manifest Store with a document: an embedded script element for inline manifests and a link element for referencing external manifests. Both use the IANA Media type application/c2pa. While this section describes both approaches, the use of an external manifest via the link element is preferred. There shall be at most one C2PA Manifest Store association per HTML

sections.title: A.7.1.1. Embedded (inline) manifests

summary.text: An embedded HTML manifest store must be placed, Base64-encoded, in a script element of type application/c2pa in the document head, and validators must strip surrounding whitespace before decoding, with an example document shown.

sections.extract: When embedding the C2PA Manifest Store into the HTML document, it shall be embedded as the Base64-encoded (per RFC 4648, Section 4) content of a script element with type="application/c2pa" placed in the head of the HTML document. When performing validation, the validator shall strip leading and trailing whitespace from the script element’s text content before Base64 decoding. NOTE: Browsers ignore script elements

sections.title: A.7.1.2. External (referenced) manifests

summary.text: A referenced HTML manifest store must be linked from the document head by a link element with rel="c2pa-manifest" and an href, which validators match on alone (type="application/c2pa" is recommended), and the external store must carry a content binding, with an example document shown.

sections.extract: When referencing the C2PA Manifest Store, a link element with an attribute of rel="c2pa-manifest", placed in the head of the HTML document, shall be used to reference an external C2PA Manifest Store via its href attribute. The type="application/c2pa" attribute should be included but is not required for discovery; the validator shall match on the rel attribute alone. The c2pa-manifest link relation is registered in

sections.title: A.7.1.3. Hard Binding

summary.text: A claim generator embedding a manifest store in HTML must include a c2pa.hash.data assertion, whose single exclusion range covers the whole script element when the manifest is embedded, and which has no exclusion range when the manifest is referenced by a link element. A note explains that the hash covers the stored bytes, so any re-serialisation of the HTML invalidates the binding by design, and advises embedding after final serialisation or using an external manifest.

sections.extract: A claim generator embedding a C2PA Manifest Store in an HTML document shall include a c2pa.hash.data assertion. For an embedded script element, the data hash assertion shall include a single exclusion range covering the entire element from the opening <script tag through the closing </script> tag, inclusive. The hash shall be computed over the document content with the exclusion range removed. For an external link

sections.title: A.7.1.4. Validator Behaviour

summary.text: Validators of text/html documents must parse the head as bytes for an application/c2pa script element or a c2pa-manifest link element, treat multiple matches as no manifest, and Base64-decode a script element's content. Resolving a link's external URI is optional, and any obtained manifest store is then validated through the normal validation process.

sections.extract: A validator encountering an HTML document (text/html) shall perform the following steps: 1. Treating the file as a series of bytes (vs. text), the validator shall parse the head element, searching for a script element with type="application/c2pa" or a link element with rel="c2pa-manifest". 2. If multiple matching elements are found, the document shall be treated as if no manifests were located. 3. If no matching

sections.title: A.8. Embedding Manifests into Unstructured Text

summary.text: Heading that opens Section A.8, Embedding Manifests into Unstructured Text; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: A.8.1. General

summary.text: Manifest stores may be embedded in unstructured Unicode text, such as text meant to be copied and pasted, as a sequence of non-rendering Unicode Variation Selectors, though this method should be used only when no other embedding is feasible and remains under review.

sections.extract: For unstructured text where traditional file-based embedding is not practical, such as content intended for copy-paste operations across different systems, C2PA Manifests may be embedded directly into a Unicode-encoded text stream. This method uses a sequence of Unicode Variation Selectors to encode a C2PA Manifest Store in a way that is not visually rendered, ensuring that Content Credentials persist with the

sections.title: A.8.2. The C2PATextManifestWrapper Structure

summary.text: Unstructured text assets that embed a Content Credential must do so with Unicode variation selectors following the defined C2PATextManifestWrapper syntax and semantics, chosen because they are non-rendering yet valid Unicode.

sections.extract: All unstructured text assets that wish to embed a Content Credential shall do so using Unicode variation selectors that adhere to the following syntax and semantics defined below. NOTE: Unicode variation selectors (U+FE00-U+FE0F and U+E0100-U+E01EF) are used because they are specifically designed to be visually non-rendering while remaining part of the valid Unicode character set.

sections.title: A.8.2.1. Definition

summary.text: Defines the C2PATextManifestWrapper as an optional container, encoded as Unicode Variation Selectors and present zero or one time, that holds a complete C2PA Manifest Store in JUMBF format.

sections.extract: Container Type: C2PATextManifestWrapper (contains a C2PA Manifest Store in JUMBF format) Encoding: Unicode Variation Selectors Mandatory: No Quantity: Zero or one The C2PATextManifestWrapper embeds C2PA provenance into unstructured text. One such container contains a complete C2PA Manifest Store in JUMBF format.

sections.title: A.8.2.2. Syntax

summary.text: Gives the binary syntax of C2PATextManifestWrapper: a 64-bit magic value "C2PATXT\0", an 8-bit version of 1, a 32-bit manifestLength, the JUMBF container bytes and optional trailing padding.

sections.extract: aligned(8) class C2PATextManifestWrapper { unsigned int(64) magic = 0x4332504154585400; // "C2PATXT\0" unsigned int(8) version = 1; unsigned int(32) manifestLength; unsigned int(8) jumbfContainer[manifestLength]; unsigned int(8) padding[]; // optional trailing padding bytes }

sections.title: A.8.2.3. Semantics

summary.text: Explains the wrapper's fields: the fixed magic identifier, the version (currently 1), the big-endian manifestLength, the raw JUMBF manifest store bytes, and padding bytes that carry no meaning, must be ignored when decoding and allow a deterministic wrapper length.

sections.extract: magic The identifier for C2PA text manifests, always C2PATXT\0 (0x4332504154585400). version Version of this text embedding specification (currently 1). manifestLength The length in bytes of the JUMBF container, encoded as a big-endian unsigned integer. jumbfContainer The raw bytes of the C2PA Manifest Store in JUMBF format. padding Zero or more bytes appended after the JUMBF container. These bytes carry no semantic

sections.title: A.8.3. Encoding and Decoding Algorithms

summary.text: Heading that opens Section A.8.3, Encoding and Decoding Algorithms; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: A.8.3.1. Byte-to-Variation-Selector Conversion

summary.text: Each wrapper byte must be converted to a variation selector, with bytes 0 to 15 mapping to U+FE00 onward and bytes 16 to 255 mapping to U+E0100 onward, as shown in pseudocode.

sections.extract: Each byte of the wrapped manifest shall be converted to a Unicode variation selector using the following algorithm: function byteToVariationSelector(byte b) { if (b >= 0 && b <= 15) { return U+FE00 + b; } else if (b >= 16 && b <= 255) { return U+E0100 + (b - 16); } }

sections.title: A.8.3.2. Variation-Selector-to-Byte Conversion

summary.text: Gives the pseudocode for decoding variation selectors back to bytes, inverting the two ranges U+FE00 to U+FE0F and U+E0100 to U+E01EF and returning INVALID for any other code point.

sections.extract: To decode variation selectors back to bytes: function variationSelectorToByte(codepoint vs) { if (vs >= U+FE00 && vs <= U+FE0F) { return vs - U+FE00; } else if (vs >= U+E0100 && vs <= U+E01EF) { return (vs - U+E0100) + 16; } else { return INVALID; } }

sections.title: A.8.3.3. Encoding Example

summary.text: A non-normative table shows sample bytes with their variation-selector code points and UTF-8 encodings, and shows how the magic value C2PATXT\0 encodes to eight variation selectors that a validator decodes and compares to identify a candidate wrapper.

sections.extract: The non-normative example at Table 13, “Encoding Example” illustrates the use of byteToVariationSelector for representative byte values. Each row gives the source byte, the resulting Unicode code point, and its UTF-8 encoding. Table 13. Encoding Example Byte; Code point; UTF-8 (hex) 0x00; U+FE00; EF B8 80 0x0F; U+FE0F; EF B8 8F 0x10; U+E0100; F3 A0 84 80 0xFF; U+E01EF; F3 A0 87 AF The eight-byte magic value

sections.title: A.8.4. Placement and Detection Strategy

summary.text: Heading that opens Section A.8.4, Placement and Detection Strategy; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: A.8.4.1. Placement Rules

summary.text: The wrapper must be a single contiguous, unsplit run of variation selectors immediately preceded by a U+FEFF marker, which counts as part of the wrapper for the c2pa.hash.data exclusion, and should be placed at the end of the visible text. A claim generator should embed at most one wrapper, and a validator finding more than one valid wrapper must treat the asset as having no manifests.

sections.extract: The C2PATextManifestWrapper shall be embedded according to the following rules: 1. The wrapper shall be embedded as a single, contiguous block of variation selectors. 2. The wrapper shall be immediately preceded by a single Zero-Width No-Break Space (U+FEFF), which marks the start of the wrapper for detection (see Section A.8.4.2, “Detection Algorithm”). This marker is part of the wrapper for the purpose of content

sections.title: A.8.4.2. Detection Algorithm

summary.text: Validators must scan text for U+FEFF markers, treat the following run of variation selectors as a candidate, check that its first eight decoded bytes match the C2PATXT\0 magic, then parse the rest, ignoring any candidate that fails either step.

sections.extract: A validator processing a text asset shall use the following method to identify the C2PATextManifestWrapper: 1. Scan the text from beginning to end for a Zero-Width No-Break Space (U+FEFF). 2. For each U+FEFF found, check that the subsequent contiguous sequence of Unicode Variation Selectors (U+FE00-U+FE0F, U+E0100-U+E01EF) is a potential wrapper. 3. For each potential wrapper: 1. Decode the first 8 variation

sections.title: A.8.5. Deterministic Wrapper Padding

summary.text: A note explains that a wrapper's UTF-8 length depends on how many bytes map to 3-byte versus 4-byte variation selectors, creating a circular dependency between the c2pa.hash.data exclusion length and the manifest bytes, which deterministic padding resolves by deriving the length from the manifest byte count alone.

sections.extract: NOTE: The UTF-8 byte length of a C2PATextManifestWrapper depends on the byte distribution of the encoded manifest. Bytes in the range 0x00-0x0F map to base Variation Selectors (U+FE00-U+FE0F), which encode to 3 UTF-8 bytes. Bytes in the range 0x10-0xFF map to supplementary Variation Selectors (U+E0100-U+E01EF), which encode to 4 UTF-8 bytes. Because the c2pa.hash.data exclusion must specify the wrapper’s byte range,

sections.title: A.8.5.1. Worst-Case Encoding Formula

summary.text: Defines the deterministic target wrapper byte length for an M-byte manifest as 3 + (13 + M) * 4 + 6, covering the U+FEFF prefix, the 13-byte header, the worst case of 4 bytes per selector, and a margin of 6. Notes explain that the margin guarantees the gap to the actual length can always be expressed as a combination of 3s and 4s, aided by the low-range bytes always present in the header.

sections.extract: For a manifest of M bytes, the deterministic target wrapper byte length is: HEADER_SIZE = 8 + 1 + 4 // magic + version + manifestLength (13) E_target = 3 + (HEADER_SIZE + M) * 4 + 6 Where: 3 = UTF-8 byte length of the ZWNBSP prefix (U+FEFF) HEADER_SIZE = 8 (magic) + 1 (version) + 4 (manifestLength) = 13 bytes 4 = maximum UTF-8 byte length per Variation Selector character 6 = padding margin to guarantee the gap

sections.title: A.8.5.2. Claim Generator Procedure

summary.text: A claim generator should build the manifest store with a placeholder exclusion_length, compute the target length E, rebuild with exclusion_length set to E (repeating once if the CBOR integer width changes), and encode the wrapper. It then fills the gap between E and the actual length with a fixed number of 0x00 and 0x10 padding bytes, so that compliant generators produce byte-identical wrappers.

sections.extract: A claim generator embedding a C2PATextManifestWrapper should use the following procedure to produce a deterministic exclusion length: 1. Build the C2PA Manifest Store with exclusion_length set to 0 (placeholder). 2. Compute E = 3 + (HEADER_SIZE + M) * 4 + 6, where M is the manifest byte count and HEADER_SIZE is 13. 3. Rebuild the Manifest Store with exclusion_length = E in the c2pa.hash.data assertion. 4. If the

sections.title: A.8.6. Validation Requirements

summary.text: Heading that opens Section A.8.6, Validation Requirements; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: A.8.6.1. Validating a data hash

summary.text: When validating c2pa.hash.data on unstructured text, the exclusions must match the wrapper's location, and the hash must be computed by removing the excluded bytes, normalising the rest to NFC and encoding as UTF-8, then must match the assertion's hash.

sections.extract: To validate a c2pa.hash.data assertion against unstructured text, a validator shall perform the standard checks for a data hash, with the following considerations: 1. The exclusions field in the assertion shall correspond to the location of the C2PATextManifestWrapper in the text. 2. The hash shall be computed by first removing the bytes specified by the exclusions field, then normalizing the remaining text to NFC

sections.title: A.8.6.2. Normalization

summary.text: Producers and consumers must normalise text to Unicode NFC before hashing so that hash values are consistent across platforms.

sections.extract: Both producers and consumers shall normalize text to Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC) before calculating hashes (see UAX #15). This ensures consistent hash values across different platforms that may store text in different normalization forms.

sections.title: A.8.6.3. Exclusion Handling

summary.text: The c2pa.hash.data exclusions use byte offsets into the stored UTF-8 text before NFC normalisation, and implementations must compute byte (not character) offsets against the stored text and ensure the exclusion covers the whole wrapper, including the U+FEFF marker and any padding.

sections.extract: The exclusions field in the c2pa.hash.data assertion uses byte offsets in the UTF-8 encoded text as stored, before NFC normalization is applied. Normalization is performed on the text that remains after the excluded bytes have been removed, as specified in Section 14.12.1.3.1, “Validating a text data hash”. Implementations shall be careful to: 1. Calculate offsets against the text as stored, not against its

sections.title: A.9. Embedding Manifests into Structured Text

summary.text: Heading that opens Section A.9, Embedding Manifests into Structured Text; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: A.9.1. General

summary.text: Structured text formats with comment syntax, such as source code, configuration files and markup, can carry a manifest store, either referenced or embedded, in a block delimited by fixed ASCII armour-style delimiters, which unlike the variation-selector method stays human-readable and needs no special Unicode support. Format-specific mechanisms should be preferred where available, and structured text inside a container format should have its manifest store embedded in the container.

sections.extract: Structured text formats that support comment syntax — including source code, configuration files (YAML, TOML, INI), markup (Markdown, AsciiDoc, LaTeX), and similar formats — allow human-readable annotations without altering the interpreted content. This section defines a method for associating a C2PA Manifest Store with such formats using a clearly delimited block with fixed ASCII armour-style delimiters (modelled

sections.title: A.9.2. Applicability

summary.text: The method applies to text/* files without their own embedding section, and to other plain-text formats with comment syntax, while HTML, SVG and TTML are excluded, and other XML formats may use XML comments. It must not be used for binary formats, formats lacking both comments and front matter such as CSV, or append-only files like logs and JSONL, which use the separate checkpoint method.

sections.extract: The structured text embedding method is applicable to any file with a media type of text/ that is not already covered by a format-specific embedding section in this specification. It also applies to formats whose media type is not text/ but whose content is plain text with a defined comment syntax (e.g., Postscript, YAML, etc.) The following text/* subtypes are excluded because they have their own embedding methods:

sections.title: A.9.3. Guidance for JSON-Based Formats

summary.text: JSON-based formats lack comments and front matter, so they cannot use the structured text manifest block, but individual formats may define their own extension point, for example a root c2pa_credential member holding a manifest URI or a data: URI. The specification does not reserve c2pa_credential for all JSON, notes that strict schemas may reject it, and gives two example documents.

sections.extract: JSON-based formats (RFC 8259) do not have a general comment syntax or front matter convention, so they are not candidates for the structured text manifest block defined in this section. Individual JSON-based formats can define their own extension point for associating a C2PA Manifest Store with an asset. For example, a format that permits additional root object members could define a c2pa_credential member whose

sections.title: A.9.4. Manifest Block Format

summary.text: A manifest block must go inside an existing front matter section, or otherwise be a single comment line, a claim generator must not add front matter where none exists, and the block is delimited by -----BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST----- and -----END C2PA MANIFEST-----. At most one manifest block is allowed per file, and a validator finding more must treat the asset as having no manifests, while append-only checkpoint lines are handled separately.

sections.extract: Where a file already contains a front matter section, the C2PA Manifest block shall appear inside it. For formats without front matter, or for files that lack a front matter section, the manifest block shall be expressed as a single comment line where the format supports comments. A claim generator shall not introduce a front matter section into a file that does not have one. In either case, the manifest block is

sections.title: A.9.4.1. Single-Line Form (Comments)

summary.text: In the single-line form the manifest block is one comment line with the host's comment prefix and suffix around the fixed delimiters and a manifest reference, which is preferably a URI or else a Base64 data: URI. The block is strongly recommended to sit at the start of the file but must go at the end when the first line is reserved (such as a shebang or XML declaration), sits after the header in formats like WebVTT, and should use preservation-hint comment conventions where available.

sections.extract: For formats with single-line or block comment syntax, the manifest block is expressed as a single comment line: <commentPrefix> -----BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST----- <manifest-reference> -----END C2PA MANIFEST----- <commentSuffix> Where: <commentPrefix> is the host format’s comment introducer (e.g., #, //, --, ;, %, /*, \<!--, NOTE) -----BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST----- and -----END C2PA MANIFEST----- are the fixed delimiters

sections.title: A.9.4.2. Multi-Line Form (Front Matter)

summary.text: Formats with front matter, such as YAML or TOML front matter, place a multi-line manifest block inside it, with the BEGIN and END C2PA MANIFEST delimiters each on its own line and the manifest reference between them, the host's front matter delimiters not being part of the block.

sections.extract: Formats that support front matter blocks — such as CommonMark (YAML front matter), TOML front matter (+), and similar conventions — use a multi-line manifest block within the front matter when the file has one. Front matter is more reliably preserved by format-specific toolchains than comments. -----BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST----- <manifest-reference> -----END C2PA MANIFEST----- The delimiters shall each appear on their

Front matter delimiters are not excluded, line terminators must be LF or CRLF (bare CR files must be converted first), and the generator must not change line endings outside the block.

Files shall be read in binary mode to preserve the exact byte representation of line terminators. For the single-line form, the manifest block is the single comment line containing the delimiters. sections.title: A.10. Embedding manifests into WARC files

summary.text: Heading that opens Section A.10, Embedding manifests into WARC files; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

sections.title: A.10.1. General

summary.text: Defines how to embed a C2PA Manifest Store in WARC files (application/warc), the archive format of concatenated capture records, applying to WARC 1.1 and optionally WARC 1.0. Notes say this in-band provenance complements existing fixity practices and contrast its signing model with WACZ, PREMIS and BagIt.

sections.extract: The Web ARChive (WARC) format (ISO 28500:2017) is used by national libraries, legal deposit systems, and digital preservation institutions to archive web content. A WARC file is a sequential concatenation of records, each containing a captured resource (such as an HTTP response) along with metadata about the capture. The format supports incremental appending of new records. NOTE: This section applies to WARC 1.1

sections.title: A.10.2. Placement of the Manifest Store

summary.text: The manifest store must be the block of a dedicated WARC record with WARC-Type c2pa-provenance, Content-Type application/c2pa, the manifest creation time and its length, without a WARC-Target-URI, and validators identify it by those two type values. That record must be the last in the file and the only one of its kind, and updates must remove it and append a replacement, leaving other records' bytes and hashes unchanged.

sections.extract: The C2PA Manifest Store shall be stored as the block of a WARC record of a dedicated record type with the following header fields: WARC-Type: c2pa-provenance Content-Type: application/c2pa WARC-Date: the time at which the manifest was created Content-Length: the byte length of the C2PA Manifest Store The remaining required and optional header fields (including WARC-Record-ID) shall conform to ISO 28500:2017. The

sections.title: A.10.3. Hashing

summary.text: A WARC file must be hashed with a collection data hash covering every record except the manifest record, each hashed over its full uncompressed bytes including headers, and each entry's uri must be the record's WARC-Record-ID, which generators must check is unique. Continuation records are hashed individually and revisit records as they appear, without dereferencing.

sections.extract: A WARC file shall be hashed using a collection data hash. Every WARC record in the file other than the C2PA manifest record shall be included as a member of the collection. The hash algorithm used shall be specified in the alg field of the collection data hash structure. The hash of each record shall be computed over the uncompressed bytes of that record, from the first byte of the version line through and including

sections.title: A.10.4. Update manifests and compressed manifests

summary.text: The WARC manifest record may contain update manifests and compressed manifests, and an update is added by removing and re-appending the manifest record, leaving the existing collection data hash binding valid since update manifests carry no content binding. Because records are identified by WARC-Record-ID rather than offset, the manifest record's offset and length may change, and manifest compression is independent of WARC record compression.

sections.extract: The block of the C2PA manifest record is a C2PA Manifest Store, so it may contain update manifests, and any manifest it contains may be a compressed manifest. An update manifest is added to a WARC file by the update procedure in Section A.10.2, “Placement of the Manifest Store”: the existing C2PA manifest record is removed and the replacement, containing the update manifest, is appended as the new last record.

sections.title: A.10.5. Compressed WARC files

summary.text: Because record hashes are computed over uncompressed bytes, records may be stored uncompressed or recompressed under per-record gzip, whole-file gzip or WARC-zstd without invalidating the collection data hash.

sections.extract: WARC files are commonly stored with per-record gzip compression, and other schemes such as WARC-zstd are also in use. Because each record’s hash is computed over its uncompressed bytes (see Section A.10.3, “Hashing”), the compression scheme does not affect the collection data hash. A record may be stored uncompressed, per-record compressed, or recompressed under a different scheme without invalidating its hash,

sections.title: A.10.6. Concatenation and splitting

summary.text: When WARC files are concatenated or split, a claim generator must remove pre-existing manifest records and append a new one covering all remaining records, optionally citing the earlier manifests as ingredients, since any change to record content or the record set requires a new manifest store.

sections.extract: When WARC files are concatenated or split, the collection data hash of a pre-existing C2PA Manifest Store will no longer cover the correct set of records. A claim generator producing a combined WARC file shall remove any pre-existing C2PA manifest records from constituent files and append a new C2PA manifest record covering all other records in the resulting file. The pre-existing manifests may be referenced as

These are recommendations, not mandates, and are expected to evolve; see the UX

Level 2: A summary of C2PA data available for a given asset. This level should provide enough information for the particular content, user, and

sections.title: B.3. Threats and Security Considerations

summary.text: Introduces the threats and security considerations section, stating that information security and privacy are principal concerns of C2PA and that this section is a non-normative summary, with the threat model, implementer considerations and best practices maintained in a separate Security Considerations document.

sections.extract: Information security and privacy are principal concerns of C2PA. This section is a non-normative summary; the threat modelling process, the resulting threat model, security considerations for implementers, and related best practices are maintained separately at Security Considerations.

sections.title: B.3.1. Resource exhaustion when hashing compressed members

summary.text: Explains that when a hard binding is computed over the uncompressed bytes of a compressed member, a highly compressed member can make validation consume unbounded memory or time, for example with per-record compressed WARC files. Before evaluating the signature, a validator shall enforce an implementation-defined maximum decompressed member size and shall reject any member whose decompressed length disagrees with the length declared in its own metadata, checks a note says exist for adversarial input so that hashing uncompressed bytes stays safe.

sections.extract: Where a hard binding is computed over the uncompressed bytes of a compressed asset member, a validator shall decompress attacker-supplied data before it can decide whether the asset is trustworthy. A member stored with a high compression ratio can expand to a size far larger than its stored form, so a small input can be made to consume unbounded memory or time during validation. This applies to any format whose

sections.title: B.3.2. Unicode security in text fields

summary.text: Notes that manifest text fields shown to users or compared programmatically, such as dc:title, description, claim generator identifiers and action reason values, are open to Unicode-based attacks that can mislead users or undermine provenance integrity.

sections.extract: C2PA Manifests contain text string fields that are displayed to users or compared programmatically, including dc:title, description, claim generator identifiers, and action reason values. These fields are susceptible to Unicode-based attacks that can mislead users or undermine provenance integrity.

sections.title: B.3.2.1. Bidirectional overrides

summary.text: Claim generators shall not include bidirectional override characters (U+202A to U+202E) in text fields, since they can reorder displayed text as in the Trojan Source attack, though bidirectional isolate characters (U+2066 to U+2069) are permitted in mixed-direction text.

sections.extract: Bidirectional override characters (U+202A through U+202E) can reorder displayed text to misrepresent field content, as demonstrated by the Trojan Source attack (CVE-2021-42574). Claim generators shall not include bidirectional override characters in text fields. Bidirectional isolate characters (U+2066 through U+2069) are permitted in fields containing mixed-direction text.

sections.title: B.3.2.2. Confusable characters

summary.text: Manifest consumers that display identity-bearing fields such as the claim generator name, dc:title or signer identity should apply confusable detection per Unicode Technical Standard #39, because look-alike characters from other scripts can impersonate legitimate identifiers.

sections.extract: Confusable characters from different scripts can impersonate legitimate identifiers. For example, Cyrillic "а" (U+0430) is visually indistinguishable from Latin "a" (U+0061) in most fonts. Manifest consumers that display identity-bearing fields (claim generator name, dc:title, signer identity) should apply confusable detection as defined in Unicode Technical Standard #39 before presenting these values to users. <a

sections.title: B.3.2.3. Normalization

summary.text: Claim generators should produce text string fields in Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC), since inconsistent normalization can give semantically identical text different hash values and disrupt search, comparison and deduplication.

sections.extract: Text fields that are not in a consistent Unicode normalization form can produce different hash values for semantically identical content, affecting search, comparison, and deduplication. Claim generators should produce text string fields in Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC), consistent with Character Model for the World Wide Web: String Matching.

sections.title: B.3.2.4. Adversarial control characters

summary.text: Claim generators shall not include tag characters, C1 control characters, interlinear annotation characters, or variation selector sequences on non-varying base characters in text fields, as these have no legitimate use there.

sections.extract: The following character categories have no legitimate use in C2PA text fields: tag characters (U+E0001 through U+E007F), C1 control characters (U+0080 through U+009F), interlinear annotation characters (U+FFF9 through U+FFFB), and sequences of variation selectors applied to non-varying base characters. Claim generators shall not include these characters in text fields. <a

sections.title: B.3.3. Retrieval of externally referenced data

summary.text: Explains that cloud data assertions, hashed external references and linked resource integrity assertions carry author-chosen URIs, so a validator resolving them makes requests to destinations picked by a potentially adversarial party. Without countermeasures this risks server-side request forgery (including via redirects or changing DNS answers), credential leakage, connection downgrade, resource exhaustion, and false hash mismatches, with countermeasures referred to Section 14.10.5.3, Retrieval Security.

sections.extract: Cloud data assertions, hashed external references, and linked resource integrity assertions contain URIs that are chosen by the author of a C2PA Manifest rather than by the operator of the validator. A validator that chooses to resolve these URIs therefore makes network requests to destinations selected by a potentially adversarial party. sections.extract: This version introduces new asset format support, new assertions, and a new JSON-based serialization for Content Credentials, alongside clarifications and improvements to actions, ingredients, live video, and cryptography. New Content Credential JSON (crJSON) Format Introduced a new JSON-LD serialization of a C2PA Manifest Store (called crJSON) for use in profile evaluation, interoperability testing, and validation

sections.title: F.3. 2.3 - December 2025

summary.text: Summarizes version 2.3 (December 2025) as focused on wider asset type support, better validation and refined assertions and actions, including live video streaming, unstructured text, OGG Vorbis, AVIX and Exif original preservation image embedding. It also lists a revised Cloud Data Assertion and a new External Reference Assertion, declaring the specification version and trust list used, new and gathered actions with deprecation of old action and ingredient versions, exclusion ranges for box hashing, content binding and validation clarifications, and deprecation of box hashing for TIFF.

sections.extract: This version introduces several new features and enhancements to the C2PA Specification, focusing on expanding support for various asset types, improving validation processes, and refining existing assertions and actions. Key highlights include: Support for Live Video Streaming Introduced specifications for live video streaming support. Embedding Enhancements Added comprehensive support for embedding C2PA manifests

sections.title: F.4. 2.2 - May 2025

summary.text: Summarizes version 2.2 (May 2025) as clarifying 2.1 features and addressing implementer requests. It lists the Soft Binding Resolution API, soft binding manifest recovery fields in ingredients, multi-part assets, time stamps and revocation information in update manifests replacing time-stamp manifests, the c2pa-kp-claimSigning EKU and its use with the C2PA Trust List, new digitalSourceType URIs, embedded data assertions replacing data boxes, and various clarifications to hard bindings, redaction, terminology and validation.

sections.extract: This version focuses on both technical and editorial changes to the specification to clarify some of the new features of 2.1, while addressing requests from implementers. The specification has been updated to reflect the latest best practices in the field. Added new supplementary specifications for the Soft Binding Resolution API Added new fields to the ingredient assertion to indicate soft-binding manifest recovery

sections.title: F.5. 2.1 - September 2024

summary.text: Summarizes version 2.1 (September 2024) as improving the security and reliability of Content Credentials, saying all publicly disclosed vulnerabilities were addressed. It lists definitions of well-formed, valid and trusted manifests and valid assets, deprecation and versioning processes, the c2pa URN namespace, the ingredients v3 and c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertions, time-stamp manifests and sigTst2 with a TSA trust list, detailed validation requirements and new status codes, hashing improvements, a separate embedding annex with JPEG-XL, action assertion changes, and editorial work towards ISO standardization.

sections.extract: This version focuses on both technical and editorial changes to the specification for the purposes of improving the security and reliability of Content Credentials. All publicly disclosed security vulnerabilities have been addressed, and the specification has been updated to reflect the latest best practices in the field. Clear definitions of Manifest & Asset states Well-formed Manifests Valid Manifests Trusted

sections.title: F.6. 2.0 - January 2024

summary.text: Summarizes version 2.0 (January 2024) as shifting trust decisions away from identifying humans or organizations toward hardware and software identified by X.509 certificates, adding a default C2PA Trust List and allowing only X.509 certificates for signing. It lists the well-formed and valid manifest concepts, the reworked c2pa.metadata approach replacing the Exif, IPTC and Schema.org assertions, removal of W3C Verifiable Credentials, actors, training and data mining and endorsement assertions, a v2 claim with created_assertions and gathered_assertions and a single claim generator, and other changes such as removing c2pa.hash.bmff and adding c2pa.watermarked.

sections.extract: This version represents a significant departure from previous versions. It reduces reliance on the term "actor" within the trust and validation model, shifting the basis for trust decisions away from identifying individual humans or organisations and toward the hardware and software components identified by X.509 certificates. In addition to validator-configured trust lists, it also introduces a new default trust

sections.title: F.7. 1.4 - November 2023

summary.text: Lists the version 1.4 (November 2023) changes, including ZIP-based format embedding, compressed manifests in a brob box, collection hashing, text regions of interest, the c2pa.metadata assertion, TIFF, font and PDF object-level embedding, and signing and box hashing clarifications.

sections.extract: Added support for embedding a C2PA Manifest into a ZIP-based format (e.g., EPUB, OOXML, ODF, OpenXPS) Manifests can now be compressed into a special brob box. Added support for multiple file, aka collection, hashing Added new regions of interest for text-based formats (e.g., PDF, Office, EPUB, etc.) Added new c2pa.metadata assertion to support Exif, IPTC, Schema.org and XMP Major revision to TIFF embedding support

sections.title: F.8. 1.3 - April 2023

summary.text: Lists the version 1.3 (April 2023) changes, including v2 actions and ingredient assertions, asset reference and asset type assertions, data boxes, general box hashing, regions of interest, the digitalSourceType field and the document signing EKU fallback. It also notes support for formats such as MPF, WebP, AIFF, AVI and GIF, the RFC 9360 COSE header update, deprecation of v1 BMFF hashing, and clarifications on JUMBF, intermediate certificates and the indefinite validity of time-stamps.

sections.extract: New v2 version of the actions assertion with support for many new options New v2 version of the ingredient assertion with support for embedded data New asset reference & asset type assertions New data boxes, for storing arbitrary data inside the Manifest New general box hash methodology for a more inclusive byte range hashing New "Regions of Interest" data structures that can be applied to various assertions Added

sections.title: F.9. 1.2 - October 2022

summary.text: Lists the version 1.2 (October 2022) changes: DNG and TIFF embedding, a digitalSourceType field for actions, renaming stds.iptc.photometadata to stds.iptc, and clarified assertion versioning for optional fields.

sections.extract: Added details about how to embed a C2PA Manifest in DNG or TIFF Added new digitalSourceType field to Actions Changed stds.iptc.photometadata → stds.iptc to support IPTC video metadata Clarified versioning of assertions when adding optional fields

sections.title: F.10. 1.1 - September 2022

summary.text: Lists the version 1.1 (September 2022) changes, including salted box hashing, the c2pa.hash.bmff.v2 assertion, claim_generator_info replacing claim_generator_hints, an Endorsements assertion, c2pa-prefixed status codes, W3C VC redaction, EKU validation, and schema, figure and reference updates.

sections.extract: Define a mechanism to support salting box hashing New c2pa.hash.bmff.v2 assertion, with changes to hashing model, to improve security Enable assertion metadata for the Claim Replaced claim_generator_hints with claim_generator_info Added a new assertion to support the concept of Endorsements Improvements to the c2pa.actions assertion All Error & Status Codes are now prefixed with c2pa Define mechanism for redaction

sections.title: F.11. 1.0 - December 2021

summary.text: Records version 1.0 (December 2021) as the initial release.

sections.title: G.4.2. BMFF Hash

summary.text: Gives the CDDL for bmff-hash-map, which holds required exclusions, an optional alg, an optional hash whose coverage depends on whether the MP4 is non-fragmented, Merkle-validated fragmented or a live segment, optional merkle rows, name, deprecated url and a live-workflow sequenceNumber. Each exclusions-map identifies boxes by a constrained xpath and can narrow the match by length, data at offsets, version, 3-byte flags and exact matching, or exclude only subset ranges within a box. Each merkle-map carries uniqueId, localId, leaf count, optional alg, an initHash whose presence depends on the MP4 layout, a row of hashes, and optional fixedBlockSize or variableBlockSizes for piecewise validation of non-fragmented mdat boxes.

sections.title: G.4.3. BMFF Merkle Hash

summary.text: The CDDL defines bmff-merkle-map, which holds enough information to validate a single 'mdat' box, or part of one, when a Merkle tree is used, with uniqueId and localId fields identifying the tree and a zero-based location index into its leaf-most row. An optional ordered hashes array gives the extra hashes needed to climb from the leaf to the tree row held in the manifest; it may be absent, excludes null hashes, and uses the alg from the matching merkle entry in the BMFF hash structure.

sections.title: G.4.7. Segment Hash

summary.text: The CDDL defines segment-hash-map, a segment hash assertion for append-only plain-text files that binds a signed checkpoint manifest byte-exactly to its covered segment, with version fixed at 1, an optional alg resolved as in other hash structures, the hash of bytes from segmentStart to segmentEnd, an optional sentinelLength (present only when the sentinel references an external URI) and optional metadata. Every checkpoint after the first must carry predecessorSentinel, whose start, length and hash fields must all appear together and authenticate the immediately preceding sentinel line, so that earlier sentinels cannot be rewritten without breaking the chain.

sections.title: G.5.1. Actions

summary.text: The CDDL defines version 2 of the actions assertion, actions-map-v2, with a required actions list and allActionsIncluded flag (previously optional) plus optional templates, softwareAgents and metadata, and it lists reason values such as c2pa.PII.present and c2pa.trade-secret.present. Each action item names the action, may carry a software agent or index, description and digitalSourceType, either an exact when time or a whenStart/whenEnd range (mutually exclusive), changed regions, related actions, and parameters such as redacted, ingredients, relatedAssertions, source and target languages for translation, name and multipleInstances, with reason and redacted required for c2pa.redacted. Action templates may use the "*" wildcard, an icon and parameters, with the older templateParameters deprecated and to be merged as if it were parameters, and the block also gives the deprecated version 1 actions-map, whose items use a string softwareAgent, a semicolon-delimited changed field, instanceID and a single ingredient parameter.

sections.title: G.5.10. Regions of Interest

summary.text: The CDDL defines region-map, which describes a region of interest through one or more ranges together with optional name, identifier, type, description and metadata fields, and a role field that is marked deprecated. Each range has a type of spatial, temporal, frame, textual or identified, with matching shape, time, frame, text or item details, where a shape is a rectangle, circle or polygon measured in pixels or percent from an origin, with an optional inside flag. Times are either NPT or wall-clock (start inclusive, end exclusive unless endInclusivity says inclusive), frames cover video frames or document pages, text ranges use fragment-based selectors modelled on W3C Web Annotation, and identified ranges pair a container-specific identifier such as track_id with a value.

summary.text: The CDDL enumerates the deprecated $role-choice values for regions of interest. They include c2pa.areaOfInterest, c2pa.cropped, c2pa.edited, c2pa.placed, c2pa.redacted, c2pa.subjectArea, c2pa.deleted and c2pa.styled, plus c2pa.watermarked and c2pa.watermarked.bound for soft binding and c2pa.watermarked.unbound for watermarking without one.

sections.title: G.5.12. Soft Binding

summary.text: The CDDL defines soft-binding-map, which stores one or more soft bindings over some or all of an asset's content, with an alg (resolved from the enclosing alg_soft if absent, invalid if neither is set), a blocks array, and optional pad fields, name, alg-params, bindingMetadata, a deprecated url and metadata. Each block pairs an algorithm-specific value with a scope given by a deprecated extent, a millisecond timespan or a region of interest, and the binding metadata may include a description, contact, informationalUrl and custom fields.

The content profile can declare a humanOversightLevel of fully_autonomous, prompt_guided or human_validated to tell validators how much human involvement there was, and further fields such as modelFrontier and harmEvaluation are noted as pending future specification.

summary.text: The CDDL defines linked-resource-integrity-map, whose resources are either externalResources (hashed external URIs, for formats that only support absolute references) or relativeResources with an alg (for formats supporting references relative to the asset). An optional allURIsIncluded flag says whether every URI embedded in the container is covered, and optional metadata may be added.

sections.title: G.5.16. Depth Map (GDepth)

summary.text: The CDDL defines depthmap-gdepth-map, an assertion holding a GDepth-format 3D depth map of the captured scene, which requires GDepth:Format (RangeInverse by default, or RangeLinear), GDepth:Near, GDepth:Far, GDepth:Mime and base64 GDepth:Data. Optional fields cover units (m or mm), measurement type (OpticalAxis or OpticRay), a confidence image and its type, the device manufacturer, model and software, and the original colour image's width and height, which apps must update when scaling, cropping or rotating that image.

summary.text: The CDDL defines the alternative content representation, a reference to another version of the content that is either an original preservation image or a generic representation with a label-style type and free-form parameters. The original preservation image form, typed exif.originalPreservationImage, can locate the image by a zero-based multiAssetPartIndex into a c2pa.hash.multi-asset assertion or by a hashed URI to an embedded data assertion or equivalent.

sections.title: G.5.18. Font Information

summary.text: The CDDL defines font-info-map, the data for the font.info assertion, which requires fullName, familyName, style, weight (a class name and a 1 to 1000 value), a constrained postScriptName, format (TrueType or OpenType) and copyrightNotice. Optional fields include version, versionUrl, releaseDate, copyrightHolder, copyrightYears, designers (each with person, foundry, contribution and start and end dates), designFoundry, sourceFoundry, identifier and metadata, and the allowed styles are Normal, Italic, Oblique, Roman and Regular.

sections.title: G.6.1. Certificate Status

summary.text: The CDDL defines certificate-status-map as a required array of one or more ocspVals byte strings.

sections.title: G.6.2. Session Keys

summary.text: The CDDL defines session-keys-data, which supplies one or more session keys for live-media validation, each with a COSE key used to sign verifiable segment info, a minimum sequence number, a createdAt time, a validity period in seconds and a signerBinding signature of the signer's end-entity certificate made with that key.

sections.title: G.6.3. Time Stamp

summary.text: The CDDL defines the time stamp map, which maps manifest URNs of the form urn:c2pa:... to time stamp byte strings.

sections.extract: ; The data structures used to store an array of ; manifest URNs to time stamp "blobs" $time-stamp-map /= { $time-stamp-entry => bstr } $time-stamp-entry /= tstr .regexp "^urn:c2pa:[\da-zA-Z_-]+$"

sections.title: G.6.4. Revocation Values (rVals)

summary.text: The CDDL defines rVals as an array of one or more ocspVals byte strings, and a note explains it is a CBOR adaptation of part of the JAdES schema that stores only OCSP responses, as binary strings.

sections.extract: ; CBOR version of rVals and related structures based on JSON schema in ; https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/119100_119199/11918201/01.01.01_60/ts_11918201v010101p.pdf ; section 5.3.5.2 rVals = { "ocspVals": [1* bstr] } NOTE: This definition is a CBOR adaptation of a subset of the schema from JAdES, section 5.3.5.2, which only stores OCSP responses, and stores them as binary strings.

sections.title: Appendix H: Deprecated Constructs

summary.text: The annex introduction says it records constructs deprecated in the specification, which claim generators shall not use but validators should still accept for backwards compatibility.

sections.extract: This annex provides historical information about constructs that have been deprecated in this specification. Claim generators shall not use these constructs. Validators should still accept them for backwards compatibility as described in Appendix E, Considerations for Deprecation.

sections.title: H.1. dataSource Field in Assertion Metadata

summary.text: The dataSource field in assertion metadata is deprecated: claim generators shall not include it, while validators shall still accept it, because no known implementations used it. The block describes its former structure, a type drawn from a table of values such as signer, claimGenerator.REE, localProvider.TEE, remoteProvider, remoteProvider.external and humanEntry (or an entity-specific namespace), and a human-readable details string.

sections.extract: IMPORTANT: The dataSource field in assertion metadata is deprecated. Claim generators shall not include a dataSource field in assertion metadata. Validators shall continue to accept the field for backwards compatibility. A previous version of this specification defined a dataSource field in the assertion metadata structure to convey the origin of assertion data. No known implementations used this field, and the

sections.title: H.2. String Label x5chain

summary.text: The string label x5chain for the X.509 certificate chain COSE header is deprecated, so claim generators shall use integer label 33, now standardised by RFC 9360, while validators shall still accept the string label.

sections.extract: IMPORTANT: Use of the string label x5chain for the X.509 certificate chain COSE header is deprecated. Claim generators shall use the integer label 33 instead, as described in Section 13.5, “X.509 Certificates”. A previous version of this specification required claim generators to write the string label x5chain for the certificate chain header parameter, to avoid a dependency on the integer label 33 being

sections.title: H.3. Data Boxes

summary.text: The note says data boxes are deprecated and kept only for historical reference, replaced by a standard assertion that holds data in a JUMBF Embedded File content type box.

sections.extract: IMPORTANT: This section is retained for historical purposes. The concept of a data box has been deprecated in favour of a standard assertion that uses a standard JUMBF Embedded File content type box to contain the data. For more information, see Section 16.6.6, “Embedded Data”.

sections.title: H.3.1. General

summary.text: Data boxes let arbitrary data referenced from an assertion be placed in the Data Box Store as single CBOR content type boxes, with the binary data in the data field, its type identified by an IANA media type in dc:format (structured suffixes such as +json are allowed), and optional asset types in data_types. A data box shall have the label c2pa.data and follows the usual assertion label rules for multiple instances.

sections.extract: Data boxes provide a way to include arbitrary data into the C2PA Manifest that is referenced from an assertion, instead of embedding it directly into a field of the assertion as a binary string. These data boxes are placed in the Data Box Store and each one will be a single CBOR Content Type box (cbor). The data of a data box is provided directly as the value of the data field, which is a bstr, so any binary data

sections.title: H.3.2. Schema and Example

summary.text: The CDDL defines data-box-map, which holds an IANA media type in dc:format, arbitrary data as a byte string and optional data_types.

sections.extract: The schema for this type is defined by the data-box-map rule in the CDDL Definition in CDDL for data box.: CDDL for data box ; box allowing for the storage of arbitrary data data-box-map = { "dc:format": format-string, ; IANA media type of the data "data" : bstr, ; arbitrary text/binary data ; additional information about the data's type ? "data_types": [1* asset-type-map], }

sections.title: H.4. Data Box Store

summary.text: The deprecated, historical Data Box Store is a JUMBF superbox that shall contain only CBOR content type boxes labelled c2pa.data, and shall itself have the label c2pa.databoxes and the c2db type UUID, and the block also includes a figure of a manifest store with data boxes.

sections.extract: IMPORTANT: This section is retained for historical purposes. The concept of a data box has been deprecated in favor of a standard assertion that uses a standard JUMBF Embedded File content type box to contain the data. For more information about the embedded data assertion, see Section 16.6.6, “Embedded Data”. A C2PA Data Box Store is a JUMBF superbox that shall contain only one or more CBOR Content Type boxes

sections.title: H.5. Action c2pa.removed

summary.text: The c2pa.removed action, formerly used for removed componentOf ingredients, is deprecated in favour of the ingredient field of c2pa.deleted, so claim generators shall not use it, though validators should still accept it.

sections.extract: A previous version of this specification allowed claim generators to write the action c2pa.removed for componentOf ingredients that have been removed. This action has since been deprecated in favour of using the ingredient field of the c2pa.deleted action. Claim generators shall not use the c2pa.removed action. Validators should continue to accept the c2pa.removed action for backwards compatibility. <a

sections.title: H.5.1. Validation rule

summary.text: The validation rule requires that the ingredients (or, for c2pa.actions, ingredient) field hold one or more valid hashed URIs, each resolving to an ingredient assertion in another manifest whose relationship is componentOf, and otherwise the claim shall be rejected with assertion.action.ingredientMismatch.

sections.extract: Check that the ingredients field (or ingredient field for c2pa.actions) contains one or more valid hashed URIs, each of which can be resolved to an ingredient assertion in another manifest whose relationship field is componentOf. If not, then the claim shall be rejected with a failure code of assertion.action.ingredientMismatch.
